# Sign Up

> Create your IBEE Solutions account — register with your email, verify it, set a password, and log in to the portal.

Create your IBEE Solutions account in four steps: register your email, verify it, set a password, and log in. The process takes under five minutes.

## Before you begin

* A valid email address you can access within 24 hours

> **Info**
>
> If you already have an account, click **Log in** at the bottom of the signup form.

### 1. Register your email

Go to [portal.ibee.ai/signup](https://portal.ibee.ai/signup).

1. Enter your **Email** address.
2. Check **I agree to the Terms of Use**. The form also links to the Privacy Policy, which explains how IBEE uses your information.
3. Click **Sign up**.

The portal confirms that a verification link was sent to your email address.

### 2. Check your inbox

> **Warning**
>
> The verification link expires in **24 hours**. If you open an expired link, the portal shows a **Resend Verification Email** option, or a **Back to Sign Up** button if a new link can't be sent for that address.

Open the email from `noreply@ibee.ai` with the subject **Verify your email address**.

### 3. Verify your email and set a password

Click **Verify Email** in the email. The **Set Your Password** page opens with your account email already filled in.

1. Enter a **Password** that meets every rule below.
2. Re-enter the same value in **Confirm Password**.
3. Click **Set Password**.

| Password rule     | Requirement                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Length            | 12–20 characters                                           |
| Uppercase         | At least one uppercase letter                              |
| Lowercase         | At least one lowercase letter                              |
| Number            | At least one number                                        |
| Special character | At least one special character (for example `!`, `@`, `#`) |

The form checks each rule as you type. After the password is saved, the portal returns you to the login page.

### 4. Log in

Go to [portal.ibee.ai](https://portal.ibee.ai).

1. Enter your **Email** and **Password**.
2. Complete the **Cloudflare** security check if it appears.
3. Click **Log in**.

If you have turned on [two-factor authentication](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/account-security#two-factor-authentication), the portal then asks for the 6-digit **2FA Code** from your authenticator app. Click **Verify & Log in**.

After your first login, you land on the **Organizations** page. It shows any pending invitations to join other organizations and a **Create New Organization** button. See [Create an organization](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/create-an-organization).

## Troubleshooting

**Verification email not received**
Check your spam folder. The sender is `noreply@ibee.ai`. If the email does not arrive after a few minutes, return to `portal.ibee.ai/signup` and sign up again with the same address.

**Verification link expired**
Open the expired link. Enter your email address under **Resend Verification Email** to get a new link. If that option isn't shown, click **Back to Sign Up** and register again with the same address.

**Password rejected**
Check every password rule in the table above. Passwords longer than 20 characters are not accepted, so a long passphrase pasted from a password manager can be rejected.

**Forgot your password**
Click **Forgot password?** on the login page. See [Account security](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/account-security#reset-a-forgotten-password).

**Security check not loading on login**
Disable browser extensions that block Cloudflare scripts and reload the page.

title: Create an Organization
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/getting-started/account-setup/create-an-organization
description: Create an IBEE Solutions organization to manage resources, billing, and team members. Learn about country restrictions, geo-detection, currency assignment, tax invoices, and GST verification for Indian businesses.

# Create an Organization

> Create an IBEE Solutions organization to manage resources, billing, and team members. Learn about country restrictions, geo-detection, currency assignment, tax invoices, and GST verification for Indian businesses.

An organization is a billing and resource boundary in IBEE Solutions. Each organization has its own wallet, team members, and workspaces. You can create multiple organizations under a single login — up to **3 owned organizations** by default. See [Organization limits](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas#organization-limits).

## Before you begin

* A signed-in IBEE Solutions account ([Sign up](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/sign-up) if you haven't already)
* Your billing address (street, city, postal code, and country)

> **Info**
>
> IBEE Solutions is available in [26 serving countries](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/restricted-countries#serving-countries). Services are not offered in [46 restricted countries](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/restricted-countries) due to U.S. export-control regulations.

## Country detection

When you open the organization creation form, the portal detects your country automatically using Cloudflare geo-detection. Three outcomes are possible:

| Detection result       | What happens                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Serving country**    | Your country is pre-filled in the form. Currency and tax type are set automatically.                                                                                     |
| **Restricted country** | A red banner appears: *"Services not available in \{country}."* You can still select a different country if your registered business is in a supported region.           |
| **Other country**      | An amber banner appears: *"We don't currently serve \{country}."* Pick a supported country where you have a registered entity, or [contact sales](mailto:sales@ibee.ai). |

## Currency and tax assignment

Currency and tax type are set automatically based on your selected country:

| Country                     | Currency           | Tax type  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------ | --------- |
| India                       | INR (Indian Rupee) | GST       |
| United States               | USD (US Dollar)    | Sales Tax |
| All other serving countries | USD (US Dollar)    | VAT       |

Currency is locked to your country and cannot be changed in the form. If you need a different currency, click **Request a change** below the currency field to submit a currency change request with supporting documents.

### 1. Go to organization setup

**First-time users:** After your first login you land on the **Organizations** page. Click **Create New Organization**.

**Existing users:** Do one of the following:

* On the **Organizations** page, click **Create Organization** in the top right.
* Open the organization switcher in the top bar and click **New Organization**.

If you already own the maximum number of organizations, the **Create Organization** button is hidden and the portal takes you to the [limit increase request](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas#request-more-organizations) instead.

### 2. Fill in Organization Details

| Field             | Required         | Notes                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Organization Name | Yes              | A nickname for your reference — shown in your organization list        |
| Organization Type | Yes              | **Business** (default) or **Individual**                               |
| Business Name     | Yes (Business)   | Legal entity name, used on invoices. Auto-filled from GST if verified. |
| Full Name         | Yes (Individual) | Your full name as on government ID, used on invoices                   |

### 3. Fill in Billing Address

| Field           | Required |
| --------------- | -------- |
| Street Address  | Yes      |
| Apartment/Suite | No       |
| City            | Yes      |
| State/Region    | No       |
| Postal Code     | Yes      |
| Country         | Yes      |

The **Country** dropdown only lists the 26 serving countries. Selecting a country automatically sets the currency and tax type.

### 4. Tax Information and Create

Check **I want a tax invoice** if you require GST, VAT, or sales tax invoices for this organization. A tax ID field appears for your country, and you must verify it before **Create Organization** is enabled.

#### GST verification (India)

For organizations in India, the field is **GST Identification Number (GSTIN)**:

1. Enter your 15-character GSTIN (auto-uppercased).
2. Click **Verify GST**.
3. The portal verifies the GSTIN against government records and shows a confirmation dialog with:
   * Company name, GSTIN, status, registration date, business type, and taxpayer type
   * Registered address from GST records
4. Click **Apply Details and Create Organization** to auto-fill the business name and address from GST records and create the organization in one step.

#### Tax ID validation (other countries)

For other serving countries, enter your tax ID and click **Validate** (the button shows the ID type, for example **Validate EIN**). The portal checks the format for your country:

| Country                 | Tax ID field                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| United States           | Employer Identification Number (EIN) |
| Australia               | Australian Business Number (ABN)     |
| Canada                  | Business Number (BN)                 |
| Singapore               | Unique Entity Number (UEN)           |
| United Kingdom          | VAT Registration Number              |
| United Arab Emirates    | Tax Registration Number (TRN)        |
| Other serving countries | VAT or tax identification number     |

Click **Change** to edit a validated ID.

When all required fields are complete, click **Create Organization**.

## After creation

The portal opens the new organization's **Workspaces** page. Every new organization starts with three workspaces — **production**, **dev**, and **stage** — which count toward the limit of 5 workspaces per organization. See [Dashboard & navigation](/docs/getting-started/overview/dashboard#workspaces-page).

If you haven't verified your identity yet, a banner prompts you to complete KYC. Click **Complete KYC** to [verify your identity](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/verify-your-identity). Full access to deploy servers and use all cloud services requires completed identity verification.

To change the organization's name, address, or tax details later, see [Organization settings](/docs/platform-fundamentals/organization-settings).

## Troubleshooting

**Create button is disabled**
Ensure all required fields are filled. If you checked **I want a tax invoice**, verify your GSTIN (India) or validate your tax ID (other countries) first.

**Create Organization button is missing**
You own the maximum number of organizations. [Request more organizations](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas#request-more-organizations).

**Country not in the dropdown**
Only the 26 serving countries appear in the dropdown. See the [restricted countries](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/restricted-countries) page for the full list.

**Red banner: "Services not available"**
You are in a restricted country. If you have a registered business in a supported country, select that country manually. Otherwise, [contact sales](mailto:sales@ibee.ai).

**Currency shows wrong value**
Currency is determined by your country: India uses INR, all others use USD. To request a different currency, click the **Request a change** link below the currency field.

**GST verification failed**
Ensure you are entering a valid, active 15-character GSTIN. Inactive or cancelled GSTINs are rejected.

## Related pages

* [Restricted countries](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/restricted-countries)
* [Verify your identity](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/verify-your-identity)
* [Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing)
* [Organization settings](/docs/platform-fundamentals/organization-settings)
* [Organizations and tenancy model](/docs/platform-fundamentals/organizations-and-tenancy-model)

# Restricted Countries

> IBEE Solutions does not offer services in certain countries due to U.S. export-control and trade-sanction regulations. Review the full list of restricted countries and the 26 countries where IBEE Solutions operates.

IBEE Solutions complies with U.S. Department of Commerce and Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) trade and export-control regulations. As a result, services are **not available** in certain countries and territories.

When you create an organization, the portal detects your location automatically. If you are in a restricted country, a banner explains that services are unavailable in your region.

> **Warning**
>
> **Important Notice**
>
> Users located in restricted countries cannot create an IBEE Solutions organization or deploy resources. If your registered business is in a supported country, you can select that country manually during organization setup. For questions, contact [sales@ibee.ai](mailto:sales@ibee.ai).

## Restricted countries

The following 46 countries and territories are restricted under U.S. export-control and OFAC sanctions regulations:

| #  | Country                          |
| -- | -------------------------------- |
| 1  | Afghanistan                      |
| 2  | Armenia                          |
| 3  | Azerbaijan                       |
| 4  | Bahrain                          |
| 5  | Belarus                          |
| 6  | Cambodia                         |
| 7  | Central African Republic         |
| 8  | China                            |
| 9  | Cuba                             |
| 10 | Democratic Republic of the Congo |
| 11 | Egypt                            |
| 12 | Eritrea                          |
| 13 | Georgia                          |
| 14 | Haiti                            |
| 15 | Hong Kong                        |
| 16 | Iran                             |
| 17 | Iraq                             |
| 18 | Jordan                           |
| 19 | Kazakhstan                       |
| 20 | Kuwait                           |
| 21 | Kyrgyzstan                       |
| 22 | Laos                             |
| 23 | Lebanon                          |
| 24 | Libya                            |
| 25 | Macau                            |
| 26 | Moldova                          |
| 27 | Mongolia                         |

| 29 | Nicaragua                        |
| 30 | North Korea                      |
| 31 | Oman                             |

| 33 | Qatar                            |
| 34 | Russia                           |
| 35 | Saudi Arabia                     |
| 36 | Somalia                          |
| 37 | South Sudan                      |
| 38 | Sudan                            |

| 40 | Tajikistan                       |
| 41 | Turkmenistan                     |
| 42 | Uzbekistan                       |
| 43 | Venezuela                        |
| 44 | Vietnam                          |
| 45 | Yemen                            |
| 46 | Zimbabwe                         |

## Why are these countries restricted?

IBEE Solutions is subject to U.S. trade and export-control laws, including regulations administered by the U.S. Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and the U.S. Department of the Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). These laws restrict the provision of cloud computing and infrastructure services to individuals and entities in sanctioned or embargoed countries and territories.

## Serving countries

IBEE Solutions currently operates in the following 26 countries:

| Region           | Countries                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Asia-Pacific** | Australia, India, Israel, Malaysia, Singapore                                                                                                         |
| **Europe**       | Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Latvia, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom |
| **Middle East**  | Turkey, United Arab Emirates                                                                                                                          |
| **Americas**     | Canada, Costa Rica, United States                                                                                                                     |

If your country is not listed above and is not restricted, you may still be able to use IBEE Solutions. Select a supported country where you have a registered business entity during organization creation, or [contact sales](mailto:sales@ibee.ai) to discuss availability in your region.

title: Verify Your Identity
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/getting-started/account-setup/verify-your-identity

---

# Verify Your Identity

> Complete identity verification (KYC) to unlock all IBEE Solutions services. Indian users verify with Aadhaar via Digilocker. International users verify with a government-issued ID and selfie.

Identity verification (KYC) is done at the **user level** — once you verify your identity, all your organizations are unlocked. Only identity verification is required; no business or GST verification is needed. The process takes about two to three minutes.

> **Info**
>
> You must complete identity verification to deploy servers, create API tokens, and access all IBEE Solutions services.

## Before you begin

* A signed-in IBEE Solutions account ([Sign up](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/sign-up) if you haven't already)
* **India:** your 12-digit Aadhaar number and a mobile number linked to Aadhaar (for OTP)
* **International:** a government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, or national ID) and a device with a camera for a selfie

## Verification methods

| Method            | Who should use it  | What you need                 | Time        |
| ----------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------- | ----------- |
| **India**         | Residents of India | Aadhaar number + OTP          | \~2 minutes |
| **International** | Everyone else      | Government-issued ID + selfie | \~3 minutes |

IBEE detects your country automatically and marks the suggested method as **Detected**. Select the other method if the detection is wrong.

### 1. Start verification

Navigate to [portal.ibee.ai/verify](https://portal.ibee.ai/verify). Click **Start Verification**.

The **Complete KYC** dialog opens with two options:

| Option            | Label                                  | Method                               |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **India**         | Verify with your **Aadhaar**           | Aadhaar via Digilocker (\~2 minutes) |
| **International** | Verify with **government ID + selfie** | ID scan + selfie (\~3 minutes)       |

Select the option that matches your country of residence.

### 2a. Verify with Aadhaar (India)

1. Click **Verify with Aadhaar**.
2. Complete Aadhaar verification through **Digilocker** — authorize document sharing and enter the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile number.
3. On success, the portal shows **Verification complete** and takes you back to the page you started from, or to your organization.

### 2b. Verify with Government ID (International)

1. Click **Verify with ID**.
2. Review the privacy notice and click **Agree and continue**.
3. Continue on your current device, or scan the QR code to use your phone's camera.
4. Scan the front of your driver's license, passport, or government-issued photo ID.
5. Take a selfie when prompted to confirm the ID belongs to you.
6. On success, the portal shows **Verification complete** and takes you back to the page you started from, or to your organization.

Once verified, your account has full access to all IBEE Solutions services across all your organizations, including VM deployment, GPU VMs, block storage, and API token creation.

## Troubleshooting

**Verification prompt not appearing**
Navigate directly to `portal.ibee.ai/verify`. If you are already verified, you are redirected to your organizations.

**Wrong country detected**
The verification modal suggests a method based on your location. If the **Detected** badge is on the wrong option, select the other one.

**DigiLocker not loading**
Ensure your browser allows redirects and pop-ups for `portal.ibee.ai`. Try a different browser if the issue persists.

**Aadhaar number rejected**
Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar number without spaces.

**No document detected during ID scan (International)**
Position your government-issued photo ID flat and in good lighting. Choose **Retake photo** to try again.

**Verification submitted but status not updated**
The portal polls for up to 60 seconds after submission. If your status does not update, refresh the page — verification may take a moment to propagate.

title: Account Security
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/getting-started/account-setup/account-security
description: Protect your IBEE Solutions login — turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, change your password, review your login history, and reset a forgotten password.
---

# Account Security

> Protect your IBEE Solutions login — turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, change your password, review your login history, and reset a forgotten password.

Your login is personal: it is the same across every organization you own or belong to. Two-factor authentication (2FA), your password, and your login history are managed from your user profile, not from an organization's settings.

## Open your security settings

1. Click your **avatar** in the top-right corner of the portal.
2. Click **View Profile**.

The **User Settings** page opens. The **Security** section contains **Two-Factor Authentication**, **Password**, and **Login History**.

## Edit your profile

The **Basic Information** section on **User Settings** shows your **Full Name**, **Display Name**, **Email**, and **Phone**. Click **Edit**, change the fields, and click **Save**. **Full Name** and **Phone** (with country code) are required. Your email address cannot be changed here.

## Two-factor authentication

With 2FA turned on, every login needs your password **and** a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone. 2FA is off until you turn it on.

### Turn on 2FA

### Install an authenticator app

Install an authenticator app on your phone — for example Google Authenticator, Authy, or Microsoft Authenticator.

### Start setup

In **Security → Two-Factor Authentication**, click **Enable Two-Factor Authentication**.

### Confirm your password

Enter your current password under **Enter Your Password to Continue** and click **Continue**.

### Scan the QR code

Open your authenticator app and scan the QR code. If you can't scan it, copy the setup key shown under **Can't scan? Enter this key manually** into the app.

> **Warning**
>
> Save the QR code or setup key somewhere secure. You need it to set up the authenticator again if you lose access to your app.

### Enter a code

Type the current 6-digit code from the app into **Enter the 6-digit Code from Your App** and click **Enable 2FA**. The code changes every 30 seconds.

The status badge changes to **Enabled**.

### Log in with 2FA

After you enter your email and password on the login page, the portal shows **Two-Factor Authentication** and asks for your **2FA Code**. Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app and click **Verify & Log in**.

### Turn off 2FA

1. In **Security → Two-Factor Authentication**, click **Disable 2FA**.
2. Enter your current password.
3. Confirm with **Disable 2FA**.

After 2FA is off, you only need your password to log in.

## Change your password

1. In **Security → Password**, click **Change Password**.
2. Enter your **Current Password**.
3. Enter a **New Password**. It must meet the same rules as when you signed up: 12–20 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.
4. Click **Update Password**.

## Login history

**Security → Login History** lists your recent login attempts:

| Column          | Description                          |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **Date & Time** | When the login was attempted         |
| **IP Address**  | The IP address the attempt came from |
| **Status**      | **Successful** or **Failed**         |

If you see a login you don't recognize, change your password right away and turn on 2FA.

## Reset a forgotten password

### Request a reset link

On the login page, click **Forgot password?**. Enter your **Email** and click **Send Reset Link**.

If an account exists for that address, a password reset link is sent to it.

### Set a new password

Open the link from the email. On **Set Your Password**, enter a new **Password**, confirm it in **Confirm Password**, and click **Set Password**. The password rules are the same as at [sign-up](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/sign-up).

### Log in

The portal returns you to the login page. Log in with your new password.

If the reset link has expired, the page shows **Request a new reset link**. Click it to start again.

title: Add Billing
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing
description: Set up billing for your IBEE Solutions organization — purchase prepaid credits (online payment in India, card in other countries), redeem promo codes, save a card, upload TDS certificates, and apply for Invoice Billing.
---

# Add Billing

> Set up billing for your IBEE Solutions organization — purchase prepaid credits (online payment in India, card in other countries), redeem promo codes, save a card, upload TDS certificates, and apply for Invoice Billing.

New IBEE Solutions organizations are billed from a **prepaid wallet**: you add credits, and usage is deducted as resources run. The platform checks your billing state before every resource creation. If your balance does not cover the resource, a **Billing needs attention** popup asks you to add credits.

How you pay depends on your organization's currency:

* **India (INR):** Online payment (UPI, cards, or net banking).
* **International (USD):** Credit or debit card. You can save cards on the organization for future purchases.

Organizations that qualify can later switch to monthly **Invoice Billing** instead of prepaid credits: usage is billed in arrears within an approved credit limit. See [Apply for Invoice Billing](#apply-for-invoice-billing).

## Before you begin

* An IBEE Solutions organization ([Create an organization](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/create-an-organization))
* A verified identity ([Verify your identity](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/verify-your-identity))
* The **Admin** or **Billing** role in the organization

## Purchase credits

### Open Payment Method

In the portal sidebar, click **Payment Method** under **Billing**.

You can also click **Add Credits** in any **Billing needs attention** popup — it opens this page with the purchase dialog already open.

### Start a purchase

In **Credits & Spend Management**, click **Purchase credits** on the **Purchased credits** card.

### Choose how to pay (India only)

Indian organizations choose **Online payment** (UPI, cards, or net banking; credited instantly) and click **Continue**.

### Choose an amount

Pick a preset amount or enter your own. The dialog checks the amount against the minimum and maximum for one purchase in your currency.

### Pay

Click **Continue** (India) or **Continue to payment** (international), then complete the payment. International organizations can pick a saved card or **New card**, then click **Pay**.

When the payment succeeds, the portal confirms it; your wallet updates shortly after.

> **Info**
>
> Indian organizations must make a first purchase before creating their first resource. The **Billing needs attention** popup shows the minimum amount.

## Redeem a promo code

1. On **Payment Method**, click **Redeem promo code** on the **Promo balance** card.
2. Enter the code and click **Apply**.

Promo credits are used before purchased credits, may be applied automatically to open invoices, and unused promo credits may expire.

## Save a card (international)

Organizations outside India can save cards in the **Payment Methods** section of the **Payment Method** page:

1. Click **Add Card**. In **Add Payment Card**, select the consent checkbox and click **Save Card**, then enter your card details. A temporary card validation charge is made and refunded automatically once the card is verified.
2. Click **Set Default** on a card to use it by default.
3. To delete a card, click its **Remove Card** (trash) icon, then **Remove**.

Saved cards belong to the organization.

## Wallet balance

The **Payment Method** page shows two balances in **Credits & Spend Management**:

| Card                  | What it holds                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Promo balance**     | Promotional credits (used first)                                                                  |
| **Purchased credits** | Credits you bought. Shows **Amount due** instead of **Available** when the balance is below zero. |

Expand **Recent wallet activity** to see the latest credits and debits (**When**, **Activity**, **Reference**, **Amount**). Click **View all** for the full list: credits are positive, and invoice and usage debits are negative.

> **Warning**
>
> If your wallet balance does not cover a new resource, the platform blocks the creation. Existing resources continue running, but you must add credits before deploying anything new.

## Upload a TDS certificate (India)

Indian organizations that deduct TDS can submit Form 16A in the **TDS certificates** section of **Payment Method**:

1. Click **Upload Form 16A**.
2. Choose the **Financial year** and **Quarter**, and select the **Form 16A PDF** (PDF up to 10 MB).
3. Click **Submit**.

Each certificate is listed with its period, submission date, and status: **Pending review**, **Approved** (with the amount credited to your wallet), or **Rejected** (with the reason).

## Apply for Invoice Billing

1. On **Payment Method**, find the **Invoice Billing** section and click **Enable**.
2. In **Request postpaid billing**, optionally attach **Supporting documents** — for example business registration, PAN, GST registration, or a signed postpaid agreement (PDF only, up to 5 files, 10 MB each).
3. Click **Request postpaid**.

The billing team reviews the request; Invoice Billing starts only after approval. While it is under review, click **View request** to see what you sent. If it is rejected, the section shows the date you can apply again; from then, click **Request again**. After approval, the section shows your credit usage — see [Invoice Billing](/docs/platform-fundamentals/billing-and-usage#invoice-billing).

## Billing admission checks

Before creating a billable resource, the platform checks your organization's billing state and balance. If the check fails, the portal explains why and, when adding credits would resolve it, offers **Add Credits**. See [Billing admission checks](/docs/platform-fundamentals/billing-and-usage#billing-admission-checks).

## Next steps

* Track spending on **Billing → Summary** and **Billing → Usage**, and download invoices from **Billing → Invoices**. See [Billing and usage](/docs/platform-fundamentals/billing-and-usage).
* Review your plan's resource limits in [Limits & Quotas](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas).

# Dashboard & Navigation

> Navigate the IBEE Solutions portal — select an organization, browse workspaces, switch between them, and access resources, billing, and settings from the sidebar.

The IBEE Solutions portal is organized around **organizations** and **workspaces**. Sign in, pick an organization, then pick a workspace to access resources. Billing, team management, and settings live at the organization level; compute, storage, and networking live inside workspaces.

## Organizations page

After sign-in, the portal shows the **Organizations** page. Each organization card displays:

* The **organization name**
* An account-type tag (e.g. **Individual** or **Business**)
* The billing **currency** (e.g. **INR**)

Click a card to open the organization. To create a new one, click **Create Organization** in the top right. See [Create an organization](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/create-an-organization).

The page also shows:

* **Pending invitations** from other organizations, with **Accept** and **Decline** buttons. See [Accepting an invitation](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles#accepting-an-invitation).
* Your organization usage, for example *"1 of 3 owned organizations used. Joined 2 of 20 organizations."* See [Organization limits](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas#organization-limits).

If you don't belong to any organization yet, the page shows **No organizations yet** and a **Create New Organization** button.

## Workspaces page

Inside an organization, the **Workspaces** page lists all workspaces and shows how many are in use (for example *"3 of 5 workspaces used"*). Every new organization starts with three workspaces: **production**, **dev**, and **stage**. Each card shows:

* The **workspace name** (click the pencil icon to rename)
* A **type** tag: Production, Dev, Stage, or Custom

Click a workspace card to enter it. The portal opens the first resource page (Bare Metal Servers) directly.

Only organization **Admins** can create or rename workspaces. Workspaces can't be deleted from the portal.

### Create a workspace

Click **Create Workspace** in the top right. In the dialog, set:

* **Type** (required) — Production (default), Dev, or Stage
* **Name** (optional) — defaults to the type name (e.g. "production")

Click **Create workspace** to confirm. The portal navigates straight to the new workspace's resource page.

> **Info**
>
> Each organization supports up to **5 workspaces**, including the three default ones. For a higher limit, contact [support@ibee.ai](mailto:support@ibee.ai).

## The sidebar

The sidebar changes depending on whether the current view is at the **organization level** or inside a **workspace**. There is no separate dashboard page — after you choose an organization, you land on its Workspaces page.

### Organization-level sidebar

Visible on the Workspaces page and organization settings:

* **Organization** — Workspaces, Organization Details, Team, API Tokens, Activity Logs
* **Billing** — Summary, Usage, Invoices, Payment Method, Usage Limits

### Workspace-level sidebar

Visible inside a workspace:

* **Infrastructure** — Bare Metal Servers, GPU VMs, Cloud VMs, Object Storage, Block Storage, Container Registry
* **Network & Security** — VPC, Reserved IPs, Load Balancer, DNS, CDN, Firewalls, SSL Certificates
* **Tools** — Backups, Snapshots, ISOs, SSH Keys, Email Service, Secret Manager
* **Workspace** — Workspace Details (returns to the Workspaces list)

Organization-level pages (Team, API Tokens, Activity Logs, and billing) are not in the workspace sidebar. Use **Workspace Details** or the organization switcher to return to the organization level.

Some products are enabled for organizations in stages, so your sidebar may not show every item listed here. Your access role also hides pages you can't use — for example, Billing members see only the **Billing** section. See [Team members & access roles](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles).

## Switching organizations and workspaces

The top bar shows a **breadcrumb-style switcher**: `Organization ▾ / Workspace ▾`. Click either chevron to open a two-column panel:

* **Left column (Organizations)** — search and select any organization. Includes **All Organizations** and **New Organization** links.
* **Right column (Workspaces)** — search and select a workspace within the current organization. Includes **All Workspaces** and **New Workspace** links.

Selecting an organization opens its Workspaces page. Selecting a workspace opens its resources.

## Billing at a glance

To check spending, open **Billing → Summary** for this month's usage charges, or **Billing → Payment Method** for your wallet balances and to purchase credits. See [Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing).

## Top bar

Every page includes a persistent top bar with:

* The **organization / workspace switcher** (breadcrumb dropdown)
* **Support** — opens the Support Center for the current organization. See [Contact Support](/docs/support/contact-support).
* **Help** (question-mark icon) — the **Need help?** menu with **Feedback**, **Documentation**, **Changelog**, and **Status** links
* **Notifications** (bell icon)
* **Account menu** (avatar) in the top right — **View Profile** opens your user settings, including [account security](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/account-security); **Logout** signs you out

The Support link appears only for roles that can open support requests (Admin and Technical).

## Navigation flow summary

```
Sign in
  → Organizations page (select an organization)
    → Workspaces page (select a workspace)
      → Resource pages (Bare Metal, GPU VMs, Cloud VMs, Storage, etc.)
```

Organization-level pages (Billing, Team, API Tokens, Activity Logs) are accessible from the organization sidebar without entering a workspace.

# Regions & Locations

> Where IBEE Solutions runs — data center locations, region codes, and availability for compute, storage, and networking resources.

IBEE Solutions resources are deployed into **regions** — isolated data center locations identified by a short region code. Use the region code when creating any resource on the platform.

## Asia

| Location         | Region code |
| ---------------- | ----------- |
| Amaravati, India | VGA         |
| Hyderabad, India | HYD         |

## Americas

| Location     | Region code |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| Ashburn, USA | IAD         |

## Choosing a region

Pick the region closest to your end users or workload:

* **India-based users or workloads** — use `VGA` (Amaravati). Use `HYD` for active-active or DR pairing once available.
* **US-based users or workloads** — use `IAD` (Ashburn, Virginia).
* **Global services** — combine regions by deploying resources in more than one location.

# First resource

> Launch your first IBEE Solutions resource — a Cloud VM — in under 5 minutes.

The fastest way to get started with IBEE Solutions is to deploy a Cloud VM. This page walks you through the minimum steps from a fresh organization to a running server.

## Before you begin

1. **Sign up** — [Create an IBEE Solutions account](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/sign-up).
2. **Verify** — Complete [account verification](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/verify-your-identity) to unlock compute access.
3. **Create an organization** — [Set up an organization](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/create-an-organization) to group your resources and billing.
4. **Add credits** — Go to **Billing → Payment Method** in the sidebar and click **Purchase credits**. The platform checks your wallet balance before deploying. See [Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing).

## Launch a Cloud VM

### Open Cloud VMs

In the portal sidebar, click **Cloud VMs** under **Products**, then click **Create server**.

### Pick a region, plan, and OS

1. Select **Asia → Amaravati (AVR)** as the region.
2. Choose a plan — `perf.1.c2.m4` is a good starting point.
3. Under **Operating System → Templates**, pick **Ubuntu → Ubuntu 24.04**.

### Add an SSH key and deploy

1. Under **SSH Keys**, paste your public key (or click **+ New** to add one).
2. Enter a hostname (e.g. `my-first-vm`).
3. Click **Deploy Now**.

### Connect

Once the VM shows **Running**, copy the public IP and SSH in:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@<public-ip>
```

## What to explore next

* **Block Storage** — [Create a volume](/docs/infrastructure/block-storage/create-a-volume) and attach persistent storage to your VM.
* **Object Storage** — [Upload your first object](/docs/infrastructure/object-storage/getting-started) to an S3-compatible bucket.
* **Firewalls** — [Create firewall rules](/docs/network-security/firewalls/create-firewall-rules) to control inbound traffic.
* **Backups** — [Enable backups](/docs/tools/backups/enable-backups) for automated recovery points.

## Related pages

# Bare Metal Servers

> Dedicated physical servers on IBEE Solutions with full hardware access — browse the Dell hardware catalog in the portal and talk to sales to order.

Bare Metal Servers are dedicated physical machines — no hypervisor, no neighbors. You get full hardware access and predictable performance for databases, latency-sensitive workloads, licensing scenarios that require physical cores, and anything that shouldn't share a host.

Ordering is **sales-assisted**: the portal shows the hardware catalog, and the IBEE sales team configures, prices, and provisions the server with you. There's no self-service deploy button for bare metal.

## Hardware catalog

In the portal sidebar, open **Infrastructure → Bare Metal Servers**. The page lists the available Dell configurations:

| Model     | RAM                   | Storage                        | RAID             |
| --------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------- |
| Dell R220 | Up to 32 GB DDR3 ECC  | Up to 4 TB SSD/HDD             | RAID 1           |
| Dell R230 | Up to 64 GB DDR4 ECC  | Up to 16 TB SSD/HDD            | RAID 1, 5, 10    |
| Dell R240 | Up to 64 GB DDR4 ECC  | Up to 32 TB SSD/HDD            | RAID 1, 5, 10    |
| Dell R430 | Up to 384 GB DDR4 ECC | Up to 18 TB SSD / 40 TB HDD    | RAID 1, 5, 10    |
| Dell R630 | Up to 1.5 TB DDR4 ECC | Up to 23 TB SSD / 18 TB HDD    | RAID 1, 5, 10    |
| Dell R640 | Up to 3 TB DDR4 ECC   | Up to 76.8 TB NVMe / 64 TB HDD | RAID 1, 5, 10    |
| Dell R730 | Up to 3 TB DDR4 ECC   | Up to 64 TB HDD / 29 TB SSD    | RAID 1, 5, 6, 10 |

To order one of these — or a configuration outside these ranges — click **talk to sales** on the Bare Metal Servers page. See [Provision a server](/docs/infrastructure/bare-metal/provision-a-server).

## Locations

| Region | Location               | Code | Status      |
| ------ | ---------------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| Asia   | Amaravati, India       | VGA1 | Available   |
| Asia   | Hyderabad, India       | HYD2 | Available   |
| Europe | Amsterdam, Netherlands | AMS1 | Coming soon |

## Pricing

Pricing is monthly in INR, plus 18% GST. The portal doesn't show bare metal prices — ask the sales team for a quote for your configuration, including the operating system (some, such as Windows, carry a licence fee) and network port.

title: Provision a server

description: Order a bare metal server on IBEE Solutions — review the hardware catalog in the portal, then talk to sales to configure, price, and provision it.

# Provision a server

> Order a bare metal server on IBEE Solutions — review the hardware catalog in the portal, then talk to sales to configure, price, and provision it.

Bare metal provisioning is sales-assisted. The portal shows the hardware catalog; you then contact the IBEE sales team, who confirm the configuration, pricing, and provisioning with you. There's no self-service configurator or deploy button for bare metal in the portal.

## Before you begin

* A verified IBEE Solutions organization with billing set up ([Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing)).
* An idea of your requirements — see the checklist below.

## Request a server

### 1. Review the hardware catalog

In the portal sidebar, open **Infrastructure → Bare Metal Servers**. The table lists each Dell model with its maximum **RAM**, **Storage**, and supported **RAID** levels. See [Bare Metal Servers](/docs/infrastructure/bare-metal#hardware-catalog) for the full list.

### 2. Talk to sales

Click **talk to sales** in the banner above the table (**Customization available, click here to talk to sales**). The IBEE contact page opens in a new browser tab.

### 3. Send your requirements

Tell the sales team what you need. Include:

| Item                 | Examples                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Location**         | Amaravati (VGA1) or Hyderabad (HYD2), India. Amsterdam (AMS1), under the Europe region, is coming soon. |
| **Hardware**         | A catalog model, or custom CPU, RAM, storage, and RAID requirements.                                    |
| **Operating system** | The OS and version you want installed. Some, such as Windows, carry a licence fee.                      |
| **Network**          | Port speed and bandwidth needs.                                                                         |
| **Hostname**         | For example `my-baremetal-01`.                                                                          |

### 4. Confirm and provision

The sales team confirms the configuration and monthly price (INR, plus 18% GST) and arranges provisioning with you.

> **Info**
>
> Bare metal servers are provisioned by the IBEE team rather than instantly. For instant self-service compute, use [Cloud VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/create-a-vm) or [GPU VMs](/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms/create-a-gpu-vm).

## Troubleshooting

**I can't find a Deploy button on the Bare Metal Servers page**
That's expected — ordering goes through sales. Click **talk to sales**.

**The configuration I need isn't in the catalog**
The catalog shows standard ranges. Custom hardware is available on request — click **talk to sales** and describe what you need.

* [Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing)
* [Cloud VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms)

title: GPU VMs
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms
description: GPU-backed virtual machines on IBEE Solutions for AI inference, training, rendering, and other accelerated workloads — deployed and managed like Cloud VMs, with per-GPU metrics.

# GPU VMs

> GPU-backed virtual machines on IBEE Solutions for AI inference, training, rendering, and other accelerated workloads — deployed and managed like Cloud VMs, with per-GPU metrics.

GPU VMs are KVM-based virtual machines with NVIDIA GPUs attached. Use them for model training and fine-tuning, inference APIs, rendering, video processing, and any workload that needs GPU acceleration. You deploy and manage them from the portal much like [Cloud VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms), with a GPU plan catalog and an extra **GPU Metrics** tab.

> **Info**
>
> **Ready to deploy?** Follow [Create a GPU VM](/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms/create-a-gpu-vm).

## What you can do

* Deploy GPU plans that combine a GPU model and GPU memory with vCPU, RAM, and disk — up to 5 identical VMs at once.
* Boot from GPU-compatible OS templates, or from an ISO, snapshot, or backup.
* Sign in with SSH keys (Linux) or a password, shown under **Overview → Connection Details**.
* Connect with a public IP, or place the VM in a VPC with **Private + NAT** or **Private only** networking. Attach Reserved IPs and protect it with a firewall group.
* Watch CPU, memory, disk, and network on the **Monitoring** tab, and GPU utilization, VRAM, temperature, and power on the **GPU Metrics** tab.
* Protect data with scheduled [backups](/docs/tools/backups) and manual [snapshots](/docs/tools/snapshots).
* Change plans and manage IPs, VPCs, SSH keys, and passwords from the **Settings** tab.

## Find GPU VMs in the portal

In the portal sidebar, open **Infrastructure → GPU VMs**. The **GPU Virtual Machines** page lists your GPU VMs with their **Instance**, **OS**, **Location**, **IP Address**, and **Status**. Click **Deploy GPU VM** to create one, or click a row to open its detail page.

## How GPU VMs differ from Cloud VMs

|                 | GPU VMs                                                                        | Cloud VMs                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Plans**       | Each plan lists the GPU model and GPU memory, plus vCPU, RAM, disk, and price. | vCPU, memory, storage, and bandwidth. See [Instance types](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/instance-types). |
| **Billing**     | **Hourly**.                                                                    | **Hourly**, or **Monthly** / **Yearly** commitments where offered.                                         |
| **Templates**   | Only GPU-compatible images are listed.                                         | Only Cloud VM images are listed.                                                                           |
| **Detail tabs** | Overview, Monitoring, **GPU Metrics**, Backups, Snapshots, Settings.           | Overview, Monitoring, Backups, Snapshots, Settings.                                                        |

Everything else — location, SSH keys, network configuration, instance count, hostnames, power actions, and the delete dialog — works the same way as for Cloud VMs.

## Lifecycle of a GPU VM

| Stage       | What you do                                                                            | Where                                                                   |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Deploy**  | Pick location, GPU plan, OS, SSH keys, network, and hostname.                          | [Create a GPU VM](/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms/create-a-gpu-vm)         |
| **Set up**  | Confirm the GPU with `nvidia-smi`; install a compatible NVIDIA driver if it's missing. | [Create a GPU VM](/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms/create-a-gpu-vm#verify)  |
| **Operate** | Start, stop, reboot; watch **Monitoring** and **GPU Metrics**.                         | [Power actions](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/power-actions)           |
| **Connect** | Manage public IP, Reserved IPs, VPCs, and access.                                      | [Networking for VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/networking-for-vms) |
| **Protect** | Enable scheduled backups or take manual snapshots.                                     | [Backups](/docs/tools/backups) · [Snapshots](/docs/tools/snapshots)     |
| **Scale**   | Change plan from **Settings → Change Plan**.                                           | [Resize a VM](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/resize-a-vm)               |
| **Retire**  | Delete the VM, optionally keeping its public IP as a Reserved IP.                      | [Power actions](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/power-actions#delete)    |

## GPU Metrics

The **GPU Metrics** tab charts **GPU Utilization**, **VRAM Utilization**, **Temperature**, and **Power Draw** over **30m**, **1h**, **6h**, **24h**, or **7d**. Collection is off until you turn it on:

1. Start the VM, and make sure `qemu-guest-agent` is running inside it.
2. On **GPU Metrics**, click **Enable monitoring**. A lightweight IBEE agent is installed through the guest agent — it opens no network port on the VM.
3. If the tab shows **NVIDIA guest driver required**, install a compatible NVIDIA driver inside the VM. Monitoring starts automatically once `nvidia-smi` works; CUDA is optional.

If the agent goes offline or setup fails, the tab explains why and offers **Repair monitoring**. Historical values stay visible while the VM is stopped.

> **Info**
>
> Browser console access isn't available in the portal yet — the **Console** action is shown as **Soon**. Use SSH or RDP with the details under **Overview → Connection Details**.

* [Cloud VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms)
* [Networking for VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/networking-for-vms)
* [SSH Keys](/docs/tools/ssh-keys)


---
title: Create a GPU VM in the portal
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms/create-a-gpu-vm
description: Deploy a GPU-enabled virtual machine on IBEE Solutions for AI, ML, rendering, and compute-intensive workloads.
---

# Create a GPU VM in the portal

> Deploy a GPU-enabled virtual machine on IBEE Solutions for AI, ML, rendering, and compute-intensive workloads.

Deploy one or more GPU-enabled virtual machines (VMs) from the IBEE Solutions portal. GPU VMs include NVIDIA GPUs for AI/ML training, inference, rendering, and other GPU-accelerated workloads. The **Deploy** page is a single scrolling form with a running summary and the **Deploy** button in the bottom bar.

## Before you begin

* An IBEE Solutions account with write access to the workspace.
* A verified account to unlock server deployment ([Verify your identity](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/verify-your-identity)).
* Sufficient wallet credits — the platform checks your balance before deploying ([Billing and usage](/docs/platform-fundamentals/billing-and-usage)).

## Deploy a GPU VM

### 1. Open GPU VMs

In the portal sidebar, open **Infrastructure → GPU VMs**, then click **Deploy GPU VM**.

### 2. Select a location

Under **Location**, select a region tab and choose a data center location within it. GPU availability varies by location.

### 3. Choose a GPU plan

Under **Choose Plan**, select a plan. Each row lists the **GPU** model and its **Memory**, plus **vCPU**, **RAM**, **Disk**, and the price per month and per hour. GPU VMs are billed **Hourly**.

### 4. Select the operating system

Pick a source for the boot disk under **Operating System**:

| Tab           | Use it for                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Templates** | OS images maintained by IBEE. The default. Only GPU-compatible images are listed.                                                |
| **ISOs**      | Boot from an ISO you added under **Tools → ISOs**. Interactive installs need a console, which isn't available in the portal yet. |
| **Snapshots** | Create the VM from a snapshot captured from another VM.                                                                          |
| **Backups**   | Create the VM from a scheduled backup recovery point.                                                                            |

On **Templates**, pick an OS family card, then choose a version from the **OS Version** dropdown. For a Windows image, the Windows licence is added automatically and its monthly price per VM appears in the bottom bar.

### 5. Add SSH keys (Linux)

For Linux images, the **SSH Keys** section appears (it's hidden for Windows images). Open **Select SSH Keys** and pick one or more saved keys, or click **Add Key** to create a key pair or import a public key. A Linux VM deployed without a key uses password login, shown under **Overview → Connection Details**. See [SSH Keys](/docs/tools/ssh-keys).

### 6. Configure the network

Under **Network Configuration**, choose **Internet and VPC access**:

* **Public IP** *(default)* — direct inbound and outbound IPv4. Optionally pick a VPC and subnet. Under **Reserved public IP**, keep **Allocate automatically** or pick one of your unattached Reserved IPs, with or without a VPC.
* **Private + NAT** — primary interface in a NAT Gateway VPC with outbound internet only.
* **Private only** — primary interface in a VPC with no internet route.

Under **Firewall**, pick a firewall group or click **Create Group**. If you don't pick one, the default firewall group is attached automatically.

See [Networking for VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/networking-for-vms) for details — the options are the same as for Cloud VMs.

### 7. Set VM details

Under **VM Details**:

* **Instances** — deploy up to **5** VMs at once. The maximum can be lower when GPU capacity or public addresses in the location are limited, and it's **1** when you pick a specific Reserved IP.
* **Hostname** — use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. With more than one instance, this becomes the base hostname and each instance is prefilled as `<base>-1`, `<base>-2`, and so on; edit them under **Instance hostnames**. Every hostname must be unique.

### 8. Deploy

Review the summary in the bottom bar, then click **Deploy** (or **Deploy N VMs**). The platform first checks your organization's billing state and wallet balance. If the check passes, provisioning starts and you return to the GPU VMs list. If not, a **Billing needs attention** popup appears — click **Add Credits** to top up and return.

## Verify

Once provisioned, your GPU VM appears in the **GPU Virtual Machines** list with status **Running**. Click it to open the detail page. **Overview → Connection Details** shows the SSH command (or username and password, or RDP details for Windows).

Confirm GPU access inside the VM:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

If `nvidia-smi` isn't found, install a compatible NVIDIA driver for your OS inside the VM.

## Use the API

The API operation is `POST /compute/gpu-vms`. It takes the same network fields as a cloud VM create (`vpc_id`, `subnet_id`, `network_connectivity`, `vpc_attachment_mode`, `reserved_public_ip_id`) and inline public keys in `ssh_keys`, plus `gpu_model` and `gpu_count`. The API accepts Linux images only (`os_type: linux`). Most other GPU VM operations mirror the cloud VM ones under `/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}`. The **GPU Metrics** tab has no public API operation yet.

## Manage your GPU VM

From the VM detail page, use **Actions** to control your server:

| Action  | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Start   | Power on a stopped server                                                                                              |
| Stop    | Shut down a running server                                                                                             |
| Reboot  | Restart the server                                                                                                     |
| Console | Shown as **Soon** — browser console access isn't available in the portal yet                                           |
| Delete  | Permanently delete the server — you type the VM name to confirm, and can choose to keep its public IP as a Reserved IP |

The detail page has these tabs:

| Tab                         | What it's for                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Overview**                | Specs, network, and **Connection Details**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Monitoring**              | CPU, memory, storage, disk, and network charts, plus recent activity. See [Monitoring](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/monitoring).                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **GPU Metrics**             | GPU utilization, VRAM, temperature, and power. Click **Enable monitoring** first — see [GPU Metrics](/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms#gpu-metrics).                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Backups** / **Snapshots** | Recovery points. See [Backups](/docs/tools/backups) and [Snapshots](/docs/tools/snapshots).                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Settings**                | **Change Plan**, **IPv4 & Reserved IP**, **VPC Networks**, and **Access** (SSH keys, password login, password reset). **Change OS** and **Hostname** aren't available yet. See [Resize a VM](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/resize-a-vm) and [Networking for VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/networking-for-vms). |

> **Warning**
>
> Deleting a GPU VM is permanent and cannot be undone. Back up your data and snapshots before deleting.

## Troubleshooting

**Deploy shows an error message**
The portal validates the form when you click **Deploy** and names the missing item — for example a plan, an OS version, a subnet, or a unique hostname for each instance.

**Billing needs attention popup**
Your organization's billing state or wallet balance blocks the deploy. Click **Add Credits** to top up, then return.

**`nvidia-smi` not found**
The NVIDIA driver isn't installed on the selected image. Install a compatible NVIDIA driver inside the VM. The **GPU Metrics** tab also shows **NVIDIA guest driver required** until it's installed.

**Server stuck in provisioning**
Wait a few minutes. If the status does not update, contact [IBEE support](/docs/support/contact-support).

* [Power actions](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/power-actions)

# Cloud VMs

> Launch and manage virtual machines on IBEE Solutions — flexible compute for web apps, APIs, backends, databases, and dev environments.

IBEE Solutions VMs are KVM-based virtual machines you can deploy in minutes from the IBEE Solutions portal, the [`ibee`](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/launch-your-first-vm#using-the-ibee-cli) CLI, or the API. Pick a location, plan, operating system, and network — your server is provisioned with a root disk, a bandwidth allowance, and either a public IP or a private VPC interface.

> **Info**
>
> **New here?** Follow the 5-minute [Launch your first VM](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/launch-your-first-vm) quickstart.

## What you can do

* Deploy general-purpose servers (Linux or Windows) in supported regions — up to 5 identical VMs at once.
* Pay **Hourly**, or commit **Monthly** or **Yearly** where the plan offers it.
* Connect with a public IP, or put the VM in a VPC with **Private + NAT** or **Private only** networking. Attach [Reserved IPs](/docs/network-security/vpc-ip-management/reserved-ips) and protect it with a firewall group.
* Change plans without rebuilding — upgrade CPU, RAM, and disk, or downgrade CPU and RAM.
* Manage SSH keys, password login, and password resets from **Settings → Access**.
* Attach block storage volumes for persistent data outside the root disk.
* Take **snapshots** as on-demand recovery points, or schedule **automated backups**.
* Restore in place, restore a single disk, or create a new VM from any recovery point.
* Monitor CPU, memory, storage, disk I/O, and network throughput in the portal.
* Automate the public VM create, read, power, metrics, and delete operations via
  the [`ibee` CLI](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/launch-your-first-vm#using-the-ibee-cli)
  and the IBEE Solutions API.

## Find your VMs

In the portal sidebar, open **Infrastructure → Cloud VMs**. The **Cloud Virtual Machines** list shows each VM's **Instance**, **OS**, **Location**, **IP Address**, and **Status**. Use **Search or filter VMs...** to find a VM, the sort menu to order by **Created**, **Name**, **Status**, or **OS** (choose **Use Ascending** to reverse the order), and the page controls to move through long lists. Click a row to open the VM.

From the API, `GET /compute/cloud-vms` lists VMs a page at a time (`limit` default 10, up to 100, plus `offset`).

## Instance families

Two families are available — choose by workload profile, then pick a size within the family.

| Family                                                           | Use case                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Standard VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/instance-types)    | Balanced vCPU and memory for everyday production workloads — web apps, SaaS, APIs, small to medium databases.        |
| [Performance VMs](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/instance-types) | Compute-optimized with higher CPU density — high-traffic web servers, gaming, batch processing, distributed systems. |

For accelerated workloads (training, inference, rendering), see [GPU VMs](/docs/infrastructure/gpu-vms).

## Regions and locations

Cloud VMs are available in the **Asia** region, in data centers in Amaravati and Hyderabad, India. The Deploy page lists the locations open to your organization.

See [Regions and locations](/docs/getting-started/overview/regions-and-locations) for the full availability matrix.

> **Info**
>
> Browser console access to VMs isn't available in the portal yet. Use SSH or RDP with the details under **Overview → Connection Details**, and **Settings → Access** to recover SSH access.

## Lifecycle of a VM

| Stage         | What you do                                                                               | Where                                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Deploy**    | Pick location, plan, OS, SSH keys, network, billing term, and hostname.                   | [Create a VM](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/create-a-vm)                                                                         |
| **Configure** | Attach volumes, adjust firewall rules, attach VPCs and Reserved IPs.                      | [Attach volumes](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/attach-volumes) · [Networking](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/networking-for-vms) |
| **Operate**   | Monitor metrics, run power actions, manage access.                                        | [Monitoring](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/monitoring) · [Power actions](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/power-actions)           |
| **Protect**   | Enable scheduled backups or take manual snapshots.                                        | [Backups](/docs/tools/backups) · [Snapshots](/docs/tools/snapshots)                                                               |
| **Scale**     | Change plan to upgrade CPU, RAM, or disk, or downgrade CPU and RAM — no rebuild required. | [Resize a VM](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/resize-a-vm)                                                                         |
| **Retire**    | Stop and delete when no longer needed.                                                    | [Power actions](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/power-actions#delete)                                                              |

* [Instance types](/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/instance-types)

title: Create a VM
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/infrastructure/cloud-vms/create-a-vm
