# Organizations and tenancy model

> Understand organizations, workspaces, ownership boundaries, and how tenancy works in IBEE Solutions.

IBEE Solutions uses a two-level tenancy model: **organizations** contain **workspaces**, and workspaces contain resources. Billing, team management, and access controls live at the organization level, while compute, storage, and networking resources are scoped to individual workspaces.

## Tenancy hierarchy

```
Account (your login)
└── Organization (billing, team, API tokens)
    └── Workspace (VMs, storage, networking, firewalls)
```

* **Account** — your login identity. One account can own or be a member of multiple organizations.
* **Organization** — the billing and administrative boundary. Each organization has its own wallet, payment method, invoices, team members, API tokens, and activity logs.
* **Workspace** — the resource boundary within an organization. VMs, block storage volumes, object storage buckets, firewalls, load balancers, DNS zones, and other infrastructure resources belong to a workspace.

## What lives where

| Level            | What it contains                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Organization** | Billing (wallet, invoices, payment method, usage limits), team members, API tokens, activity logs, organization settings, KYC/verification status                                                                           |
| **Workspace**    | Cloud VMs, GPU VMs, bare metal servers, object storage buckets, block storage volumes, load balancers, DNS zones, VPCs, firewalls, SSL certificates, backups, snapshots, ISOs, SSH keys, secret manager, container registry |

## URL structure

The portal URL reflects the tenancy model:

| Scope                 | URL pattern                                           | Example              |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| Organization home     | `/organizations/{orgId}/workspaces`                   | Workspace listing    |
| Organization settings | `/organizations/{orgId}/settings`                     | Organization details |
| Billing               | `/organizations/{orgId}/billing/summary`              | Billing summary      |
| Team                  | `/organizations/{orgId}/users`                        | Team members         |
| Workspace resource    | `/organizations/{orgId}/workspaces/{wsId}/{resource}` | Cloud VMs list       |

## Creating an organization

See [Create an organization](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/create-an-organization) for the step-by-step process. Each organization requires a name, account type (Business or Individual), billing address, and currency. You can own up to 3 organizations and join up to 20 by default — see [Organization limits](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas#organization-limits).

To update an organization's name, address, or tax details later, see [Organization settings](/docs/platform-fundamentals/organization-settings).

## Switching organizations

Use the **organization switcher** dropdown in the top navigation bar to move between organizations. You can also return to the Organizations page and select a different card.

## Workspaces

When you open an organization, you land on the **Workspaces** page. Select a workspace to access its resources. Resources like VMs, storage, networking, and SSH keys are scoped to the active workspace.

Every new organization starts with three workspaces — **production**, **dev**, and **stage**. An organization can have up to 5 workspaces; Admins can create more and rename them from the Workspaces page. See [Dashboard & navigation](/docs/getting-started/overview/dashboard#workspaces-page).

Organization-level concerns — billing, team, API tokens, and activity logs — are in the sidebar's **Organization** and **Billing** sections at the organization level. Inside a workspace, the sidebar shows only workspace resources; use **Workspace Details** or the organization switcher to go back.

## Billing scope

Billing is aggregated at the organization level. All resources across all workspaces in an organization share the same wallet balance, payment method, and invoices. Usage limits and quotas also apply at the organization level.

Before creating any billable resource, the portal asks Billing whether the organization can create it, including whether your plan's resource limits allow it. If Billing refuses, for example because the balance is too low or a plan limit is reached, the portal explains why. See [Billing admission checks](/docs/platform-fundamentals/billing-and-usage#billing-admission-checks).

## Best practices

* Use **one organization per billing entity** — each organization gets its own invoices and payment method.
* Use **workspaces to separate environments** — for example, the default `production`, `dev`, and `stage` workspaces within a single organization.
* Assign **least-privilege roles** to team members at the organization level.
* Use **API tokens** scoped to the whole organization, or to specific workspaces, for automation and CI/CD.

* [Team members & access roles](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles)
* [Dashboard](/docs/getting-started/overview/dashboard)

# Organization Settings

> View and edit your IBEE Solutions organization's details — name, type, legal name, billing address, and tax information (GST, VAT, or sales tax) — from the Organization Details page.

The **Organization Details** page holds the information IBEE uses to identify your organization and to prepare billing documents: the organization name, type, legal name, billing address, and tax information. You enter these details when you [create the organization](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/create-an-organization) and can update most of them later.

## Open Organization Details

At the organization level (for example, on the Workspaces page), click **Organization Details** under **Organization** in the sidebar.

## Who can view and edit

| Role                                    | Access                                                 |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Admin** (including the primary owner) | View and edit                                          |
| **Technical**, **Collaborator**         | View only                                              |
| **Billing**                             | Not available — Billing members see only billing pages |

See [Team members & access roles](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles).

## What the page shows

| Field                                       | Notes                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Organization ID**                         | Unique ID of the organization. Cannot be changed.                                                     |
| **Organization Name**                       | The nickname shown in your organization list and switcher                                             |
| **Organization Type**                       | **Business** or **Individual**                                                                        |
| **Currency**                                | Set automatically from the billing country. Cannot be edited here.                                    |
| **Legal Business Name** / **Full Name**     | The name printed on invoices — the legal entity name for a Business, your full name for an Individual |
| **Business Address** / **Personal Address** | The billing address used on invoices                                                                  |
| **Tax Information**                         | GST, VAT, or sales tax number used on billing documents                                               |

## Edit organization details

### Start editing

On **Organization Details**, click **Edit**.

### Update the fields

Change the organization name, organization type, legal name, address, or tax information as needed. The organization ID and currency stay read-only.

### Add or update tax information

Under **Tax Information**, choose the tax type — **GST**, **VAT**, or **Sales Tax** — and enter your number. For GST, the portal verifies the GSTIN against government records and flags a mismatch between the registered company name and the name on your organization.

### Save

Click **Save**. Click **Cancel** to discard your changes.

## IP allowlist

The **IP Allowlist** card on **Organization Details** controls which IP addresses can access the organization. When the list has entries, only requests from those addresses are allowed. The card shows **Your current IP**; include the address you sign in from so you keep your own access.

### Open the add dialog

Click **+ Add IP Address**, or click **Add** next to **Your current IP** to prefill your current address.

### Enter the address

In **Add IP to Allowlist**, enter the **IP Address or CIDR**: an IPv4 address such as `203.0.113.42`, or a range such as `203.0.113.0/24`. Add a **Name** such as `Office` and an optional **Description**.

### Add it

Click **Add IP**. The entry appears in the table with its **Status** and the date it was **Added**.

To take an address off the list, click **Remove** on its row. Only members who can edit organization details can add or remove entries.

* [Organizations and tenancy model](/docs/platform-fundamentals/organizations-and-tenancy-model)
* [Team members & access roles](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles)

---
title: Team Members & Access Roles
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles
description: Invite team members to your IBEE Solutions organization, assign access roles (Admin, Technical, Collaborator, Billing), and control workspace-level permissions.
---

# Team Members & Access Roles

> Invite team members to your IBEE Solutions organization, assign access roles (Admin, Technical, Collaborator, Billing), and control workspace-level permissions.

Team management in IBEE Solutions is organization-level. The organization owner (Primary) invites team members, assigns access roles, and controls which workspaces each member can reach. Each role determines what the member sees and does — from full organization control to read-only workspace access or billing-only views.

## Access roles

Every team member holds one of four access roles:

| Role             | Scope                      | Capabilities                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Admin**        | Organization-wide          | Full access — workspaces, resources, billing, team management, activity logs, support, and API tokens                        |
| **Technical**    | All or selected workspaces | Read & write access to compute, storage, network, tools, support, and resource activity. No billing or team management       |
| **Collaborator** | All or selected workspaces | Read-only access to resources and activity. Cannot create, edit, or delete resources, manage billing, or manage team members |
| **Billing**      | Organization billing       | View and manage Billing Summary, Usage, Invoices, Payment Method, and Usage Limits. No workspace or resource access          |

### Workspace-scoped roles

**Technical** and **Collaborator** roles support workspace scoping:

* **All workspaces** — the member accesses every workspace in the organization, including newly created ones
* **Selected workspaces** — the member accesses only the workspaces chosen during invitation. Toggle each workspace on or off

**Admin** and **Billing** roles are always organization-wide and cannot be workspace-scoped.

> **Warning**
>
> Access roles and workspace scope cannot be edited in place. To change either one, remove the member and send a new invitation with the required role and workspace access.

### Permission details

| Capability                                    | Admin | Technical       | Collaborator    | Billing |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----- | --------------- | --------------- | ------- |
| View workspaces & resources                   | Yes   | Yes             | Yes (read-only) | No      |
| Create, edit, delete resources                | Yes   | Yes             | No              | No      |
| Create workspaces                             | Yes   | No              | No              | No      |
| View billing (Summary, Invoices, etc.)        | Yes   | No              | No              | Yes     |
| Manage billing (Payment Method, Usage Limits) | Yes   | No              | No              | Yes     |
| View team members                             | Yes   | Yes (read-only) | Yes (read-only) | No      |
| Invite, remove, and resend invitations        | Yes   | No              | No              | No      |
| View Organization Details                     | Yes   | Yes (read-only) | Yes (read-only) | No      |
| Edit Organization Details                     | Yes   | No              | No              | No      |
| View activity logs                            | Yes   | Yes             | Yes             | No      |
| Access support                                | Yes   | Yes             | No              | No      |
| Create API tokens                             | Yes   | No              | No              | No      |

## Primary owner

The organization creator is the **Primary owner**, who always holds the Admin role. The Primary owner:

* Cannot be removed from the organization
* Has full access to all workspaces and settings
* Manages team members, along with any other Admins
* Appears at the top of the Team Members table with a "Primary owner" label
* Is the only user who can [transfer ownership](#transfer-ownership)

### Transfer ownership

The Primary owner can hand ownership to another member. The new owner must already be an **active** member — invite them and wait until they accept first.

1. On the **Team Members** page, click **Transfer ownership** in the Primary owner's row.
2. Under **New primary owner**, select an active team member.
3. Type the organization name exactly as shown to confirm.
4. Click **Transfer ownership**.

The selected member becomes the Primary owner. You stay in the organization as an **Admin** with full organization and workspace access. Billing, resources, KYC, workspaces, and notification preferences stay with the organization.

## Invite a team member

Only organization **Admins** can invite team members.

### Go to Team

In the portal sidebar (organization level), click **Team** under **Organization**.

### Click Add Team Member

Click **Add Team Member** in the top right of the Team Members page.

### Enter email

Enter the team member's **Email Address**. This is the only required field — the invitee fills in their name and profile on acceptance.

### Choose an access role

Select one of the four roles:

* **Admin** — full organization access
* **Collaborator** — read-only workspace access
* **Billing** — billing-only organization access
* **Technical** — read & write workspace access

### Select workspace access (Technical and Collaborator only)

For **Technical** and **Collaborator** roles, a workspace access table appears. Each workspace is listed with a toggle switch.

* **Select all** — grants access to every workspace (including future ones)
* **Toggle individual workspaces** — choose exactly which workspaces the member can access

At least one workspace must be selected.

### Send the invitation

Click **Send Invitation**. The invitee receives an email with a link to accept.

> **Info**
>
> Invited members must **sign up** (or log in if they already have an IBEE account) and **accept the invitation** before they gain access. Access is not granted until acceptance.

## Notification types

Each role carries default notification subscriptions:

| Notification type | Description                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Technical**     | Infrastructure alerts, maintenance windows, resource status changes |
| **Billing**       | Invoice notifications, payment confirmations, billing alerts        |
| **Abuse**         | Abuse reports and compliance notifications                          |
| **Emergency**     | Critical infrastructure alerts, security incidents                  |

### Defaults by role

| Role             | Default notifications                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| **Admin**        | Technical, Billing, Abuse, Emergency (all) |
| **Technical**    | Technical, Abuse, Emergency                |
| **Collaborator** | Technical                                  |
| **Billing**      | Billing                                    |

## Manage team members

The **Team Members** page lists all members and invitations in a table with these columns:

* **Member** — name and email address
* **Access Role** — Admin, Technical, Collaborator, or Billing (color-coded badge)
* **Workspace Access** — "All organization workspaces", specific workspace names, or "No workspace access" (Billing role)
* **Status** — **Active** for members; **Invite sent** (awaiting acceptance), **Invite expired**, or **Invitation declined** for invitations
* **Actions** — for Admins: **Resend** for sent or expired invitations, and the trash icon to remove a member or invitation

Technical and Collaborator members can open the Team Members page to see who is in the organization, but they can't invite, remove, or change anyone.

### Resend an invitation

For an invitation that shows **Invite sent** or **Invite expired**, click **Resend**. The invitee receives a new invitation email.

### Remove a team member

Click the **trash icon** to remove a member. A confirmation dialog appears. Removal:

* Revokes access to the organization immediately
* Removes login access to all workspaces in the organization
* Cannot be undone — re-invite to restore access

To assign a different access role or workspace scope, remove the member and send a new invitation with the updated selections.

### Remove an invitation

Sent, expired, and declined invitations appear in the table. Click the **trash icon** to delete an invitation.

## Accepting an invitation

When invited, a team member:

1. Receives an email with invitation details (organization name, role, inviter).
2. Sees the invitation on the **Organizations** page — with the inviter, role, workspace access, and expiry date — and **Accept** and **Decline** buttons.
3. Clicking **Accept** grants access immediately with the assigned role and workspace scope.
4. Clicking **Decline** marks the invitation as declined. The admin can remove it or re-invite.

Invitations expire. If an invitation has expired, ask the admin to click **Resend** on the Team Members page.

> **Info**
>
> You can be a member of up to 20 organizations that you don't own. See [Limits & Quotas](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas#organization-limits).

## FAQ

**What happens when "All workspaces" is selected for a Technical member?**
The member gains access to every current workspace and any workspace created in the future. This is equivalent to organization-scope access for that role.

**Can a Billing role member see resources?**
No. Billing members see only billing pages (Summary, Usage, Invoices, Payment Method, Usage Limits) and have no workspace or resource access.

title: Activity logs
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/platform-fundamentals/activity-logs

# Activity logs

> Review who did what across your IBEE Solutions organization — search, filter by service, workspace, status, and time range, open an event's details, and export the results as CSV.

**Activity Logs** records actions taken across your organization — creating, changing, and deleting resources, team and billing changes, security events, and support activity — together with who performed them and whether they succeeded. Use it to answer "who changed this?", to trace a failed operation, or to keep a record for audits.

## Open Activity Logs

At the organization level, click **Activity Logs** under **Organization** in the sidebar. The page covers the whole organization; when it has more than one workspace, use the **Workspace** filter to narrow it to one.

Admin, Technical, and Collaborator members can open Activity Logs. Billing members cannot. Each member sees only the activity their role allows. See [Team members & access roles](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles).

## Read the list

Each row is one event, newest first:

| Column                 | What it shows                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Time**               | When the event happened. Hover for the full timestamp.                                      |
| **Action**             | What was done, for example a create, update, restore, or delete                             |
| **Product / resource** | The resource acted on, with its type and context (such as the VM a volume was attached to)  |
| **Actor**              | The member who performed the action, or **System** for actions IBEE performed automatically |
| **Source service**     | The IBEE service that recorded the event                                                    |
| **Status**             | **Succeeded**, **Failed**, **In progress**, **Accepted**, or **Cancelled**                  |

Click a row to expand its details:

| Detail                 | Notes                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Time**               | Full date and time                                                                                 |
| **Product / resource** | Product, resource type, name, and ID                                                               |
| **Workspace**          | The workspace the resource belongs to, when it has one                                             |
| **Actor**              | Name, email, and the IP address the action came from                                               |
| **Source service**     | The service that recorded the event                                                                |
| **Changed**            | The fields that changed, for update events                                                         |
| **Reason**             | For failed events: the error code, the HTTP status, and — for bulk actions — how many items failed |
| **Reference**          | The event ID. Click to copy it — include it when you contact support about an event.               |

## Search and filter

Use the controls above the list. Filters combine, and the list reloads as you change them.

| Control        | Options                                                                                            |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Search**     | Matches a user, resource, or action                                                                |
| **Service**    | All services, Compute, Storage, Network, Billing, Organization, Security, Registry, Support, Email |
| **Workspace**  | All workspaces or one workspace                                                                    |
| **Status**     | All statuses, Succeeded, Failed, In progress, Accepted, Cancelled                                  |
| **Time range** | Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, **Last 30 days** (default), Last 90 days                               |

The list loads in pages. Click **Load more** at the bottom to see older events, and the refresh button next to **Export CSV** to fetch new ones.

> **Tip**
>
> To investigate a failed operation, set **Status** to **Failed**, then expand the event to read the **Reason** and copy its **Reference**.

## Export to CSV

Click **Export CSV** to download the events that match your current search, filters, and time range. The file is named `activity-<organization-id>-<date>.csv`.

The button is disabled when the list is empty. If the export is too large, the portal shows an error — narrow the time range or add a filter, then export again.

## Troubleshooting

**"No activity in this period."**
Nothing was recorded in the selected time range. Choose a longer range, up to **Last 90 days**.

**"No activity matches these filters."**
Clear the search box or set the filters back to **All** to widen the results.

**I can't see Activity Logs in the sidebar.**
Your role does not include activity access — Billing members cannot view it. Ask an organization Admin to change your role.

title: Billing and usage
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/platform-fundamentals/billing-and-usage
description: Learn how billing works in IBEE Solutions — prepaid wallet credits or Invoice Billing, the billing summary, usage charts, invoices, billing checks before creation, and plan limits.
---

# Billing and usage

> Learn how billing works in IBEE Solutions — prepaid wallet credits or Invoice Billing, the billing summary, usage charts, invoices, billing checks before creation, and plan limits.

New IBEE Solutions organizations use a **prepaid wallet**: you add credits, and usage is deducted as resources run. Organizations approved for **Invoice Billing** are billed monthly in arrears within a credit limit instead. Before creating a new resource, the platform checks your billing state — if your wallet does not cover it or billing needs attention, you'll be asked to resolve it first.

## Billing model

All billing is scoped to the **organization** level. Every workspace within an organization shares the same wallet balance, payment method, and invoices.

| Concept            | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Wallet balance** | Prepaid credits available for usage. Split into **Promo balance** and **Purchased credits**. |
| **Billing cycle**  | The current month's accumulated usage charges.                                               |
| **Invoices**       | Statements for the organization, with a PDF for each.                                        |
| **Payment method** | Cards saved on the organization (organizations outside India).                               |
| **Usage limits**   | Your plan's resource limits, such as the number of CPU VMs or total block storage size.      |
| **Currency**       | Amounts are shown in your organization's billing currency (INR or USD).                      |

The billing pages are under **Billing** in the sidebar: **Summary**, **Usage**, **Invoices**, **Payment Method**, and **Usage Limits**. Only members with the **Admin** or **Billing** role can open them; other members see *"You don't have access to billing for this organization."* See [Team members & access roles](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles).

## Billing summary

**Billing → Summary** shows the current billing cycle:

* **Current cycle** — the total so far this month, with the cycle dates and when it was computed.
* **Usage charges** — charges grouped by product category. Click a category or product to expand it; each line shows **Component**, **Usage**, **Rate**, and **Amount**. When charges name individual resources, switch between **By category** and **By resource**.

Everything starts collapsed. Amounts do not include sales tax. Click **Refresh** to reload.

## Usage

**Billing → Usage** charts usage over time.

1. Choose a period: **24 hours**, **7 days**, **30 days** (default), or **90 days**.
2. Choose **Cost** to chart spend per service, or **Units** to chart metered quantities (shown when unit data is available).

The page shows the **Total for period**, a card per service with its share of the total, and a **Breakdown** table per product with **Component**, **Plan**, **Usage**, **Rate**, and **Amount**. If some hours of usage were not recorded, a notice says how many; gaps are left blank rather than estimated.

## Invoices

**Billing → Invoices** lists the organization's invoices, newest first, with **Date**, **Type**, **Number**, **Amount**, **Due date**, and **Status** (for example **Paid**, **Payment due**, or **Overdue**). Click the download icon on a row to open the invoice PDF; it is disabled until the PDF is ready.

## Invoice Billing

For an organization on Invoice Billing, **Billing → Payment Method** shows an **Invoice Billing** card instead of the purchase flow:

* **Credit used** against the credit limit, with the percentage used.
* **This month**, **Earlier months not yet invoiced**, and **Unpaid invoices** — what the credit used is made of.
* **Payment terms** and the **Next invoice** date.

At 80% of the limit the card warns you. When the limit is reached, new resources are blocked until unpaid invoices are paid; running resources are not affected. Click **Request higher limit** to ask support for a higher limit, or **View invoices** to open the invoice list. To apply for Invoice Billing, see [Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing#apply-for-invoice-billing).

## Billing admission checks

Before creating a billable resource — for example a Cloud VM, GPU VM, block storage volume, snapshot, bucket, load balancer, reserved IP, CDN distribution, custom domain, secret, or container registry — the portal asks Billing whether the organization can create it. Creation continues only when Billing allows it.

If Billing refuses, the portal explains why. On the VM, GPU VM, and Container Registry pages this is a **Billing needs attention** popup; other pages show the message as an error.

| Situation                                                             | What to do                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| First top-up not made yet (prepaid)                                   | Add credits. The message shows the minimum amount. |
| Wallet balance does not cover the resource                            | Add credits and try again.                         |
| Billing is past due                                                   | Add credits or settle the outstanding usage.       |
| Credit limit reached (Invoice Billing)                                | Pay unpaid invoices.                               |
| Organization is billing-suspended, or an overdue billing case is open | Resolve billing, then try again.                   |
| Pricing could not be verified                                         | Refresh the page or choose another plan.           |

When adding credits can resolve the block, the popup shows **Add Credits**. It opens **Payment Method** with the purchase dialog already open; after paying, return to the create page to continue.

### Plan limit reached

If a create would go over your plan's resource limit, the portal shows a message such as *"Your plan allows N CPU VMs. Upgrade your plan or request a limit increase to add more."*, with your plan's number. Click **Request a limit increase** to open Support. See [Limits & Quotas](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas).

### Use the API

Public API integrations make the same check with `POST /billing/resource-eligibility` (scope `billing.read`) and continue only when `allowed` is exactly `true`. Add `resource_type`, `quantity`, and, for sized resources, `size_gb` so Billing also checks your plan's resource limits; `operation` defaults to `CREATE_RESOURCE`. The response lists the plan's `resource_limits`. When a limit refuses the request, `reason` is `resource_limit_reached`, and `resource_limit_key`, `resource_limit`, and `resource_usage` say which limit applied and how much is used. See [Billing admission before creation](/docs/api-reference/introduction#billing-admission-before-creation).

Product APIs do not receive wallet balances or other client-supplied billing state.

## Adding credits

Open **Billing → Payment Method** and click **Purchase credits**, or click **Add Credits** in a billing popup. See [Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing).

## Usage limits

**Billing → Usage Limits** shows your current tier, your billing mode, and, for each limited resource, how much is **Used**, the **Limit**, and what is **Remaining**, across all workspaces. The page is read-only; to change your plan, raise a support request. See [Limits & Quotas](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas).

## Restricted or suspended organizations

If an organization is restricted — for example for an overdue payment — a red banner appears at the top of every page. You can still view resources and pay, but you can't create or change anything.

If an organization is suspended, its virtual machines are switched off and its resource pages are hidden. Organization details, team, **Summary**, **Invoices**, **Payment Method**, and Support stay open. The banner says what is owed and warns that the resources will be deleted if the suspension is not resolved in time.

Click **Go to billing** to pay (shown to members who can open billing), or **Contact support**.

## Related pages

* [Organizations and tenancy model](/docs/platform-fundamentals/projects-and-tenancy-model)
* [Add billing](/docs/getting-started/account-setup/add-billing)
* [Limits and quotas](/docs/platform-fundamentals/limits-and-quotas)
* [Dashboard](/docs/getting-started/overview/dashboard)

# Limits & Quotas

> Compare IBEE Solutions plans, monthly spend thresholds, and resource allowances, see your usage against them, and learn how to request a plan change.

Open **Billing → Usage Limits** in the portal to see your organization's current tier and billing mode and, for each limited resource, how much is **Used**, its **Limit**, and what is **Remaining**, across all workspaces. A limit shows **Unlimited** when the plan sets none and **Not included in tier** when the plan allows none. Click **Refresh** to reload, or **click here** on that page to open the plan comparison below.

When a create would go over a limit, the portal refuses it with a message naming your plan's limit and a **Request a limit increase** button that opens Support.

CDN refers to CDN distributions. Monthly spend is shown in INR and USD.

Monthly spend thresholds are shown in INR and USD; use the value for your billing currency. They are not a flat subscription price or a promise of an automatic plan change. Request a plan change through support.

Storage allowances are total capacity, not the number of volumes or snapshots. In this table, 1 TB corresponds to 1,024 GB in the portal. Reserved IP allowances apply to customer-reserved addresses.

**Postpaid organizations have the same resource allowances as prepaid ones.** Their credit limit is a separate, monetary check. Organization, workspace, and technical service limits are also separate from these resource allowances.

## Change your plan

To change your organization's plan, raise a support request:

1. Click **Support** in the portal's top bar, then **Technical Support**.
2. Select **Others** as the product.
3. Give your organization, current tier (shown on **Billing → Usage Limits**), the plan you want, and the reason, then click **Submit Request**.

A request does not change your plan or resource allowances by itself; your current plan stays active until the change is approved. See [Create a request](/docs/support/create-a-request) for the support flow.

## Organization limits

These limits apply to your login rather than to a single organization:

| Limit                                        | Default | Adjustable                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Organizations you own                        | 3       | Yes — [request more organizations](#request-more-organizations) |
| Organizations you've joined as a team member | 20      | No                                                              |

The **Organizations** page shows your usage, for example *"1 of 3 owned organizations used. Joined 2 of 20 organizations."* When you reach the owned-organization limit, the **Create Organization** button is hidden.

### Request more organizations

### Open the request

On the **Organizations** page, click **click here** in the usage line (it appears when you've reached your limit). If you try to create an organization while at the limit, the portal opens the same **Request More Organizations** page.

### Fill in the request

In **Increase organization limit**:

* **Requested total** — the total number of owned organizations you need (up to 20).
* **Reason** — explain how the additional organizations will be used (20–2,000 characters).

### Send the request

Click **Send request**. The usage line changes to **Request submitted** while the request waits for approval.

When the request is decided, the Organizations page shows the result. If it's approved, your owned-organization limit increases. If it's rejected, your limit stays the same and the portal shows when you can apply again.

## Workspace limits

| Resource                    | Default limit | Adjustable                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspaces per organization | 5             | Yes — contact [support@ibee.ai](mailto:support@ibee.ai) |

Every new organization starts with three workspaces — **production**, **dev**, and **stage** — which count toward this limit. When the limit is reached, the Workspaces page shows a **contact support** link for more workspaces.

## Product limits

The [plan comparison](#plan-comparison) covers CPU VMs, GPU VMs, block storage capacity, snapshot capacity, CDN distributions, load balancers, and reserved IPs. Product-specific technical constraints are documented on the relevant product pages and are separate from plan allowances.

Snapshots can capture the root disk and attached data volumes. Select **Root only**, **All attached**, or **Selective** when creating a snapshot.

## API and access limits

| Resource                    | Default limit | Adjustable |
| --------------------------- | ------------- | ---------- |
| API tokens per organization | 10            | No         |
| SSH keys                    | 50            | No         |

To own more organizations, use the [organization limit request](#request-more-organizations). For a different resource allowance, [request a plan change](#change-your-plan).

# Support

> Get help from IBEE Solutions — open a Technical Support request from the portal Support Center, find organization and billing settings, and track every request in one place.

The **Support Center** is where you ask the IBEE team for help — a server that's down, a bucket you can't reach, or a question about your account. Open a request, attach context, and follow it through to resolution from the same screen.

Open the Support Center by clicking **Support** in the portal's top bar, or go to `portal.ibee.ai/organizations/{orgId}/support`. Support is available to **Admin** and **Technical** members — see [Team members & access roles](/docs/platform-fundamentals/team-members-access-roles).

## What support covers

Basic technical support is included with every VM, whether you manage it from the portal, the [CLI](/docs/api-reference/cli), or the API. Raise a request from the Support Center or email [support@ibee.ai](mailto:support@ibee.ai). Each request gets a ticket number and a priority, and is tracked until it is resolved.

**Included in basic support**

* VM provisioning issues — a VM that isn't created or doesn't start
* A VM that isn't reachable over SSH, and help recovering access (SSH keys or password reset)
* Platform-level performance issues (CPU, disk, network)
* Unexpected VM reboots or crashes
* Resizing or upgrading vCPU, RAM and disk
* Network, IP and firewall issues on IBEE's side
* Help with snapshots, backups and restores
* Billing and account questions

**Not included in basic support**

* Administration inside the operating system — installing or configuring packages, users and services
* Your own applications, code, databases and third-party software
* Security hardening and patching inside the VM
* Recovering data when no snapshot or backup exists — see [Snapshots](/docs/tools/snapshots) and [Backups](/docs/tools/backups)

## Choose a category

The Support Center landing page shows three categories. Only **Technical Support** opens a request form; the other two take you to the self-service page for that area.

#### Organization Support

#### Billing Support

#### Technical Support

To raise a billing or account question with the support team, open **Technical Support** and choose the **Others** product ("General enquiries, billing, account & anything else"). See [Create a request](/docs/support/create-a-request) for the full form.

## My Requests

Below the categories, the **My Requests** card opens the list of every request raised in your organization at `portal.ibee.ai/organizations/{orgId}/support/request/all`.

Each row shows the request subject, ticket number, who created it, the related resource (if any), how long ago it was opened, and its priority and status. Use **Search requests...** to find a request, and the filters to narrow by **Status**, **Priority**, or time (**Today**, **Yesterday**, **This Week**, or a custom range).

| Status               | Meaning                                          |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **Created**          | Request received                                 |
| **Assigned**         | An engineer has picked up the request            |
| **In Progress**      | The support team is working on it                |
| **Waiting for User** | The support team replied and needs your response |
| **Resolved**         | The issue is resolved                            |
| **Closed**           | The request is closed                            |

Click any row to open the request: the message thread, the **Issue Details** you submitted, and a **Reply** option. A resolved or closed request can be reopened with **Reopen ticket** so you can reply again; if it was closed too long ago, create a new request instead.

## Response expectations

You set the priority when you submit a request. Higher-priority requests are reviewed first.

| Priority   | Use when                                                   |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Low**    | Question or minor issue with no business impact            |
| **Medium** | Standard issue with no immediate business impact (default) |
| **High**   | Significant impact requiring prompt attention              |
| **Urgent** | Critical — service is down or severely degraded            |

> **Info**
>
> For fastest response on critical issues, set priority to **Urgent** and include error logs or screenshots in your request.

## Contact by email

| Type              | Email                                     |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Technical support | [support@ibee.ai](mailto:support@ibee.ai) |
| Abuse reports     | [abuse@ibee.ai](mailto:abuse@ibee.ai)     |
| Sales inquiries   | [sales@ibee.ai](mailto:sales@ibee.ai)     |

# Create a Support Request

> Submit a Technical Support request from the IBEE Solutions portal. Pick a product and resource, describe your issue, set priority, attach screenshots, and track the request through resolution.

Open the Support Center by clicking **Support** in the portal's top bar (or go to `portal.ibee.ai/organizations/{orgId}/support`). Open **Technical Support**, fill in the form, and submit. Every request you open shows up under **My Requests** for tracking and replies.

## Categories

| Category                 | What happens when you click it                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Organization Support** | Opens **Organization Details**, where you manage your organization's settings.                                                                       |
| **Billing Support**      | Opens the billing pages — payment methods, credits, and invoices.                                                                                    |
| **Technical Support**    | Opens the request form below. Use it for every request to the support team, including billing and account questions (choose the **Others** product). |

## Create a Technical Support request

The Technical Support form is dynamic — fields appear based on the **Product** and **Issue Type** you choose.

### 1. Open Technical Support

In the Support Center, click **Technical Support**. The form lives at `portal.ibee.ai/organizations/{orgId}/support/technical` with the heading *"Select a product to get started with your support request."*

### 2. Select a product

Click the **Product** dropdown and pick the affected service. Each option shows a one-line description.

| Product            | Description                                         |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **Object Storage** | S3-Compatible Object Storage                        |
| **Cloud VMs**      | Scalable Virtual Machines                           |
| **GPU VMs**        | High-Performance GPU Virtual Machines               |
| **Baremetal**      | Dedicated Baremetal Servers                         |
| **Load Balancer**  | Load Balancer as a Service                          |
| **Firewall**       | Firewall as a Service                               |
| **Database**       | Database as a Service                               |
| **Block Storage**  | High-Performance Block Storage Volumes              |
| **Others**         | General enquiries, billing, account & anything else |

### 3. Select a resource

After choosing a product, a second dropdown appears for the specific resource (e.g. **Cloud VM**). The list shows each resource with its specs, location, and status:

| Display          | Example                                        |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Name             | `web-prod-01`                                  |
| Specs · Location | `8 vCPU · 32 GB · India - Mumbai`              |
| Status           | Running (green) / Stopped (grey) / Error (red) |

A search field at the top filters the list.

### 4. Select an issue type

The **Issue Type** dropdown shows a searchable list scoped to the chosen product. For Cloud VMs:

* Provisioning Failed / Instance Not Created
* VM Not Reachable (SSH / RDP)
* Performance Low / High CPU Usage
* Unexpected Reboot / Crash
* Resize / Upgrade Request

Additional fields appear under the dropdown based on which issue type you pick.

### 5. Fill in the issue details

Each issue type renders its own structured fields. Examples:

**VM Not Reachable (SSH / RDP)**

| Field                                  | Type                          |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Which IP is affected?                  | Public IP / Private IP / Both |
| Access Method                          | SSH / RDP / Console / VNC     |
| When did it start?                     | Date & time                   |
| Any firewall / security group changes? | Yes / No                      |
| Attach error / log output              | Text area                     |

**Resize / Upgrade Request**

| Field                           | Type                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Upgrade Type \*                 | Multi-select: vCPU, RAM, Disk Size    |
| Downtime allowed? \*            | Yes / No                              |
| Preferred Maintenance Window \* | ASAP / Schedule specific time / Other |

### 6. Set priority and details

Every request also shares these fields:

| Field                        | Description                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Region / Site** (optional) | The site your issue is in. Leave it empty if you're not sure — it's filled in from the resource when you picked one. |
| **Priority** \*              | `Low` / `Medium` (default) / `High` / `Urgent`                                                                       |
| **Additional Details** \*    | Free-text, at least 20 characters — *"Describe the issue or request in detail…"*                                     |
| **Attachments** (optional)   | Upload screenshots or images — PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF, WebP (Max 10 MB each)                                            |

### 7. Submit

Click **Submit Request**. The request is created and appears under **My Requests**.

## Track your requests

Click **My Requests** in the Support Center, or open `portal.ibee.ai/organizations/{orgId}/support/request/all`. The **Support Requests** page lists your organization's requests with a **Search requests...** field and filters for **Status**, **Priority**, and time range.

Each row shows:

| Field      | Example                                                                             |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title      | `Server Not Reachable`                                                              |
| Ticket #   | `#07248819`                                                                         |
| Created by | The member who opened the request                                                   |
| Resource   | `in-vga-pi-r02-srv01`                                                               |
| Age        | `28d ago`                                                                           |
| Priority   | `Low` / `Medium` / `High` / `Urgent`                                                |
| Status     | `Created` / `Assigned` / `In Progress` / `Waiting for User` / `Resolved` / `Closed` |

Click a row to open the full request detail.

## Request detail view

The detail panel shows the full message thread plus an **Issue Details** card with the structured fields you filled in at submission time. For a *"Server Not Reachable"* request:

| Field                       | Example                 |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Which IP is not reachable?  | `Ipmi`                  |
| Issue Type                  | `Ssh Fails`             |
| When did it start?          | `Mar 6, 2026, 10:12 AM` |
| Business Impact             | `Partial Service`       |
| Is IPMI / iDRAC accessible? | `No`                    |
| Any recent changes made?    | `None`                  |

The header shows the title, who created the request, its age, ticket number, status badge, and priority badge.

## Reply to a request

Click **Reply** at the bottom-right of the detail panel to open the **Writing a Reply** composer.

| Field       | Description                                              |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Message     | Free-text — *"Type your reply…"*                         |
| Attachments | Click to upload images — PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP — Max 10 MB |

Click **Send Reply** to post. **Cancel** discards the draft.

### Reopen a resolved or closed request

You can't reply to a request that is **Resolved** or **Closed**. Open it and click **Reopen ticket** to continue the conversation. If the request was closed too long ago, the portal says it can't be reopened — click **Create a new support ticket** instead.

## Tips for faster resolution

* **Pick the right product and resource** — the support team uses these to scope their investigation.
* **Set Priority honestly** — `Urgent` is for downtime; over-using it slows everyone down.
* **Attach logs and screenshots** — paste error output into Additional Details and attach screenshots showing the symptom.
* **Mention what changed recently** — recent deploys, network changes, or scaling events often correlate with the issue.

* [Contact support](/docs/support/contact-support)

title: Introduction
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/introduction
description: Overview of the IBEE Solutions public API.
---

# Introduction

> Overview of the IBEE Solutions public API.

The IBEE Solutions API gives you programmatic access to your infrastructure. You can manage virtual machines, object storage buckets, secrets, and more — all from your own code or automation tools.

## Base URL

All API requests use the following base URL:

```
https://api.ibee.ai/v1
```

## Workspace scoping

Every API request must include a `workspace_id` query parameter. This scopes the request to a specific workspace within your organization.

```bash
curl https://api.ibee.ai/v1/object-storage/buckets?workspace_id=907479 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

Workspaces isolate resources so that production, staging, and development environments stay separate. You choose which workspaces a token can access when you create it.

## Billing admission before creation

Public API integrations use the same centralized billing admission flow as the
IBEE portal. Before sending a billable create request, call
`POST /billing/resource-eligibility` for the same workspace and continue only
when the response contains `"allowed": true`.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/billing/resource-eligibility?workspace_id=907479" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sku_code":"OBJECTST-STD"}'
```

The token needs `billing.read` in addition to the write scope for the product
being created. Treat a denied, malformed, or unavailable decision as a blocked
create; do not send the product request. The decision is point-in-time and does
not reserve funds, so perform it immediately before creation.

To have Billing also check your plan's resource limits, add `resource_type`
(for example `cpu_vm`, `block_volume` or `public_ipv4`), `quantity`, and
`size_gb` for sized resources. `operation` defaults to `CREATE_RESOURCE`. The
response lists the plan's `resource_limits`; when a limit refuses the request,
`reason` is `resource_limit_reached` and `resource_limit_key`,
`resource_limit` and `resource_usage` say which limit and how much is used.

Billing state and prices are evaluated by the shared billing admission layer.
Do not send wallet balances, credit limits, or other billing state to product
APIs.

## Available resources

| Resource            | Description                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Secret Store**    | Create stores, manage secrets, and retrieve values.                          |
| **Object Storage**  | Create and manage S3-compatible storage buckets.                             |
| **Compute catalog** | Discover placement sites, plans, and compatible OS images.                   |
| **Cloud VMs**       | Deploy and manage cloud virtual machines.                                    |
| **GPU VMs**         | Deploy and manage GPU-accelerated virtual machines for AI/ML workloads.      |
| **VPC networking**  | Manage isolated networks, subnets, VM attachments, NAT, and port forwarding. |
| **Reserved IPs**    | Reserve and move portable public IPv4 addresses.                             |
| **Firewalls**       | Manage firewall groups, rules, and VM attachments.                           |
| **Load balancers**  | Provision and manage L4 and L7 load balancers.                               |
| **Billing**         | Run the resource eligibility preflight before billable creates.              |

## Response format

All responses are JSON. Successful responses return the resource directly.

## Errors

Every error uses one body. A refusal from the gateway carries a
machine-readable `error` code, plus `required_scope`, `billing_reason`,
`billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` (each
`null` when it does not apply). A refusal from the product service behind the
gateway carries `detail` instead.

```json
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "required_scope": "vm.write",
  "billing_reason": null,
  "billing_sku_code": null,
  "billing_evaluated_at": null,
  "admission_context_id": null
}
```

| Status | Gateway `error` codes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`  | `workspace_id_required`, `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required` or `invalid_site_id`.                                                                                                                                       |
| `401`  | `invalid_api_key` — the token is missing, malformed, or unknown.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `402`  | `billing_denied` — Billing refused the request. `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required` or `resource_limit_reached`. Nothing is provisioned.                                                                    |
| `403`  | `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member`, `principal_permission_denied`; on writes also `organization_restricted` and `verification_required`. |
| `423`  | `organization_suspended` — writes are refused while the organization is suspended.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `429`  | A concurrency limit was reached, for example too many console sessions. Retry later.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `503`  | A service the request depends on did not answer, for example `billing_admission_unavailable` or `workspace_verification_unavailable`.                                                                                                                                                                    |

`404` and `409` come from the product service with `detail`. Each endpoint in
the API reference lists the statuses it can return.

## Pagination

The cloud VM, GPU VM, and firewall group lists return 10 records unless you
pass `limit` (at most 100). Use `offset` to read the next page:

```bash
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vms?workspace_id=907479&limit=100&offset=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN"
```

Other lists have their own `limit` default and maximum, shown on each endpoint.

## Async operations

Some operations — creating, deleting, starting, stopping, or rebooting virtual machines — are asynchronous. These endpoints return `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id` you can poll:

```json
{
  "operation_id": "op_123",
  "vm_id": "vm_abc123",
  "status": "accepted",
  "submitted_at": "2026-07-01T12:00:00Z"
}
```

Use the [Get operation status](/docs/api-reference/cloud-vms/get-compute-operation) endpoint to check progress.

## VM network options and delete

VM create accepts launch network options: `vpc_id` with `subnet_id`,
`network_connectivity` (`private`, `nat` or `public_ip`),
`vpc_attachment_mode` (`primary` or `secondary`) and `reserved_public_ip_id`.
Omit them to launch on the public provider network. Inline public keys go in
`ssh_keys`, next to saved keys in `ssh_key_ids`. See
[Create a cloud VM](/docs/api-reference/cloud-vms/create-cloud-vm) for the
rules that combine them.

VM delete takes an optional body. A VM whose public IP was assigned
automatically is refused with `400` unless you set `public_ip_action`:
`release` releases the address with the VM, and `reserve` keeps it as a
Reserved IP (send `reserved_ip_billing_catalog` with it, and optionally
`reserved_ip_label`).

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vms/vm_abc123?workspace_id=907479" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: delete-vm-abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"public_ip_action":"release"}'
```

## Idempotency

VM create, delete, and power operations require an `X-Idempotency-Key` header.
If one of these requests fails due to a network issue, you can safely retry it
with the same key. Other write operations do not currently require this header;
follow the requirement shown on each endpoint.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vms?workspace_id=907479 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: unique-request-id-123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"web-server-01","plan_id":"plan_standard_2c_4g","template_id":"tmpl_ubuntu_2204","os_distro":"ubuntu","os_type":"linux","cpu":2,"ram_mb":4096}'
```

## Machine-readable access

Everything in this reference is also available as data, for code generators
and AI agents:

| What                                                                                                             | Where                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| OpenAPI 3.1 specification, as served by the docs                                                                 | [openapi.yaml](https://ibee.ai/docs/openapi.yaml) · [openapi.json](https://ibee.ai/docs/openapi.json)                                                        |
| The authored specification, with the API title, version, introduction and tag descriptions the served copy omits | [contract/ibee-cloud.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devs-ibee/examples/main/contract/ibee-cloud.yaml) in the public `devs-ibee/examples` repository |
| API catalog ([RFC 9727](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9727))                                                 | [/.well-known/api-catalog](https://ibee.ai/.well-known/api-catalog)                                                                                          |
| Index of every docs page, one line each                                                                          | [/docs/llms.txt](https://ibee.ai/docs/llms.txt)                                                                                                              |
| Full text of every docs page in one file                                                                         | [/docs/llms-full.txt](https://ibee.ai/docs/llms-full.txt)                                                                                                    |
| Markdown of any page                                                                                             | append `.md` to its URL, for example [create-cloud-vm.md](https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/cloud-vms/create-cloud-vm.md)                                   |
| MCP server for AI clients (Claude Code, Cursor and others)                                                       | `https://ibee.ai/docs/_mcp/server`                                                                                                                           |

claude mcp add --transport http ibee-docs https://ibee.ai/docs/_mcp/server

title: Authentication
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/authentication
description: Learn how to create API tokens and authenticate your requests.

# Authentication

> Learn how to create API tokens and authenticate your requests.

Every API request must include a valid platform API token. Tokens use Bearer authentication and are scoped to your organization.

## Create an API token

1. Log in to the [IBEE portal](https://portal.ibee.ai).
2. Go to **Settings → API Tokens**.
3. Click **Create Token**.
4. Give the token a name, select the scopes it needs, and choose a workspace policy.
5. Click **Create**. Copy the token immediately — it is shown only once.

> **Warning**
>
> Store your token securely — it cannot be viewed again after creation. If a
> token is lost or exposed, revoke it and create a new one. Never embed a token
> in client-side code (browser or mobile apps) or commit it to source control.

## Using your token

Include the token in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token:

```bash
curl https://api.ibee.ai/v1/object-storage/buckets?workspace_id=907479 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ibee_prod_key_xxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`. Development tokens start with
`ibee_dev_key_` and must be sent to `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1`. Tokens are
environment-specific; a development token is not valid against production and
vice versa.

## Scopes

Each token is granted specific scopes that control which resources it can access. Select the minimum scopes your integration needs.

| Scope                      | Permission                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `secret-store.read`        | List stores, get secret metadata and values.                                                                                                                                 |
| `secret-store.write`       | Create stores, create and update secrets, and manage access identities. Reading an identity's login details also needs this scope, because each call issues a new secret ID. |
| `object-storage.read`      | List and read buckets.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `object-storage.write`     | Create buckets.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `object-storage.delete`    | Delete buckets.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `network.read`             | List VPCs, subnets, NAT gateways, reserved IPs, and firewall resources.                                                                                                      |
| `network.write`            | Create, update, attach, and delete networking resources.                                                                                                                     |
| `load-balancer.read`       | List load balancers and read provisioning status.                                                                                                                            |
| `load-balancer.write`      | Create, update, and delete load balancers.                                                                                                                                   |
| `vm.read`                  | List and get virtual machines and operations.                                                                                                                                |
| `vm.write`                 | Create, update, delete VMs and run power actions.                                                                                                                            |
| `billing.read`             | Check whether a workspace is eligible to create billable resources.                                                                                                          |
| `block-storage.read`       | List volumes and read volume operation history.                                                                                                                              |
| `block-storage.write`      | Create, attach, detach, resize, and delete volumes.                                                                                                                          |
| `cdn.read`                 | List CDN distributions, website settings, and custom domains.                                                                                                                |
| `cdn.write`                | Manage distributions, website settings, domains, URLs, and cache purges.                                                                                                     |
| `container-registry.read`  | List and get registries, storage plans, registry access tokens, repositories, images, vulnerability findings, SBOMs, and metrics.                                            |
| `container-registry.write` | Create, change, empty, and delete registries; upgrade storage plans; create, rotate, and revoke registry access tokens; delete repositories and images; rescan images.       |

A request to an endpoint that requires a scope the token does not have returns `403 Forbidden`.

The SDKs and CLI expose an explicit billing eligibility check for previews and
diagnostics. A token needs `billing.read` only when your integration calls that
check directly. Billable create requests need only the corresponding product
write scope: the public gateway makes a fail-closed, authoritative billing
decision before it forwards the request to the existing product service.

## Workspace policies

When you create a token, you choose how it accesses workspaces:

| Policy                  | Behavior                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Entire organization** | The token can access any workspace in the organization.                                                   |
| **Specific workspaces** | The token can only access the workspaces you select. Requests to other workspaces return `403 Forbidden`. |

Use **Specific workspaces** when you want to limit a CI/CD pipeline or integration to a single environment (for example, only staging).

## Revoking tokens

To revoke a token:

1. Go to **Settings → API Tokens** in the portal.
2. Find the token and click **Revoke**.

Revoked tokens are rejected immediately on all subsequent requests.

## Error responses

| Status             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | `invalid_api_key`: the token is missing, malformed, or unknown.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `403 Forbidden`    | The token may not make this call. `insufficient_scope` names the missing scope in `required_scope`; `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive` and `key_expired` describe the token; `workspace_not_allowed` means the token's workspace policy excludes the workspace. On writes, `organization_restricted` and `verification_required` are also possible. |
| `423 Locked`       | `organization_suspended`: writes are refused while the organization is suspended.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

The `error` field of the response body carries the code. See
[Errors](/docs/api-reference/introduction#errors) for the full body and the
other statuses.


---
title: Rate limits
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/rate-limits
description: Understand API request limits and how to handle them.
---

# Rate limits

> Understand API request limits and how to handle them.

The IBEE Solutions API may apply rate limits to ensure fair usage and platform stability.

## Current policy

The API reference does not publish request-rate numbers, and limits can vary
by environment, endpoint, and account. Do not hard-code a request rate. Contact
IBEE support when you need a confirmed quota for production.

The API reference documents one limit: creating a VM console session
(`POST /compute/console/sessions`) returns `429` when the number of active
sessions per user or per workspace is reached; `detail.code` is `user_limit`
or `workspace_limit`. Close sessions you no longer need, then retry.

## Handling rate limits

When the gateway returns `429 Too Many Requests`, wait before retrying. Honor a
`Retry-After` header when it is present; otherwise use exponential backoff with
jitter. Treat the error body as descriptive rather than parsing a fixed message.

**Best practices:**

* Add exponential backoff with jitter to retry logic.
* Cache responses when possible instead of re-fetching.
* Batch operations where the API supports it rather than making individual calls.

## Higher limits

If your integration needs higher rate limits, contact [IBEE support](https://ibee.ai/support).

title: SDKs
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/sdk-overview
description: Official Python and TypeScript SDKs for the IBEE Solutions API.
