# SDKs

> Official Python and TypeScript SDKs for the IBEE Solutions API.

Official client libraries for the IBEE Solutions API, version 0.5.0.

| SDK        | Install                | Requires                     |
| ---------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Python     | `pip install ibee`     | Python 3.10+                 |
| TypeScript | `npm install ibee-sdk` | Node 18+ or a modern browser |

Both SDKs are generated from the public API contract. Each API operation is one
method named after its `operationId`: `create_cloud_vm` in Python,
`createCloudVm` in TypeScript. The SDKs send your request as you write it and
return the server's answer unchanged. Prices, eligibility, limits and resource
states are decided by the API, not by the client.

## Configure

Create an API token in the portal under **Settings → API Tokens**. Pass the
token and workspace to the client, or set them in the environment:

| Setting     | Environment variable                                                    |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Token       | `IBEE_API_TOKEN` or `IBEE_TOKEN`                                        |
| Workspace   | `IBEE_WORKSPACE_ID` (a call can still pass its own `workspace_id`)      |
| Environment | `IBEE_ENV=dev` for the development API with an `ibee_dev_key_...` token |

The default is production, `https://api.ibee.ai/v1`.

## Python

```python
from ibee import Ibee

client = Ibee(token="ibee_prod_key_...", workspace_id="907479")  # or Ibee() to read the environment

sites = client.compute_catalog.list_compute_sites().sites
plans = client.compute_catalog.list_compute_plans(vm_type="cloud", site_id=sites[0].site_id).plans

operation = client.cloud_vms.create_cloud_vm(
    name="web-1",
    site_id=sites[0].site_id,
    plan_id=plans[0].plan_id,
    template_id="TEMPLATE_ID",
    billing_term="HOURLY",
)
status = client.cloud_vms.get_compute_operation(operation.operation_id)
print(status.status)  # accepted, running, ..., succeeded or failed
```

`AsyncIbee` has the same methods for `asyncio`. To use the development API, pass
`environment=IbeeEnvironment.DEVELOPMENT` (from `ibee`) or set `IBEE_ENV=dev`.
The full method list is in
[`reference.md`](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-python/blob/main/src/ibee/reference.md).

## TypeScript

```typescript
import { Ibee } from "ibee-sdk";

const ibee = new Ibee({ token: "ibee_prod_key_...", workspaceId: "907479" }); // or new Ibee() to read the environment

const { plans } = await ibee.computeCatalog.listComputePlans({ vm_type: "cloud", site_id: "SITE_ID" });
const plan = plans[0];

const operation = await ibee.cloudVms.createCloudVm({
  name: "web-1",
  site_id: "SITE_ID",
  plan_id: plan.plan_id,
  template_id: "TEMPLATE_ID",
  os_type: "linux",
  os_distro: "ubuntu",
  cpu: plan.cpu,
  ram_mb: plan.ram_mb,
  billing_term: "HOURLY",
});
const status = await ibee.cloudVms.getComputeOperation({ operation_id: operation.operation_id });
```

Methods take the request fields by their API names (`vm_id`, `site_id`,
`plan_id`). To use the development API, pass
`environment: IbeeEnvironment.Development` or set `IBEE_ENV=dev`. Add
`.withRawResponse()` to a call to read the response headers too.

## Errors

Every API error carries the HTTP status and the server's fields exactly as sent.
The SDKs add no wording of their own.

**`Python`**

```python title="Python"
from ibee.core.api_error import ApiError

try:
    client.cloud_vms.create_cloud_vm(name="web-1", plan_id="PLAN_ID", template_id="TEMPLATE_ID")
except ApiError as error:
    print(error.status_code)     # 402
    print(error.code)            # "billing_denied"
    print(error.billing_reason)  # "resource_limit_reached"
    print(error.message)         # the server's message, or None
    print(error.request_id)      # the x-request-id response header
```

**`TypeScript`**

```typescript title="TypeScript"
import { IbeeError } from "ibee-sdk";

try {
  await ibee.cloudVms.createCloudVm(request);
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof IbeeError) {
    console.error(err.statusCode, err.code, err.billingReason, err.serverMessage, err.requestId);
  }
  throw err;
}
```

Each status also has its own class, such as `PaymentRequiredError`,
`ForbiddenError`, `ConflictError` and `LockedError` (in `ibee.errors` for
Python). Branch on `status_code` and `code`, not on message text.

## Retries and idempotency

* Write operations that take an `X-Idempotency-Key` get a random key when you
  pass none. Pass your own `idempotency_key` to retry a write safely across
  processes.
* Reads are retried on 429 and 503 (Python also retries reads on 502 and 504).
  Writes are retried only when they carry an idempotency key, and only on 429
  and 503.
* VM creates are never retried, and neither is any answer that carries a billing
  or admission code.
* At most 2 retries by default, honouring `Retry-After`. Set `max_retries`
  (Python) or `maxRetries` (TypeScript) to change it; `0` turns retries off.

Until the API resolves VM billing SKUs itself, VM create still fills in the
plan's `billing_catalog` for `billing_term`, and VM delete releases an
auto-assigned public IP by default. These temporary behaviours are listed in
[`held.py`](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-python/blob/main/src/ibee/held.py)
and [`held.ts`](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-typescript/blob/main/src/wrapper/held.ts).

## Upgrading from 0.4

0.5.0 removes the client-side rule layers. Requests the SDKs used to check or
refuse are now sent, and the API answers them.

* **Removed:** client-side validation, billing preflights and estimators
  (`require_resource_eligibility`, `estimate_eligibility_cost_minor`,
  `billingBlockMessage`, ...), waiters (`wait_for_*`, `operations.wait`) and
  auto-pagers (`iter_*`, `list_all_*`, `listAll*`). Poll
  `get_compute_operation` instead of waiting.
* **Errors:** catch `ApiError` (Python, now in `ibee.core.api_error`) or
  `IbeeError` (TypeScript, was `ApiError`) and read `status_code`/`statusCode`
  and `code`. The per-reason error classes are gone.
* **Arguments:** `check_state`, `preflight_billing` and similar options are
  removed. `workspace_id` is optional once it is set on the client.
  `create_bucket` needs `region`.
* **TypeScript names:** methods use the `operationId` (`cloudVms.list` →
  `listCloudVms`, `computeCatalog.listSites` → `listComputeSites`,
  `operations.get` → `cloudVms.getComputeOperation`), request fields use API
  names, `IbeeEnvironment.PRODUCTION` → `Production`, and `timeoutMs` →
  `timeoutInSeconds`.

The full lists are in the
[Python CHANGELOG](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-python/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
and the
[TypeScript CHANGELOG](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-typescript/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

#### [Python SDK on GitHub](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-python)

#### [ibee on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/ibee/)

#### [TypeScript SDK on GitHub](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-typescript)

#### [ibee-sdk on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ibee-sdk)

See also the [CLI](/docs/api-reference/cli), the
[Terraform provider](/docs/api-reference/terraform) and the
[examples](/docs/api-reference/examples).

# CLI

> Manage compute, networking, storage, and secrets from your terminal.

The IBEE CLI (`ibee`), version 0.5.0, manages your cloud resources from the
terminal. It is built on the [Python SDK](/docs/api-reference/sdk-overview):
each command makes one API call and prints the server's answer.

## Install

```bash
pip install ibee-cli
```

Requires Python 3.10+. This installs the `ibee` command.

## Authenticate

Create an API token in the portal under **Settings → API Tokens**, then set:

```bash
export IBEE_TOKEN="ibee_prod_key_xxxxxxxxxxxx"   # or IBEE_API_TOKEN
export IBEE_WORKSPACE_ID="907479"
```

Both can also be passed per command with `--token` and `--workspace`.

## Quickstart

Find a site, plan, and image, then create a VM and wait for it:

```bash
ibee compute sites
ibee compute plans --vm-type cloud --site-id SITE_ID
ibee compute images --vm-type cloud --site-id SITE_ID

ibee vms create web-1 --site-id SITE_ID --plan-id PLAN_ID --template-id IMAGE_ID \
  --ssh-key-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub --wait
ibee vms list
ibee vms delete VM_ID --yes --wait
```

Asynchronous commands return an operation. Without `--wait`, wait for it later:

```bash
ibee ops wait OPERATION_ID
```

## Common commands

```bash
ibee vms get VM_ID
ibee vms stop VM_ID --wait
ibee gpus list
ibee buckets create my-bucket --region in-south-2
ibee buckets list
ibee block-storage list
ibee cdn list
ibee secrets stores list
ibee vpcs list
ibee reserved-ips list
ibee firewalls list
ibee load-balancers list
ibee billing eligibility --resource-type cpu_vm
```

`gpus` takes the same commands as `vms`. Run `ibee --help` or
`ibee GROUP --help` for every command and option. Commands that delete, detach,
or release ask for confirmation; add `--yes` to skip it.

## Global options

| Option              | Environment variable               | Description                                              |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--token`           | `IBEE_TOKEN` (or `IBEE_API_TOKEN`) | API token                                                |
| `--workspace`, `-w` | `IBEE_WORKSPACE_ID`                | Workspace ID                                             |
| `--dev`             | `IBEE_ENV=dev`                     | Use the development API with an `ibee_dev_key_...` token |
| `--base-url`        | `IBEE_BASE_URL`                    | Custom API endpoint                                      |
| `-o`, `--output`    | `IBEE_OUTPUT`                      | `table`, `json`, `yaml`, or `id`                         |
| `--json`            |                                    | Same as `-o json`                                        |
| `--yes`, `-y`       | `IBEE_ASSUME_YES=1`                | Answer yes to every confirmation                         |

```bash
ibee -o json buckets list | jq '.buckets[].name'
```

## Errors and exit codes

Every error prints the HTTP status and the server's fields as sent:

```text
Error: HTTP 402
  code: billing_denied
  reason: resource_limit_reached
  message: -
  request_id: 6f1c2e...
```

With `-o json` the same fields, plus the raw `body`, are printed on stderr as
`{"error": {...}}`.

| Exit code | Meaning                                                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 0         | Success                                                            |
| 1         | Failed operation, declined confirmation, or another error          |
| 2         | Usage or configuration error; nothing was sent                     |
| 3         | `--wait` reached `--timeout` while the operation was still running |
| 4         | Network error (no HTTP answer)                                     |
| 10–14     | HTTP 400, 401, 402, 403, 404                                       |
| 15–18     | HTTP 409, 422, 423, 429                                            |
| 19        | HTTP 5xx                                                           |

## Retries

Reads are retried on 429, 502, 503, and 504. Writes are retried only on 429
and 503, and only when they carry an idempotency key; an answer with a billing
or admission code is never retried. Write commands that take
`--idempotency-key KEY` send it unchanged; without one, a random key is sent.
After a retryable failure the CLI prints the key, so you can repeat the command
without doing the write twice.

## Upgrading from 0.4

* `--check-billing`, `--check-state`, `--preflight-billing`, and the other
  client-side check options are removed. The API answers what they checked.
* API errors exit with the codes above instead of `1`.
* `billing eligibility` takes options (`--sku-code`, `--resource-type`,
  `--quantity`, `--size-gb`) instead of a SKU argument.
* `buckets create` needs `--region`. Values the CLI used to fill in or refuse
  are now sent as given.
* `vpcs virtual-ips` and `block-storage attach-vm`/`detach-vm` are removed;
  use `vms volume-attach` and `vms volume-detach` for volumes.

See the [CLI CHANGELOG](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-cli/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for the full list.

## Related

* [Python SDK](/docs/api-reference/sdk-overview), the library the CLI is built on
* [Examples](/docs/api-reference/examples): a `cli.sh` for every product
* [`ibee-cli` on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/ibee-cli/) and [on GitHub](https://github.com/devs-ibee/ibee-cli)

# Terraform

> Install the IBEE Terraform provider, authenticate to a workspace, and manage infrastructure as code.

Use Terraform to describe IBEE infrastructure in configuration files and review
changes before applying them. The `devs-ibee/ibee` provider, version 0.5.0, is
published on the [Terraform Registry](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/devs-ibee/ibee/latest)
and covers compute, networking, storage, secrets, and CDN.

## Before you begin

* Install [Terraform](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/install) 1.11 or
  later (1.14 or later for Terraform actions).
* In the portal, open **Settings → API Tokens** and create a token for the
  workspace you want Terraform to manage, with the permissions your resources
  need. Add **Billing: Read** only if you use the `ibee_billing_eligibility`
  data source. See [API Tokens](/docs/tools/api-tokens).

## Get started

### 1. Set your credentials

```bash
export IBEE_TOKEN="ibee_prod_key_xxxxxxxxxxxx"
export IBEE_WORKSPACE_ID="907479"
```

Production is the default. Set `IBEE_ENV=dev` with a development token to use
the development API. Keep the token out of Terraform files and source control.

### 2. Write a configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in a new directory:

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11.0"
  required_providers {
    ibee = {
      source  = "devs-ibee/ibee"
      version = "~> 0.5.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "ibee" {}

variable "site_id" {
  description = "An available network site ID"
  type        = string
}

resource "ibee_vpc" "example" {
  name    = "terraform-example"
  site_id = var.site_id
}

output "vpc_id" {
  value = ibee_vpc.example.id
}
```

Find site IDs in the portal or with the
[`ibee_network_sites`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/devs-ibee/ibee/latest/docs/data-sources/network_sites)
data source.

### 3. Initialize, plan, and apply

```bash
terraform init
terraform plan -var="site_id=SITE_ID"
terraform apply -var="site_id=SITE_ID"
```

Some resources incur charges. Review every plan before you apply it.

### 4. Clean up

```bash
terraform destroy -var="site_id=SITE_ID"
```

## Errors and retries

The provider calls the API and relays its answer. A failed request shows the
HTTP status, the server's code and message, and the request ID. Reads are
retried on 429, 502, 503, and 504; writes only on 429 and 503, and never when
the answer carries a billing or admission code.

## Upgrading from 0.4

* `ibee_cloud_vm`, `ibee_gpu_vm`: `billing_interval` no longer defaults to
  `HOURLY`. Set it for new VMs. Changing `plan_id` now resizes the VM in place
  instead of replacing it, and changing `ssh_key_ids` updates access in place.
* `ibee_compute_plans`: `currency` and `billing_interval` no longer default to
  `INR` and `HOURLY`.
* `ibee_secret_store`: `force_archive` is removed. Remove it from your
  configuration.
* `ibee_block_volume`: shrinking `size_gb` no longer replaces the volume; the
  API's answer is shown.
* Provider-side checks (plan selectable and priced, VM power states, billing
  catalog rules) are removed. The API decides.

See the [provider CHANGELOG](https://github.com/devs-ibee/terraform-provider-ibee/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for details.

## Next steps

* [Provider documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/devs-ibee/ibee/latest/docs) on the Terraform Registry
* [Terraform examples](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/terraform): a web app, a private network, a static site, and storage with secrets
* [Provider source](https://github.com/devs-ibee/terraform-provider-ibee) on GitHub

# Examples

> Short, runnable examples for IBEE products with the Python SDK, TypeScript SDK, CLI, and Terraform provider.

The [IBEE examples repository](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples) has short,
runnable examples for the 0.5.0 clients. Each one does one task, usually create a
resource, read it, and delete it, with a `main.py`, an `index.ts`, and a
`cli.sh`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples.git
cd examples
pip install ibee ibee-cli boto3
npm install
export IBEE_TOKEN="ibee_prod_key_..."
export IBEE_WORKSPACE_ID="<workspace-id>"

python3 getting-started/main.py   # lists the site, plan, and image IDs the other examples use
npx tsx cloud-vms/index.ts
bash cloud-vms/cli.sh

## Compute

#### [Getting started](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/getting-started)

Check your token and list sites, plans, and images. Nothing is created.

#### [Cloud VMs](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/cloud-vms)

Create a VM, wait for it, read it, and delete it.

#### [GPU VMs](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/gpu-vms)

Create, read, and delete a GPU VM.

#### [VM operations](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/vm-operations)

Metrics, events, and moving a VM to another plan.

#### [Snapshots and backups](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/snapshots-and-backups)

Snapshot a VM's root disk, list snapshots and backup runs.

## Storage

#### [Object Storage](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/object-storage)

A private bucket, a bucket-scoped S3 key, and boto3.

#### [Block Storage](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/block-storage)

Create, attach, detach, and delete a volume.

#### [Container Registry](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/container-registry)

Build, push, and pull an image with Docker.

## Networking and security

#### [VPC](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/vpc)

A private network with a subnet and an attached VM.

#### [Reserved IPs](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/reserved-ips)

Reserve, attach, detach, and release a public IP.

#### [Firewalls](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/firewalls)

A firewall group for HTTP and HTTPS attached to a VM.

#### [Load Balancers](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/load-balancers)

An L7 HTTP load balancer in front of two VMs.

#### [CDN](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/cdn)

Serve a public bucket with single-page-app routing and a cache purge.

#### [Secret Manager](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/secret-manager)

A store and a versioned secret.

## Terraform

#### [Terraform provider](/docs/api-reference/terraform)

Install the provider from the Registry and create a VPC.

#### [Terraform examples](https://github.com/devs-ibee/examples/tree/main/terraform)

A load-balanced web app, a private network, a static site on the CDN, and storage with secrets.

# List secret stores

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores

Lists secret stores in a workspace. Requires scope: secret-store.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/list-secret-stores

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `page` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Page number.
- `limit` (integer, optional, default: 50) — Maximum number of records to return.
- `include_archived` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Include archived stores in the result.

## Response

### 200

Stores returned successfully.

- `stores` (list of SecretStore, optional) — Stores on this page.
- `total` (integer, optional) — Total number of items matching the request.
- `page` (integer, optional) — Page number returned (1-based).
- `limit` (integer, optional) — Page size that was applied.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### SecretStore

A secret store: a named container for secrets inside a workspace.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique ID of the store.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, optional) — Display name of the store.
- `store_key` (string, optional) — URL-safe slug derived from the store name.
- `description` (string, optional) — Description of the store.
- `status` (enum, optional) — - `active`: in use. - `archived`: archived; can be unarchived. - `deleting`: permanent deletion in progress.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `archived`, `deleting`
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was last changed (ISO 8601).

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Create secret store

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a secret store in a workspace. Requires scope: secret-store.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "production-secrets"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/create-secret-store

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateSecretStoreRequest.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the store (1-128 characters). Its URL-safe form becomes `store_key`.
- `description` (string, optional) — Optional description.

## Response

### 201

Store created successfully.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique ID of the store.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, optional) — Display name of the store.
- `store_key` (string, optional) — URL-safe slug derived from the store name.
- `description` (string, optional) — Description of the store.
- `status` (enum, optional) — - `active`: in use. - `archived`: archived; can be unarchived. - `deleting`: permanent deletion in progress.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `archived`, `deleting`
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was last changed (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 402 Payment Required Error

Billing refused the request (`billing_denied`). `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason unchanged, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` (a plan limit) or `resource_usage_unavailable` (Billing could not count usage). `billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` identify the decision. Nothing is provisioned; resolve the reason and retry with the same idempotency key where supported.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.

### 423 Locked Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. # Get secret store

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/{store_id}

Gets one secret store. Requires scope: secret-store.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# STORE_ID: Secret store ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/$STORE_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/get-secret-store

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `store_id` (string, required) — Secret store ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Store returned successfully.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique ID of the store.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, optional) — Display name of the store.
- `store_key` (string, optional) — URL-safe slug derived from the store name.
- `description` (string, optional) — Description of the store.
- `status` (enum, optional) — - `active`: in use. - `archived`: archived; can be unarchived. - `deleting`: permanent deletion in progress.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `archived`, `deleting`
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was last changed (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. # Update secret store

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/{store_id}
Content-Type: application/json

Updates store name or description. Requires scope: secret-store.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# STORE_ID: Secret store ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/$STORE_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "production-secrets", "description": "Updated description"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/update-secret-store

- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

let headers = [

# Archive secret store

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/{store_id}/archive

Archives a secret store. Requires scope: secret-store.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# STORE_ID: Secret store ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/$STORE_ID/archive?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/archive-secret-store

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `store_id` (string, required) — Secret store ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Store archived successfully.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique ID of the store.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, optional) — Display name of the store.
- `store_key` (string, optional) — URL-safe slug derived from the store name.
- `description` (string, optional) — Description of the store.
- `status` (enum, optional) — - `active`: in use. - `archived`: archived; can be unarchived. - `deleting`: permanent deletion in progress.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `archived`, `deleting`
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was last changed (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 423 Locked Error

The organization is suspended (`organization_suspended`), so writes are refused.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

# Permanently delete secret store

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/{store_id}/permanent

Irreversibly deletes a store and all store-scoped secrets, versions, identities, and policies. Requires scope: secret-store.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# STORE_ID: Secret store ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/$STORE_ID/permanent?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/permanently-delete-secret-store

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `store_id` (string, required) — Secret store ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Store and its resources permanently deleted.

- `status` (enum, required) — - `destroyed`: the versions' data was irreversibly destroyed. - `permanently_deleted`: the secret and all its versions were removed.
  - Allowed values: `destroyed`, `permanently_deleted`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. # List secrets

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/{store_id}/secrets

Lists secret metadata in a store. Secret values are not returned. Requires scope: secret-store.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# STORE_ID: Secret store ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/$STORE_ID/secrets?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### Secret

A secret's metadata. Values are returned by the value endpoints only.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique ID of the secret.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `store_id` (string, optional) — ID of the store that holds the secret.
- `store_key` (string, optional) — URL-safe key of that store.
- `secret_name` (string, optional) — Name of the secret within the store.
- `status` (enum, optional) — - `active`: readable. - `soft_deleted`: deleted but recoverable until permanently deleted.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `soft_deleted`
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was last changed (ISO 8601).

title: Create secret

# Create secret

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/{store_id}/secrets
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a secret in a store. Requires scope: secret-store.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# STORE_ID: Secret store ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/$STORE_ID/secrets?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"secret_name": "database-url", "value": {"url": "postgres://user:pass@host:5432/mydb"}}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/create-secret

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `store_id` (string, required) — Secret store ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateSecretRequest.

- `secret_name` (string, required) — Unique name for the secret within the store. Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens only.
- `value` (map from string to any, required) — Key-value pairs containing the secret data.

## Response

### 201

Secret created successfully.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique ID of the secret.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `store_id` (string, optional) — ID of the store that holds the secret.
- `store_key` (string, optional) — URL-safe key of that store.
- `secret_name` (string, optional) — Name of the secret within the store.
- `status` (enum, optional) — - `active`: readable. - `soft_deleted`: deleted but recoverable until permanently deleted.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `soft_deleted`
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was last changed (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 402 Payment Required Error

Billing refused the request (`billing_denied`). `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason unchanged, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` (a plan limit) or `resource_usage_unavailable` (Billing could not count usage). `billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` identify the decision. Nothing is provisioned; resolve the reason and retry with the same idempotency key where supported.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

### 423 Locked Error

# Batch-create secrets

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/{store_id}/secrets:batchIngest
Content-Type: application/json

Creates up to 500 secrets without overwriting existing names. Requires scope: secret-store.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# STORE_ID: Secret store ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/stores/$STORE_ID/secrets:batchIngest?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"secrets": [{"secret_name": "<secret_name>", "value": {}}]}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/secret-store/batch-create-secrets

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `store_id` (string, required) — Secret store ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a BatchCreateSecretsRequest.

- `secrets` (list of BatchCreateSecretItem, required) — Secrets to create (1-500).

## Response

### 200

Batch processed; inspect each result for created, skipped, or failed status.

- `results` (list of BatchCreateSecretResult, required) — One result per requested secret, in request order.
- `created_count` (integer, required) — Number of secrets created.
- `skipped_count` (integer, required) — Number of secrets skipped because they already existed.
- `failed_count` (integer, required) — Number of secrets that failed to create.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. - `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. ## Types

### BatchCreateSecretItem

One secret in a batch create.

- `secret_name` (string, required) — Unique name for the secret within the store (2-64 characters).
- `value` (map from string to any, required) — Key-value pairs containing the secret data.

### BatchCreateSecretResult

Outcome for one secret in a batch create.

- `secret_name` (string, required) — Name of the secret the result refers to.
- `status` (enum, required) — - `created`: the secret was created. - `skipped`: a secret with this name already existed. - `failed`: creation failed; see `error`.
  - Allowed values: `created`, `skipped`, `failed`
- `secret` (Secret, optional, nullable) — The created secret, when `status` is `created`.
- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `failed`.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### Secret

A secret's metadata. Values are returned by the value endpoints only.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique ID of the secret.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `store_id` (string, optional) — ID of the store that holds the secret.
- `store_key` (string, optional) — URL-safe key of that store.
- `secret_name` (string, optional) — Name of the secret within the store.
- `status` (enum, optional) — - `active`: readable. - `soft_deleted`: deleted but recoverable until permanently deleted.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `soft_deleted`
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional) — When the record was last changed (ISO 8601).

# Get secret metadata

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/secrets/{secret_id}

Gets one secret metadata record. Secret value is not returned. Requires scope: secret-store.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# SECRET_ID: Secret ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/secret-store/secrets/$SECRET_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```

- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.
