# Attach a node to a VPC

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nodes
Content-Type: application/json

Attaches a VM to a VPC subnet so it can reach other VMs on the private network, optionally with a reserved public IP. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nodes?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"vm_id": "<vm_id>", "subnet_id": "<subnet_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/attach-vpc-node

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an AttachVpcNodeRequest.

- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM to attach.
- `subnet_id` (string, required) — Subnet of the VPC to attach the VM to.
- `connectivity` (enum, optional, default: private) — How the VM reaches the internet from this subnet. - `private`: no internet path. - `public_ip`: a Reserved IP is attached to the allocation. - `nat`: outbound traffic goes through the VPC's NAT gateway. Default `private`.
  - Allowed values: `private`, `public_ip`, `nat`
- `reserved_public_ip_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Reserved IP to attach to the VM. Only valid with `public_ip` connectivity.

## Response

### 201

Node attached successfully.

- `allocation_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the attachment.
- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC the VM is attached to.
- `subnet_id` (string, required) — Subnet the VM is attached to.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the attached VM.
- `connectivity` (enum, required) — How the VM reaches the internet from this subnet. - `private`: no internet path. - `public_ip`: a Reserved IP is attached to the allocation. - `nat`: outbound traffic goes through the VPC's NAT gateway.
  - Allowed values: `private`, `public_ip`, `nat`
- `private_ip` (string, required) — Private IPv4 address assigned to the VM.
- `prefix_length` (integer, required) — Prefix length of the subnet.
- `subnet_mask` (string, required) — Subnet mask in dotted-decimal form.
- `gateway` (string, required) — Gateway IPv4 address of the subnet.
- `dns` (list of string, required) — DNS resolvers handed to the VM.
- `status` (string, required) — Attachment state: `reserved`, `attaching`, `attached`, `moving`, `detaching` or `releasing`.
- `public_ip_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Reserved IP attached to the allocation, when `connectivity` is `public_ip`.
- `public_ip` (string, optional, nullable) — Address of that Reserved IP.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, optional, nullable) — NAT gateway used, when `connectivity` is `nat`.
- `nat_public_ip` (string, optional, nullable) — Public address of that NAT gateway.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.

- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 423 Locked Error

The organization is suspended (`organization_suspended`), so writes are refused.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. - `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. # List NAT gateways

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nat-gateways

Lists the managed NAT gateways in a VPC. Requires scope: network.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nat-gateways?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/list-nat-gateways

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

NAT gateways returned successfully.

- `list of NatGateway`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### NatGateway

A managed NAT gateway that gives a VPC's VMs outbound internet access through one public address.

- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the gateway.
- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC the gateway serves.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site the gateway lives at.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the gateway.
- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — ID of the public IP the gateway uses.
- `public_ip` (string, required) — Public IPv4 address of the gateway.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a VPC, subnet, NAT gateway or port-forwarding rule. - `provisioning`: being created. - `available`: ready for use. - `error`: the last change failed; see `error_message`. - `deleting`: being removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `available`, `error`, `deleting`
- `subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet the gateway is placed in.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `pricing` (NatPricing, optional) — Price of a NAT gateway as recorded when it was created.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `error`.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### NatPricing

Price of a NAT gateway as recorded when it was created.

- `currency` (string, optional, default: USD) — ISO 4217 code of the currency the prices are in.
- `price_per_hour` (double, optional, default: 0) — Hourly charge for the gateway.
- `data_price_per_gb` (double, optional, default: 0) — Charge per GB of data processed.
- `billing_enforced` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Whether these charges are being applied.

# Create a NAT gateway

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nat-gateways
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a managed NAT gateway that gives VMs in a VPC outbound internet access without public IPs of their own. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nat-gateways?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"subnet_id": "<subnet_id>", "reserved_public_ip_id": "<reserved_public_ip_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/create-nat-gateway

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateNatGatewayRequest.

- `subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet the gateway is placed in; chosen by the service when omitted.
- `reserved_public_ip_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Reserved IP to use as the gateway's public address; a platform-assigned address is used when omitted.
- `name` (string, optional, default: NAT Gateway) — Display name of the gateway. Default `NAT Gateway`.

## Response

### 201

NAT gateway created successfully.

- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the gateway.
- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC the gateway serves.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site the gateway lives at.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the gateway.
- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — ID of the public IP the gateway uses.
- `public_ip` (string, required) — Public IPv4 address of the gateway.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a VPC, subnet, NAT gateway or port-forwarding rule. - `provisioning`: being created. - `available`: ready for use. - `error`: the last change failed; see `error_message`. - `deleting`: being removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `available`, `error`, `deleting`
- `subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet the gateway is placed in.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `pricing` (NatPricing, optional) — Price of a NAT gateway as recorded when it was created.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `error`.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 402 Payment Required Error

Billing refused the request (`billing_denied`). `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason unchanged, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` (a plan limit) or `resource_usage_unavailable` (Billing could not count usage). `billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` identify the decision. Nothing is provisioned; resolve the reason and retry with the same idempotency key where supported.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. ### 503 Service Unavailable Error

## Types

### NatPricing

Price of a NAT gateway as recorded when it was created.

- `currency` (string, optional, default: USD) — ISO 4217 code of the currency the prices are in.
- `price_per_hour` (double, optional, default: 0) — Hourly charge for the gateway.
- `data_price_per_gb` (double, optional, default: 0) — Charge per GB of data processed.
- `billing_enforced` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Whether these charges are being applied.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

```swift
  if (error != nil) {
    print(error as Any)
  } else {
    let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse
    print(httpResponse)
  }
})

dataTask.resume()
```

title: Delete a NAT gateway

# Delete a NAT gateway

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nat-gateways/{nat_gateway_id}

Deletes a NAT gateway from a VPC. VMs that relied on it lose outbound internet access. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
# NAT_GATEWAY_ID: NAT gateway ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nat-gateways/$NAT_GATEWAY_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/delete-nat-gateway

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 204

NAT gateway deleted successfully.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.

# List NAT port-forwarding rules

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nat-gateways/{nat_gateway_id}/port-forwarding-rules

Lists the port-forwarding rules on a NAT gateway. Requires scope: network.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
# NAT_GATEWAY_ID: NAT gateway ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nat-gateways/$NAT_GATEWAY_ID/port-forwarding-rules?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/list-nat-port-forwarding-rules

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Port-forwarding rules returned successfully.

- `list of NatPortForwardingRule`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. ### 503 Service Unavailable Error

Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. ## Types

### NatPortForwardingRule

A port-forwarding rule on a NAT gateway.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the rule.
- `external_port` (integer, required) — Port on the gateway's public address (1-65535).
- `internal_ip` (string, required) — Private IPv4 address of the VM inside the VPC that receives the traffic.
- `internal_port` (integer, required) — Port on the VM that receives the traffic (1-65535).
- `port_forward_rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC the rule belongs to.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway the rule is configured on.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a VPC, subnet, NAT gateway or port-forwarding rule. - `provisioning`: being created. - `available`: ready for use. - `error`: the last change failed; see `error_message`. - `deleting`: being removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `available`, `error`, `deleting`
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `protocol` (enum, optional, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp`
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`
- `note` (string, optional, default: ) — Free-text note stored with the rule. Default empty.
- `enabled` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Whether the rule is applied. Default true.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `site_id` (string, optional) — Site the gateway lives at.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `error`.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Create a NAT port-forwarding rule

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nat-gateways/{nat_gateway_id}/port-forwarding-rules
Content-Type: application/json

Adds a port-forwarding rule that sends traffic arriving on a NAT gateway port to a private IP and port inside the VPC. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
# NAT_GATEWAY_ID: NAT gateway ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nat-gateways/$NAT_GATEWAY_ID/port-forwarding-rules?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>", "external_port": 1, "internal_ip": "<internal_ip>", "internal_port": 1}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/create-nat-port-forwarding-rule

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateNatPortForwardingRuleRequest.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the rule.
- `external_port` (integer, required) — Port on the gateway's public address (1-65535).
- `internal_ip` (string, required) — Private IPv4 address of the VM inside the VPC that receives the traffic.
- `internal_port` (integer, required) — Port on the VM that receives the traffic (1-65535).
- `protocol` (enum, optional, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp`
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`
- `note` (string, optional, default: ) — Free-text note stored with the rule. Default empty.
- `enabled` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Whether the rule is applied. Default true.

## Response

### 201

Port-forwarding rule created successfully.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the rule.
- `external_port` (integer, required) — Port on the gateway's public address (1-65535).
- `internal_ip` (string, required) — Private IPv4 address of the VM inside the VPC that receives the traffic.
- `internal_port` (integer, required) — Port on the VM that receives the traffic (1-65535).
- `port_forward_rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC the rule belongs to.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway the rule is configured on.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a VPC, subnet, NAT gateway or port-forwarding rule. - `provisioning`: being created. - `available`: ready for use. - `error`: the last change failed; see `error_message`. - `deleting`: being removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `available`, `error`, `deleting`
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `protocol` (enum, optional, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp`
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`
- `note` (string, optional, default: ) — Free-text note stored with the rule. Default empty.
- `enabled` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Whether the rule is applied. Default true.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `site_id` (string, optional) — Site the gateway lives at.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `error`.

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.

- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.

# Delete a NAT port-forwarding rule

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nat-gateways/{nat_gateway_id}/port-forwarding-rules/{port_forwarding_rule_id}

Removes a port-forwarding rule from a NAT gateway. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
# NAT_GATEWAY_ID: NAT gateway ID
# PORT_FORWARDING_RULE_ID: NAT port-forwarding rule ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nat-gateways/$NAT_GATEWAY_ID/port-forwarding-rules/$PORT_FORWARDING_RULE_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/delete-nat-port-forwarding-rule

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway ID.
- `port_forwarding_rule_id` (string, required) — NAT port-forwarding rule ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 204

Port-forwarding rule deleted successfully.

# Update a NAT port-forwarding rule

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/{vpc_id}/nat-gateways/{nat_gateway_id}/port-forwarding-rules/{port_forwarding_rule_id}
Content-Type: application/json

Changes a NAT port-forwarding rule's ports, target, protocol, or enabled state. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VPC_ID: VPC ID
# NAT_GATEWAY_ID: NAT gateway ID
# PORT_FORWARDING_RULE_ID: NAT port-forwarding rule ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/vpcs/$VPC_ID/nat-gateways/$NAT_GATEWAY_ID/port-forwarding-rules/$PORT_FORWARDING_RULE_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>", "protocol": "tcp"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/vpcs/update-nat-port-forwarding-rule

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC ID.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway ID.
- `port_forwarding_rule_id` (string, required) — NAT port-forwarding rule ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an UpdateNatPortForwardingRuleRequest.

- `name` (string, optional) — Display name of the rule.
- `protocol` (enum, optional) — - `tcp` - `udp`
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`
- `external_port` (integer, optional) — Port on the gateway's public address (1-65535).
- `internal_ip` (string, optional) — Private IPv4 address of the VM inside the VPC that receives the traffic.
- `internal_port` (integer, optional) — Port on the VM that receives the traffic (1-65535).
- `note` (string, optional) — Free-text note stored with the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, optional) — Whether the rule is applied.

## Response

### 200

Port-forwarding rule updated successfully.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the rule.
- `external_port` (integer, required) — Port on the gateway's public address (1-65535).
- `internal_ip` (string, required) — Private IPv4 address of the VM inside the VPC that receives the traffic.
- `internal_port` (integer, required) — Port on the VM that receives the traffic (1-65535).
- `port_forward_rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `vpc_id` (string, required) — VPC the rule belongs to.
- `nat_gateway_id` (string, required) — NAT gateway the rule is configured on.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a VPC, subnet, NAT gateway or port-forwarding rule. - `provisioning`: being created. - `available`: ready for use. - `error`: the last change failed; see `error_message`. - `deleting`: being removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `available`, `error`, `deleting`
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `protocol` (enum, optional, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp`
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`
- `note` (string, optional, default: ) — Free-text note stored with the rule. Default empty.
- `enabled` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Whether the rule is applied. Default true.
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `site_id` (string, optional) — Site the gateway lives at.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `error`.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

```json
}
```

# List Reserved IPs

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips

Lists customer-reserved public IP addresses. Requires scope: network.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/list-reserved-ips

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `site_id` (string, optional) — Optional exact site filter. Copy `site_id` from `GET /networking/sites`.

## Response

### 200

Reserved IPs returned successfully.

- `list of ReservedIp`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

## Types

### ReservedIp

A portable public IPv4 address reserved by the workspace. It stays allocated until released and can be moved between VMs.

- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the Reserved IP.
- `address` (string, required) — The IPv4 address.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site whose pool the address comes from.
- `status` (string, required) — `reserved` when not attached, `attached` when in use, `releasing` while being released.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `label` (string, optional) — Label shown as the address's name in the portal.
- `reverse_dns` (string, optional) — Reverse DNS hostname set on the address; empty when none.
- `reservation_type` (enum, optional, nullable) — - `user_reserved`: a Reserved IP created by the customer. - `platform_assigned`: an address IBEE assigned to an instance or service. Null on legacy records whose classification the service infers.
  - Allowed values: `user_reserved`, `platform_assigned`
- `attached_resource_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of resource the address is attached to, for example `vm` or `nat_gateway`; null when not attached.
- `attached_resource_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of that resource; null when not attached.
- `attached_vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.
- `attached_subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Reserve a public IP

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips
Content-Type: application/json

Reserves an address from a site's public IP pool. Discover an available site with `GET /networking/sites`. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"site_id": "68b99bd78a8eda32ff3f16ea"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/reserve-ip

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a ReserveIpRequest.

- `site_id` (string, required) — Site whose public IP pool allocates the address. Copy an available `site_id` from `GET /networking/sites`; use the target VM or VPC's site when the address will be attached.
- `label` (string, optional, default: ) — Optional label for the address (up to 120 characters), shown as its name in the portal.

## Response

### 201

Public IP reserved successfully.

- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the Reserved IP.
- `address` (string, required) — The IPv4 address.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site whose pool the address comes from.
- `status` (string, required) — `reserved` when not attached, `attached` when in use, `releasing` while being released.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `label` (string, optional) — Label shown as the address's name in the portal.
- `reverse_dns` (string, optional) — Reverse DNS hostname set on the address; empty when none.
- `reservation_type` (enum, optional, nullable) — - `user_reserved`: a Reserved IP created by the customer. - `platform_assigned`: an address IBEE assigned to an instance or service. Null on legacy records whose classification the service infers.
  - Allowed values: `user_reserved`, `platform_assigned`
- `attached_resource_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of resource the address is attached to, for example `vm` or `nat_gateway`; null when not attached.
- `attached_resource_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of that resource; null when not attached.
- `attached_vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.
- `attached_subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

### 402 Payment Required Error

Billing refused the request (`billing_denied`). `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason unchanged, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` (a plan limit) or `resource_usage_unavailable` (Billing could not count usage). `billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` identify the decision. Nothing is provisioned; resolve the reason and retry with the same idempotency key where supported.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. # Get a Reserved IP

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/{reserved_ip_id}

Returns a reserved public IPv4 address, including its label, reverse DNS, and the VM it is attached to. Requires scope: network.read.


# Release a Reserved IP

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/{reserved_ip_id}

Releases a reserved public IPv4 address from your workspace. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# RESERVED_IP_ID: Reserved IP ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/$RESERVED_IP_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/release-reserved-ip

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `reserved_ip_id` (string, required) — Reserved IP ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 204

Reserved IP released successfully.

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

# Update a Reserved IP

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/{reserved_ip_id}
Content-Type: application/json

Changes a reserved IP's label or reverse DNS (PTR) record. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# RESERVED_IP_ID: Reserved IP ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/$RESERVED_IP_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"label": "<label>", "reverse_dns": "<reverse_dns>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/update-reserved-ip

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `reserved_ip_id` (string, required) — Reserved IP ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an UpdateReservedIpRequest.

- `label` (string, optional) — New label (the portal's **Name**).
- `reverse_dns` (string, optional) — Reverse DNS hostname for the address, as a fully qualified domain name.

## Response

### 200

Reserved IP updated successfully.

- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the Reserved IP.
- `address` (string, required) — The IPv4 address.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site whose pool the address comes from.
- `status` (string, required) — `reserved` when not attached, `attached` when in use, `releasing` while being released.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `label` (string, optional) — Label shown as the address's name in the portal.
- `reverse_dns` (string, optional) — Reverse DNS hostname set on the address; empty when none.
- `reservation_type` (enum, optional, nullable) — - `user_reserved`: a Reserved IP created by the customer. - `platform_assigned`: an address IBEE assigned to an instance or service. Null on legacy records whose classification the service infers.
  - Allowed values: `user_reserved`, `platform_assigned`
- `attached_resource_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of resource the address is attached to, for example `vm` or `nat_gateway`; null when not attached.
- `attached_resource_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of that resource; null when not attached.
- `attached_vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.
- `attached_subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

---
title: Attach a Reserved IP
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/attach-reserved-ip
---

# Attach a Reserved IP

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/{reserved_ip_id}/attach
Content-Type: application/json

Attaches a reserved public IP to a VM, optionally through a VPC subnet. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# RESERVED_IP_ID: Reserved IP ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/$RESERVED_IP_ID/attach?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"vm_id": "<vm_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/attach-reserved-ip

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `reserved_ip_id` (string, required) — Reserved IP ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an AttachReservedIpRequest.

- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM to attach the address to.
- `vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the VM when attaching inside a VPC. Send together with `subnet_id`.
- `subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the VM's VPC attachment. Send together with `vpc_id`.

## Response

### 200

Reserved IP attached successfully.

- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the Reserved IP.
- `address` (string, required) — The IPv4 address.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site whose pool the address comes from.
- `status` (string, required) — `reserved` when not attached, `attached` when in use, `releasing` while being released.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `label` (string, optional) — Label shown as the address's name in the portal.
- `reverse_dns` (string, optional) — Reverse DNS hostname set on the address; empty when none.
- `reservation_type` (enum, optional, nullable) — - `user_reserved`: a Reserved IP created by the customer. - `platform_assigned`: an address IBEE assigned to an instance or service. Null on legacy records whose classification the service infers.
  - Allowed values: `user_reserved`, `platform_assigned`
- `attached_resource_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of resource the address is attached to, for example `vm` or `nat_gateway`; null when not attached.
- `attached_resource_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of that resource; null when not attached.
- `attached_vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.
- `attached_subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.

Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"net/http"
	"io"
)

func main() {

	url := "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/reserved_ip_123/attach?workspace_id=710995"

	payload := strings.NewReader("{\n  \"vm_id\": \"<vm_id>\"\n}")

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, payload)

	req.Header.Add("Authorization", "Bearer <token>")
	req.Header.Add("Content-Type", "application/json")

	res, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(res.Body)

	fmt.Println(res)
	fmt.Println(string(body))

}
```

```swift
import Foundation

let headers = [
  "Authorization": "Bearer <token>",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
]
let parameters = ["vm_id": "<vm_id>"] as [String : Any]

let postData = JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: parameters, options: [])

let request = NSMutableURLRequest(url: NSURL(string: "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/reserved_ip_123/attach?workspace_id=710995")! as URL,
                                        cachePolicy: .useProtocolCachePolicy,
                                    timeoutInterval: 10.0)
request.httpMethod = "POST"
request.allHTTPHeaderFields = headers
request.httpBody = postData as Data

let session = URLSession.shared
let dataTask = session.dataTask(with: request as URLRequest, completionHandler: { (data, response, error) -> Void in
  if (error != nil) {
    print(error as Any)
  } else {
    let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse
    print(httpResponse)
  }
})

dataTask.resume()
```

# Detach a Reserved IP

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/{reserved_ip_id}/detach

Detaches a reserved public IP from its VM. The address stays reserved in your workspace. Requires scope: network.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# RESERVED_IP_ID: Reserved IP ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/$RESERVED_IP_ID/detach?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/detach-reserved-ip

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `reserved_ip_id` (string, required) — Reserved IP ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Reserved IP detached successfully.

- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the Reserved IP.
- `address` (string, required) — The IPv4 address.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site whose pool the address comes from.
- `status` (string, required) — `reserved` when not attached, `attached` when in use, `releasing` while being released.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `label` (string, optional) — Label shown as the address's name in the portal.
- `reverse_dns` (string, optional) — Reverse DNS hostname set on the address; empty when none.
- `reservation_type` (enum, optional, nullable) — - `user_reserved`: a Reserved IP created by the customer. - `platform_assigned`: an address IBEE assigned to an instance or service. Null on legacy records whose classification the service infers.
  - Allowed values: `user_reserved`, `platform_assigned`
- `attached_resource_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of resource the address is attached to, for example `vm` or `nat_gateway`; null when not attached.
- `attached_resource_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of that resource; null when not attached.
- `attached_vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.
- `attached_subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 423 Locked Error

The organization is suspended (`organization_suspended`), so writes are refused.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.
