# Move a Reserved IP

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/{reserved_ip_id}/move
Content-Type: application/json

Atomically moves a Reserved IP to another VM attachment.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# RESERVED_IP_ID: Reserved IP ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/reserved-ips/$RESERVED_IP_ID/move?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"vm_id": "<vm_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/reserved-ips/move-reserved-ip

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `reserved_ip_id` (string, required) — Reserved IP ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an AttachReservedIpRequest.

- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM to attach the address to.
- `vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the VM when attaching inside a VPC. Send together with `subnet_id`.
- `subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the VM's VPC attachment. Send together with `vpc_id`.

## Response

### 200

Reserved IP moved successfully.

- `public_ip_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the Reserved IP.
- `address` (string, required) — The IPv4 address.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Site whose pool the address comes from.
- `status` (string, required) — `reserved` when not attached, `attached` when in use, `releasing` while being released.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `organization_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, optional) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `label` (string, optional) — Label shown as the address's name in the portal.
- `reverse_dns` (string, optional) — Reverse DNS hostname set on the address; empty when none.
- `reservation_type` (enum, optional, nullable) — - `user_reserved`: a Reserved IP created by the customer. - `platform_assigned`: an address IBEE assigned to an instance or service. Null on legacy records whose classification the service infers.
  - Allowed values: `user_reserved`, `platform_assigned`
- `attached_resource_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of resource the address is attached to, for example `vm` or `nat_gateway`; null when not attached.
- `attached_resource_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of that resource; null when not attached.
- `attached_vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.
- `attached_subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of the attachment, when the address is attached inside a VPC.

# List firewall groups

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups

Lists one page of the firewall groups in a workspace: 10 by default, at most 100 per page. Use `limit` and `offset` to page through the rest. Requires scope: firewall.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/list-firewall-groups

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `limit` (integer, optional, default: 10) — Maximum number of records to return. The server returns 10 when this is omitted; use `offset` to read further pages.
- `offset` (integer, optional, default: 0) — Number of records to skip before the first one returned.

## Response

### 200

Firewall groups returned successfully.

- `list of FirewallGroup`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### FirewallGroup

A stateful firewall group: a named set of rules applied to the VMs attached to it.

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the group.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `is_default` (boolean, required) — Whether this is the workspace's default group.
- `status` (string, required) — Status of the group; `active` when usable.
- `rules` (list of FirewallRule, required) — Rules in the group.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description of the group.
- `linked_instance_count` (integer, optional) — Number of VMs the group is attached to.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### FirewallRule

A rule in a firewall group.

- `direction` (enum, required, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, required, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `action` (enum, required, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, required) — Whether the rule is applied.
- `system_managed` (boolean, required) — True for rules the platform manages.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.

# Create a firewall group

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a firewall group, a reusable set of inbound and outbound rules you can apply to VMs. Requires scope: firewall.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/create-firewall-group

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateFirewallGroupRequest.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description.
- `is_default` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Mark the group as the workspace's default group. Default false.

## Response

### 201

Firewall group created successfully.

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the group.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `is_default` (boolean, required) — Whether this is the workspace's default group.
- `status` (string, required) — Status of the group; `active` when usable.
- `rules` (list of FirewallRule, required) — Rules in the group.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description of the group.
- `linked_instance_count` (integer, optional) — Number of VMs the group is attached to.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### FirewallRule

A rule in a firewall group.

- `direction` (enum, required, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, required, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `action` (enum, required, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, required) — Whether the rule is applied.
- `system_managed` (boolean, required) — True for rules the platform manages.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Get a firewall group

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}

Returns a firewall group with its rules. Requires scope: firewall.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/get-firewall-group

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Firewall group ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Firewall group returned successfully.

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the group.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `is_default` (boolean, required) — Whether this is the workspace's default group.
- `status` (string, required) — Status of the group; `active` when usable.
- `rules` (list of FirewallRule, required) — Rules in the group.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description of the group.
- `linked_instance_count` (integer, optional) — Number of VMs the group is attached to.

# Delete a firewall group

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}

Deletes a firewall group. Requires scope: firewall.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/delete-firewall-group

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Firewall group ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 204

Firewall group deleted successfully.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

# Add a firewall rule

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}/rules
Content-Type: application/json

Adds a rule to a firewall group, with its direction, protocol, port range, remote targets, action, and priority. Requires scope: firewall.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID/rules?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"description": "<description>", "direction": "ingress"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/create-firewall-rule

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Firewall group ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateFirewallRuleRequest.

- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `direction` (enum, optional, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, optional, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `action` (enum, optional, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.

## Response

### 201

Firewall rule added successfully.

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the group.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `is_default` (boolean, required) — Whether this is the workspace's default group.
- `status` (string, required) — Status of the group; `active` when usable.
- `rules` (list of FirewallRule, required) — Rules in the group.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description of the group.
- `linked_instance_count` (integer, optional) — Number of VMs the group is attached to.

Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### FirewallRule

A rule in a firewall group.

- `direction` (enum, required, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, required, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `action` (enum, required, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, required) — Whether the rule is applied.
- `system_managed` (boolean, required) — True for rules the platform manages.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Delete a firewall rule

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}/rules/{firewall_rule_id}

Removes a rule from a firewall group. Requires scope: firewall.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
# FIREWALL_RULE_ID: Firewall rule ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID/rules/$FIREWALL_RULE_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/delete-firewall-rule

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Firewall group ID.
- `firewall_rule_id` (string, required) — Firewall rule ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Firewall rule deleted successfully.

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the group.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `is_default` (boolean, required) — Whether this is the workspace's default group.
- `status` (string, required) — Status of the group; `active` when usable.
- `rules` (list of FirewallRule, required) — Rules in the group.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description of the group.
- `linked_instance_count` (integer, optional) — Number of VMs the group is attached to.

## Errors

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. # Update a firewall rule

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}/rules/{firewall_rule_id}
Content-Type: application/json

Changes an existing rule in a firewall group. Requires scope: firewall.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
# FIREWALL_RULE_ID: Firewall rule ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID/rules/$FIREWALL_RULE_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"description": "<description>", "direction": "ingress"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/update-firewall-rule

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Firewall group ID.
- `firewall_rule_id` (string, required) — Firewall rule ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an UpdateFirewallRuleRequest.

- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `direction` (enum, optional, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, optional, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `action` (enum, optional, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, optional) — Whether the rule is applied.

## Response

### 200

Firewall rule updated successfully.

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the group.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `is_default` (boolean, required) — Whether this is the workspace's default group.
- `status` (string, required) — Status of the group; `active` when usable.
- `rules` (list of FirewallRule, required) — Rules in the group.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description of the group.
- `linked_instance_count` (integer, optional) — Number of VMs the group is attached to.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### FirewallRule

A rule in a firewall group.

- `direction` (enum, required, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, required, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `action` (enum, required, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, required) — Whether the rule is applied.
- `system_managed` (boolean, required) — True for rules the platform manages.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

	payload := strings.NewReader("{\n  \"description\": \"<description>\",\n  \"direction\": \"ingress\"\n}")

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("PATCH", url, payload)

	req.Header.Add("Authorization", "Bearer <token>")
	req.Header.Add("Content-Type", "application/json")

	res, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(res.Body)

	fmt.Println(res)
	fmt.Println(string(body))

}

# List firewall group attachments

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}/attachments

Lists the VMs a firewall group is applied to. Requires scope: firewall.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID/attachments?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/list-firewall-group-attachments

### Query parameters

- `limit` (integer, optional, default: 50) — Maximum number of records to return.
- `skip` (integer, optional, default: 0) — Number of items to skip before the first returned item. Default 0.

### 200

Firewall attachments returned successfully.

# Attach a VM to a firewall group

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}/attachments
Content-Type: application/json

Applies a firewall group's rules to a VM. Requires scope: firewall.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID/attachments?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"vm_id": "<vm_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/attach-firewall-group

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Firewall group ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a FirewallAttachmentRequest.

- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM.

## Response

### 200

VM attached successfully.

- `firewall_group_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the group.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the group.
- `is_default` (boolean, required) — Whether this is the workspace's default group.
- `status` (string, required) — Status of the group; `active` when usable.
- `rules` (list of FirewallRule, required) — Rules in the group.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description of the group.
- `linked_instance_count` (integer, optional) — Number of VMs the group is attached to.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.

## Types

### FirewallRule

A rule in a firewall group.

- `direction` (enum, required, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, required, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `action` (enum, required, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, required) — Whether the rule is applied.
- `system_managed` (boolean, required) — True for rules the platform manages.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Detach a VM from a firewall group

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/{firewall_group_id}/attachments/{vm_id}

Removes a firewall group from a VM. Its rules no longer apply to that VM. Requires scope: firewall.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# FIREWALL_GROUP_ID: Firewall group ID
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/firewall-groups/$FIREWALL_GROUP_ID/attachments/$VM_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/firewalls/detach-firewall-group

- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 423 Locked Error

The organization is suspended (`organization_suspended`), so writes are refused.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### FirewallRule

A rule in a firewall group.

- `direction` (enum, required, default: ingress) — - `ingress`: traffic into the VM (default). - `egress`: traffic out of the VM.
  - Allowed values: `ingress`, `egress`
- `protocol` (enum, required, default: tcp) — - `tcp` (default) - `udp` - `icmp` - `any`: all protocols.
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `any`
- `action` (enum, required, default: allow) — - `allow`: let matching traffic through (default). - `drop`: discard matching traffic.
  - Allowed values: `allow`, `drop`
- `rule_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the rule.
- `enabled` (boolean, required) — Whether the rule is applied.
- `system_managed` (boolean, required) — True for rules the platform manages.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the rule was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description of the rule.
- `port_start` (integer, optional, nullable) — First port of the range (1-65535). Required for `tcp` and `udp`; ignored for other protocols.
- `port_end` (integer, optional, nullable) — Last port of the range (1-65535). Defaults to `port_start`.
- `remote_targets` (list of string, optional) — Remote IPv4 addresses or CIDRs the rule matches, for example `0.0.0.0/0`.
- `priority` (integer, optional, nullable) — Evaluation priority of the rule.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# List load balancers

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers

Lists the L4 and L7 load balancers in a workspace. Requires scope: load-balancer.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/list-load-balancers

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `status` (enum, optional) — Return only load balancers in this status.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `layer` (enum, optional) — Return only load balancers of this layer. - `l4` - `l7`
  - Allowed values: `l4`, `l7`
- `protocol` (enum, optional) — Return only load balancers that accept this protocol.
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `limit` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Maximum number of items to return (1-500). Default 100.
- `skip` (integer, optional, default: 0) — Number of items to skip before the first returned item. Default 0.

## Response

### 200

Load balancers returned successfully.

- `list of LoadBalancer`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. ## Types

### LoadBalancer

A load balancer.

- `lb_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the load balancer.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `layer` (enum, required) — - `l4`: TCP or TLS pass-through. - `l7`: HTTP or HTTPS.
  - Allowed values: `l4`, `l7`
- `protocol` (enum, required) — Protocol the load balancer accepts. - `http`, `https`: L7 load balancers. - `tcp`: L4 pass-through of TCP connections. - `tls_passthrough`: L4 pass-through of TLS connections without terminating them.
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a load balancer. - `provisioning`: being created. - `active`: serving traffic. - `failed`: provisioning failed; see `error_message` on the status endpoint. - `deleting`: being removed. - `deleted`: removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `endpoint` (LoadBalancerEndpoint, required) — Where clients connect to the load balancer.
- `url` (string, required) — Public hostname of the load balancer.
- `endpoint_url` (string, required) — URL with scheme and, for L4, port: for example `https://host` or `tcp://host:443`.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Backends the load balancer sends traffic to.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `namespace` (string, optional) — Kubernetes namespace the load balancer runs in.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional, nullable) — L7 routing rules; null for L4 load balancers.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### LoadBalancerEndpoint

Where clients connect to the load balancer.

- `host` (string, required) — Public hostname.
- `port` (integer, required) — Listener port.

### LoadBalancerBackend

A backend the load balancer sends traffic to.

- `target` (string, required) — Backend address: a service name, an IP address or an FQDN, depending on `type`.
- `port` (integer, required) — Backend port (1-65535).
- `type` (enum, optional, default: service) — - `service`: a Kubernetes service name (default). - `ip`: an IP address. - `hostname`: a fully qualified domain name.
  - Allowed values: `service`, `ip`, `hostname`
- `weight` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Relative weight for traffic distribution (1-1000). Default 100.
- `tls` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Use TLS between the load balancer and the backend. Default false.

### LoadBalancerRule

An L7 routing rule.

- `priority` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Order in which rules are evaluated; lower values first. Default 1.
- `path_prefix` (string, optional, default: /) — Request path prefix the rule matches. Default `/`.
- `headers` (map from string to string, optional, nullable) — Header names and values a request must carry to match.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional, nullable) — Backends for matching requests; the load balancer's own backends are used when omitted.

# Create an L4 load balancer

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l4
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a layer 4 (TCP/UDP) load balancer that spreads connections across backend VMs, with optional TLS. Requires scope: load-balancer.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l4?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>", "protocol": "tcp", "backends": [{"target": "<target>", "port": 1}]}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/create-l-4-load-balancer

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateL4LoadBalancerRequest.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `protocol` (enum, required) — - `tcp` - `tls_passthrough`
  - Allowed values: `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Backends to send traffic to.
- `routing` (LoadBalancerRouting, optional) — How requests are distributed across backends.
- `tls` (LoadBalancerTls, optional) — TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.

## Response

### 201

L4 load balancer created successfully.

- `lb_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the load balancer.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `layer` (enum, required) — - `l4`: TCP or TLS pass-through. - `l7`: HTTP or HTTPS.
  - Allowed values: `l4`, `l7`
- `protocol` (enum, required) — Protocol the load balancer accepts. - `http`, `https`: L7 load balancers. - `tcp`: L4 pass-through of TCP connections. - `tls_passthrough`: L4 pass-through of TLS connections without terminating them.
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a load balancer. - `provisioning`: being created. - `active`: serving traffic. - `failed`: provisioning failed; see `error_message` on the status endpoint. - `deleting`: being removed. - `deleted`: removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `endpoint` (LoadBalancerEndpoint, required) — Where clients connect to the load balancer.
- `url` (string, required) — Public hostname of the load balancer.
- `endpoint_url` (string, required) — URL with scheme and, for L4, port: for example `https://host` or `tcp://host:443`.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Backends the load balancer sends traffic to.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `namespace` (string, optional) — Kubernetes namespace the load balancer runs in.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional, nullable) — L7 routing rules; null for L4 load balancers.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

Billing refused the request (`billing_denied`). `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason unchanged, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` (a plan limit) or `resource_usage_unavailable` (Billing could not count usage). `billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` identify the decision. ## Types

### LoadBalancerBackend

A backend the load balancer sends traffic to.

- `target` (string, required) — Backend address: a service name, an IP address or an FQDN, depending on `type`.
- `port` (integer, required) — Backend port (1-65535).
- `type` (enum, optional, default: service) — - `service`: a Kubernetes service name (default). - `ip`: an IP address. - `hostname`: a fully qualified domain name.
  - Allowed values: `service`, `ip`, `hostname`
- `weight` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Relative weight for traffic distribution (1-1000). Default 100.
- `tls` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Use TLS between the load balancer and the backend. Default false.

### LoadBalancerRouting

How requests are distributed across backends.

- `algorithm` (enum, optional, default: round_robin) — - `round_robin`: backends in turn (default). - `least_request`: the backend with the fewest active requests. - `random`: a random backend. - `consistent_hash`: the same backend for the same `sticky_header` value.
  - Allowed values: `round_robin`, `least_request`, `random`, `consistent_hash`
- `sticky_header` (string, optional, nullable) — Request header whose value selects the backend with `consistent_hash`.

### LoadBalancerTls

TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.

- `mode` (enum, required) — - `terminate`: TLS ends at the load balancer. - `passthrough`: TLS is forwarded to the backend unchanged.
  - Allowed values: `terminate`, `passthrough`
- `certificate_source` (string, optional, default: managed) — `managed` for a platform-issued certificate, or `custom` to supply `cert_pem` and `key_pem`. Default `managed`.
- `cert_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded certificate chain; required with `certificate_source: custom`.
- `key_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded private key; required with `certificate_source: custom`.

### LoadBalancerEndpoint

Where clients connect to the load balancer.

- `host` (string, required) — Public hostname.
- `port` (integer, required) — Listener port.

### LoadBalancerRule

An L7 routing rule.

- `priority` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Order in which rules are evaluated; lower values first. Default 1.
- `path_prefix` (string, optional, default: /) — Request path prefix the rule matches. Default `/`.
- `headers` (map from string to string, optional, nullable) — Header names and values a request must carry to match.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional, nullable) — Backends for matching requests; the load balancer's own backends are used when omitted.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any
