# Create an L7 load balancer

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l7
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) load balancer with routing rules, optional TLS, and an optional custom domain. Requires scope: load-balancer.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l7?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>", "protocol": "http", "backends": [{"target": "<target>", "port": 1}]}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/create-l-7-load-balancer

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateL7LoadBalancerRequest.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `protocol` (enum, required) — - `http` - `https`
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Default backends for requests no rule matches.
- `routing` (LoadBalancerRouting, optional) — How requests are distributed across backends.
- `tls` (LoadBalancerTls, optional) — TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.
- `custom_domain` (CreateL7LoadBalancerRequestCustomDomain, optional, nullable) — Custom hostname to serve. Point its DNS CNAME at the load balancer's endpoint host.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional) — Path- and header-based routing rules.

## Response

### 201

L7 load balancer created successfully.

- `lb_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the load balancer.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `layer` (enum, required) — - `l4`: TCP or TLS pass-through. - `l7`: HTTP or HTTPS.
  - Allowed values: `l4`, `l7`
- `protocol` (enum, required) — Protocol the load balancer accepts. - `http`, `https`: L7 load balancers. - `tcp`: L4 pass-through of TCP connections. - `tls_passthrough`: L4 pass-through of TLS connections without terminating them.
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a load balancer. - `provisioning`: being created. - `active`: serving traffic. - `failed`: provisioning failed; see `error_message` on the status endpoint. - `deleting`: being removed. - `deleted`: removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `endpoint` (LoadBalancerEndpoint, required) — Where clients connect to the load balancer.
- `url` (string, required) — Public hostname of the load balancer.
- `endpoint_url` (string, required) — URL with scheme and, for L4, port: for example `https://host` or `tcp://host:443`.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Backends the load balancer sends traffic to.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `namespace` (string, optional) — Kubernetes namespace the load balancer runs in.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional, nullable) — L7 routing rules; null for L4 load balancers.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 402 Payment Required Error

Billing refused the request (`billing_denied`). `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason unchanged, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` (a plan limit) or `resource_usage_unavailable` (Billing could not count usage). `billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` identify the decision. Nothing is provisioned; resolve the reason and retry with the same idempotency key where supported.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 409 Conflict Error

The request conflicts with the current resource state.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

### 423 Locked Error

The organization is suspended (`organization_suspended`), so writes are refused.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

## Types

### LoadBalancerBackend

A backend the load balancer sends traffic to.

- `target` (string, required) — Backend address: a service name, an IP address or an FQDN, depending on `type`.
- `port` (integer, required) — Backend port (1-65535).
- `type` (enum, optional, default: service) — - `service`: a Kubernetes service name (default). - `ip`: an IP address. - `hostname`: a fully qualified domain name.
  - Allowed values: `service`, `ip`, `hostname`
- `weight` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Relative weight for traffic distribution (1-1000). Default 100.
- `tls` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Use TLS between the load balancer and the backend. Default false.

### LoadBalancerRouting

How requests are distributed across backends.

- `algorithm` (enum, optional, default: round_robin) — - `round_robin`: backends in turn (default). - `least_request`: the backend with the fewest active requests. - `random`: a random backend. - `consistent_hash`: the same backend for the same `sticky_header` value.
  - Allowed values: `round_robin`, `least_request`, `random`, `consistent_hash`
- `sticky_header` (string, optional, nullable) — Request header whose value selects the backend with `consistent_hash`.

### LoadBalancerTls

TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.

- `mode` (enum, required) — - `terminate`: TLS ends at the load balancer. - `passthrough`: TLS is forwarded to the backend unchanged.
  - Allowed values: `terminate`, `passthrough`
- `certificate_source` (string, optional, default: managed) — `managed` for a platform-issued certificate, or `custom` to supply `cert_pem` and `key_pem`. Default `managed`.
- `cert_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded certificate chain; required with `certificate_source: custom`.
- `key_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded private key; required with `certificate_source: custom`.

### CreateL7LoadBalancerRequestCustomDomain

Custom hostname to serve. Point its DNS CNAME at the load balancer's endpoint host.

- `hostname` (string, optional) — Fully qualified domain name to serve.

### LoadBalancerRule

An L7 routing rule.

- `priority` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Order in which rules are evaluated; lower values first. Default 1.
- `path_prefix` (string, optional, default: /) — Request path prefix the rule matches. Default `/`.
- `headers` (map from string to string, optional, nullable) — Header names and values a request must carry to match.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional, nullable) — Backends for matching requests; the load balancer's own backends are used when omitted.

### LoadBalancerEndpoint

Where clients connect to the load balancer.

- `host` (string, required) — Public hostname.
- `port` (integer, required) — Listener port.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

```go
	defer res.Body.Close()

	fmt.Println(string(body))

}
```

```php
  "backends": [
```

```swift
  if (error != nil) {
    print(error as Any)

    let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse
    print(httpResponse)
```

# Get a load balancer

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/{load_balancer_id}

Returns a load balancer's configuration, including its backends, routing, and TLS settings. Requires scope: load-balancer.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# LOAD_BALANCER_ID: Load balancer ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/get-load-balancer

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `load_balancer_id` (string, required) — Load balancer ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Load balancer returned successfully.

- `lb_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the load balancer.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `layer` (enum, required) — - `l4`: TCP or TLS pass-through. - `l7`: HTTP or HTTPS.
  - Allowed values: `l4`, `l7`
- `protocol` (enum, required) — Protocol the load balancer accepts. - `http`, `https`: L7 load balancers. - `tcp`: L4 pass-through of TCP connections. - `tls_passthrough`: L4 pass-through of TLS connections without terminating them.
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a load balancer. - `provisioning`: being created. - `active`: serving traffic. - `failed`: provisioning failed; see `error_message` on the status endpoint. - `deleting`: being removed. - `deleted`: removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `endpoint` (LoadBalancerEndpoint, required) — Where clients connect to the load balancer.
- `url` (string, required) — Public hostname of the load balancer.
- `endpoint_url` (string, required) — URL with scheme and, for L4, port: for example `https://host` or `tcp://host:443`.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Backends the load balancer sends traffic to.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `namespace` (string, optional) — Kubernetes namespace the load balancer runs in.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional, nullable) — L7 routing rules; null for L4 load balancers.

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### LoadBalancerEndpoint

Where clients connect to the load balancer.

- `host` (string, required) — Public hostname.
- `port` (integer, required) — Listener port.

### LoadBalancerBackend

A backend the load balancer sends traffic to.

- `target` (string, required) — Backend address: a service name, an IP address or an FQDN, depending on `type`.
- `port` (integer, required) — Backend port (1-65535).
- `type` (enum, optional, default: service) — - `service`: a Kubernetes service name (default). - `ip`: an IP address. - `hostname`: a fully qualified domain name.
  - Allowed values: `service`, `ip`, `hostname`
- `weight` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Relative weight for traffic distribution (1-1000). Default 100.
- `tls` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Use TLS between the load balancer and the backend. Default false.

### LoadBalancerRule

An L7 routing rule.

- `priority` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Order in which rules are evaluated; lower values first. Default 1.
- `path_prefix` (string, optional, default: /) — Request path prefix the rule matches. Default `/`.
- `headers` (map from string to string, optional, nullable) — Header names and values a request must carry to match.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional, nullable) — Backends for matching requests; the load balancer's own backends are used when omitted.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Delete a load balancer

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/{load_balancer_id}

Deletes a load balancer. The backend VMs are not deleted. Requires scope: load-balancer.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# LOAD_BALANCER_ID: Load balancer ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/delete-load-balancer

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `load_balancer_id` (string, required) — Load balancer ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 204

Load balancer deletion accepted.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

### 423 Locked Error

# Update an L4 load balancer

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l4/{load_balancer_id}
Content-Type: application/json

Changes an L4 load balancer's backends, routing, or TLS settings. Requires scope: load-balancer.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# LOAD_BALANCER_ID: Load balancer ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l4/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>", "backends": [{"target": "<target>", "port": 1}]}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/update-l-4-load-balancer

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `load_balancer_id` (string, required) — Load balancer ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an UpdateL4LoadBalancerRequest.

- `name` (string, optional) — New display name.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional) — Replacement backend list.
- `routing` (LoadBalancerRouting, optional) — How requests are distributed across backends.
- `tls` (LoadBalancerTls, optional) — TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.

## Response

### 200

L4 load balancer updated successfully.

- `lb_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the load balancer.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `layer` (enum, required) — - `l4`: TCP or TLS pass-through. - `l7`: HTTP or HTTPS.
  - Allowed values: `l4`, `l7`
- `protocol` (enum, required) — Protocol the load balancer accepts. - `http`, `https`: L7 load balancers. - `tcp`: L4 pass-through of TCP connections. - `tls_passthrough`: L4 pass-through of TLS connections without terminating them.
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a load balancer. - `provisioning`: being created. - `active`: serving traffic. - `failed`: provisioning failed; see `error_message` on the status endpoint. - `deleting`: being removed. - `deleted`: removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `endpoint` (LoadBalancerEndpoint, required) — Where clients connect to the load balancer.
- `url` (string, required) — Public hostname of the load balancer.
- `endpoint_url` (string, required) — URL with scheme and, for L4, port: for example `https://host` or `tcp://host:443`.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Backends the load balancer sends traffic to.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `namespace` (string, optional) — Kubernetes namespace the load balancer runs in.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional, nullable) — L7 routing rules; null for L4 load balancers.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. - `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. - `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. ## Types

### LoadBalancerBackend

A backend the load balancer sends traffic to.

- `target` (string, required) — Backend address: a service name, an IP address or an FQDN, depending on `type`.
- `port` (integer, required) — Backend port (1-65535).
- `type` (enum, optional, default: service) — - `service`: a Kubernetes service name (default). - `ip`: an IP address. - `hostname`: a fully qualified domain name.
  - Allowed values: `service`, `ip`, `hostname`
- `weight` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Relative weight for traffic distribution (1-1000). Default 100.
- `tls` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Use TLS between the load balancer and the backend. Default false.

### LoadBalancerRouting

How requests are distributed across backends.

- `algorithm` (enum, optional, default: round_robin) — - `round_robin`: backends in turn (default). - `least_request`: the backend with the fewest active requests. - `random`: a random backend. - `consistent_hash`: the same backend for the same `sticky_header` value.
  - Allowed values: `round_robin`, `least_request`, `random`, `consistent_hash`
- `sticky_header` (string, optional, nullable) — Request header whose value selects the backend with `consistent_hash`.

### LoadBalancerTls

TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.

- `mode` (enum, required) — - `terminate`: TLS ends at the load balancer. - `passthrough`: TLS is forwarded to the backend unchanged.
  - Allowed values: `terminate`, `passthrough`
- `certificate_source` (string, optional, default: managed) — `managed` for a platform-issued certificate, or `custom` to supply `cert_pem` and `key_pem`. Default `managed`.
- `cert_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded certificate chain; required with `certificate_source: custom`.
- `key_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded private key; required with `certificate_source: custom`.

### LoadBalancerEndpoint

Where clients connect to the load balancer.

- `host` (string, required) — Public hostname.
- `port` (integer, required) — Listener port.

### LoadBalancerRule

An L7 routing rule.

- `priority` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Order in which rules are evaluated; lower values first. Default 1.
- `path_prefix` (string, optional, default: /) — Request path prefix the rule matches. Default `/`.
- `headers` (map from string to string, optional, nullable) — Header names and values a request must carry to match.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional, nullable) — Backends for matching requests; the load balancer's own backends are used when omitted.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

title: Update an L7 load balancer
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/update-l-7-load-balancer

# Update an L7 load balancer

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l7/{load_balancer_id}
Content-Type: application/json

Changes an L7 load balancer's backends, routing rules, TLS settings, or custom domain. Requires scope: load-balancer.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# LOAD_BALANCER_ID: Load balancer ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l7/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>", "backends": [{"target": "<target>", "port": 1}]}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/update-l-7-load-balancer

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `load_balancer_id` (string, required) — Load balancer ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects an UpdateL7LoadBalancerRequest.

- `name` (string, optional) — New display name.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional) — Replacement default backend list.
- `routing` (LoadBalancerRouting, optional) — How requests are distributed across backends.
- `tls` (LoadBalancerTls, optional) — TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.
- `custom_domain` (UpdateL7LoadBalancerRequestCustomDomain, optional, nullable) — Custom hostname to serve. Point its DNS CNAME at the load balancer's endpoint host.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional) — Replacement routing rules.

## Response

### 200

L7 load balancer updated successfully.

- `lb_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the load balancer.
- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning organization.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the owning workspace.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the load balancer.
- `layer` (enum, required) — - `l4`: TCP or TLS pass-through. - `l7`: HTTP or HTTPS.
  - Allowed values: `l4`, `l7`
- `protocol` (enum, required) — Protocol the load balancer accepts. - `http`, `https`: L7 load balancers. - `tcp`: L4 pass-through of TCP connections. - `tls_passthrough`: L4 pass-through of TLS connections without terminating them.
  - Allowed values: `http`, `https`, `tcp`, `tls_passthrough`
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a load balancer. - `provisioning`: being created. - `active`: serving traffic. - `failed`: provisioning failed; see `error_message` on the status endpoint. - `deleting`: being removed. - `deleted`: removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `endpoint` (LoadBalancerEndpoint, required) — Where clients connect to the load balancer.
- `url` (string, required) — Public hostname of the load balancer.
- `endpoint_url` (string, required) — URL with scheme and, for L4, port: for example `https://host` or `tcp://host:443`.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, required) — Backends the load balancer sends traffic to.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the resource was last changed (ISO 8601).
- `workspace_name` (string, optional) — Display name of the workspace.
- `namespace` (string, optional) — Kubernetes namespace the load balancer runs in.
- `rules` (list of LoadBalancerRule, optional, nullable) — L7 routing rules; null for L4 load balancers.

Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 409 Conflict Error

The request conflicts with the current resource state.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

### 423 Locked Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. - `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### LoadBalancerBackend

A backend the load balancer sends traffic to.

- `target` (string, required) — Backend address: a service name, an IP address or an FQDN, depending on `type`.
- `port` (integer, required) — Backend port (1-65535).
- `type` (enum, optional, default: service) — - `service`: a Kubernetes service name (default). - `ip`: an IP address. - `hostname`: a fully qualified domain name.
  - Allowed values: `service`, `ip`, `hostname`
- `weight` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Relative weight for traffic distribution (1-1000). Default 100.
- `tls` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Use TLS between the load balancer and the backend. Default false.

### LoadBalancerRouting

How requests are distributed across backends.

- `algorithm` (enum, optional, default: round_robin) — - `round_robin`: backends in turn (default). - `least_request`: the backend with the fewest active requests. - `random`: a random backend. - `consistent_hash`: the same backend for the same `sticky_header` value.
  - Allowed values: `round_robin`, `least_request`, `random`, `consistent_hash`
- `sticky_header` (string, optional, nullable) — Request header whose value selects the backend with `consistent_hash`.

### LoadBalancerTls

TLS settings for the load balancer's listener.

- `mode` (enum, required) — - `terminate`: TLS ends at the load balancer. - `passthrough`: TLS is forwarded to the backend unchanged.
  - Allowed values: `terminate`, `passthrough`
- `certificate_source` (string, optional, default: managed) — `managed` for a platform-issued certificate, or `custom` to supply `cert_pem` and `key_pem`. Default `managed`.
- `cert_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded certificate chain; required with `certificate_source: custom`.
- `key_pem` (string, optional, nullable) — PEM-encoded private key; required with `certificate_source: custom`.

### UpdateL7LoadBalancerRequestCustomDomain

Custom hostname to serve. Point its DNS CNAME at the load balancer's endpoint host.

- `hostname` (string, optional) — Fully qualified domain name to serve.

### LoadBalancerRule

An L7 routing rule.

- `priority` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Order in which rules are evaluated; lower values first. Default 1.
- `path_prefix` (string, optional, default: /) — Request path prefix the rule matches. Default `/`.
- `headers` (map from string to string, optional, nullable) — Header names and values a request must carry to match.
- `backends` (list of LoadBalancerBackend, optional, nullable) — Backends for matching requests; the load balancer's own backends are used when omitted.

### LoadBalancerEndpoint

Where clients connect to the load balancer.

- `host` (string, required) — Public hostname.
- `port` (integer, required) — Listener port.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

```go
import (

func main() {

	url := "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/l7/load_balancer_123?workspace_id=710995"

	payload := strings.NewReader("{\n  \"name\": \"<name>\",\n  \"backends\": [\n    {\n      \"target\": \"<target>\",\n      \"port\": 1\n    }\n  ]\n}")

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("PATCH", url, payload)

	req.Header.Add("Authorization", "Bearer <token>")
	req.Header.Add("Content-Type", "application/json")

	res, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(res.Body)

	fmt.Println(res)
	fmt.Println(string(body))

}
```

```swift
  if (error != nil) {
    print(error as Any)
  } else {
    let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse
    print(httpResponse)
  }
})

dataTask.resume()
```

# Get load balancer status

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/{load_balancer_id}/status

Returns a load balancer's provisioning status, endpoint URL, and any error conditions. Requires scope: load-balancer.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# LOAD_BALANCER_ID: Load balancer ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID/status?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/load-balancers/get-load-balancer-status

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `load_balancer_id` (string, required) — Load balancer ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Load balancer status returned successfully.

- `lb_id` (string, required) — ID of the load balancer.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a load balancer. - `provisioning`: being created. - `active`: serving traffic. - `failed`: provisioning failed; see `error_message` on the status endpoint. - `deleting`: being removed. - `deleted`: removed.
  - Allowed values: `provisioning`, `active`, `failed`, `deleting`, `deleted`
- `endpoint` (LoadBalancerEndpoint, required) — Where clients connect to the load balancer.
- `url` (string, required) — Public hostname of the load balancer.
- `endpoint_url` (string, required) — URL with scheme and, for L4, port.
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the status last changed (ISO 8601).
- `conditions` (list of map from string to any, optional) — Provisioning conditions reported by the platform, passed through as returned.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `failed`.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

```swift
let headers = ["Authorization": "Bearer <token>"]

let request = NSMutableURLRequest(url: NSURL(string: "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/networking/load-balancers/load_balancer_123/status?workspace_id=710995")! as URL,
                                        cachePolicy: .useProtocolCachePolicy,
                                    timeoutInterval: 10.0)
request.httpMethod = "GET"
request.allHTTPHeaderFields = headers

let session = URLSession.shared
let dataTask = session.dataTask(with: request as URLRequest, completionHandler: { (data, response, error) -> Void in
  if (error != nil) {
    print(error as Any)
  } else {
    let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse
    print(httpResponse)
  }
})

dataTask.resume()
```

# List compute sites

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/sites

Lists sites where cloud and GPU VMs can be placed. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/sites?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/compute-catalog/list-compute-sites

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Compute sites returned successfully.

- `sites` (list of ComputeSite, required) — Available sites.
- `count` (integer, required) — Number of items in `sites`.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### ComputeSite

A placement site (data-centre location) that accepts VM creation.

- `site_id` (string, required) — Canonical opaque placement ID accepted by VM creation. Copy it exactly; do not substitute `site_code`, `region_id`, or `name`.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the site.
- `site_code` (string, optional, nullable) — Short site code, when the catalog has one.
- `location` (string, optional, nullable) — City or location label, as shown in the portal.
- `region_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the region the site belongs to.
- `country_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the country the site is in.
- `timezone` (string, optional, nullable) — IANA time zone of the site.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# List compute plans

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/plans

Lists billable cloud or GPU VM plans. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/plans?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID&vm_type=cloud" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/compute-catalog/list-compute-plans

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `vm_type` (enum, required) — Kind of VM the plans are for. Required. - `cloud` - `gpu`
  - Allowed values: `cloud`, `gpu`
- `site_id` (string, optional) — Optional exact placement filter. Copy `site_id` from `GET /compute/sites`.
- `currency` (string, optional, default: INR) — ISO 4217 code of the currency to quote prices in. Default `INR`.
- `billing_interval` (enum, optional, default: MONTHLY) — Billing period to quote prices for. - `HOURLY` - `MONTHLY` (default)
  - Allowed values: `HOURLY`, `MONTHLY`

## Response

### 200

Compute plans returned successfully.

- `plans` (list of ComputePlan, required) — Plans matching the request.
- `count` (integer, required) — Number of items in `plans`.
- `vm_type` (enum, required) — Kind of virtual machine. - `cloud`: general-purpose cloud VM. - `gpu`: VM with attached GPUs.
  - Allowed values: `cloud`, `gpu`
- `currency` (string, required) — ISO 4217 code of the currency the prices are quoted in.
- `billing_interval` (enum, required, default: MONTHLY) — Billing period a price is quoted for. - `HOURLY`: price per hour of running time. - `MONTHLY`: price per calendar month (default).
  - Allowed values: `HOURLY`, `MONTHLY`
- `site_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Site filter that was applied, when one was given.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### ComputePlan

A billable compute plan: the vCPU, memory, root-disk and (for GPU plans) GPU shape, with its catalog price.

- `plan_id` (string, required) — Plan ID accepted by VM creation.
- `vm_type` (enum, required) — Kind of virtual machine. - `cloud`: general-purpose cloud VM. - `gpu`: VM with attached GPUs.
  - Allowed values: `cloud`, `gpu`
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the plan.
- `code` (string, required) — Plan SKU code from the billing catalog.
- `cpu` (integer, required) — vCPUs included in the plan.
- `ram_mb` (integer, required) — Memory included in the plan, in MB.
- `disk_gb` (integer, required) — Root disk included in the plan, in GB.
- `gpu_count` (integer, required) — GPUs included in the plan; 0 for cloud plans.
- `selectable` (boolean, required) — Whether the plan can be chosen for a new VM right now.
- `pricing_status` (enum, required) — - `priced`: the catalog has a price and the plan can be quoted. - `unpriced`: no catalog price; the plan cannot be used to create a VM.
  - Allowed values: `priced`, `unpriced`
- `currency` (string, required) — ISO 4217 code of the currency the price fields are in.
- `billing_interval` (enum, required, default: MONTHLY) — Billing period a price is quoted for. - `HOURLY`: price per hour of running time. - `MONTHLY`: price per calendar month (default).
  - Allowed values: `HOURLY`, `MONTHLY`
- `gpu_model` (string, optional, nullable) — GPU model for GPU plans, for example `A100`; null for cloud plans.
- `gpu_memory_gb` (double, optional, nullable) — GPU memory in GB as listed in the catalog; null for cloud plans.
- `hourly_price_minor` (integer, optional, nullable) — Hourly price in the currency's minor unit (for example paise for INR); null when not priced.
- `monthly_price_minor` (integer, optional, nullable) — Monthly price in the currency's minor unit; null when not priced.
- `site_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Site the list was filtered by, when a `site_id` was given.
- `billing_catalog` (map from string to any, optional, nullable) — Canonical billing SKU reference for this plan. Pass this object unmodified as `billing_catalog` when creating a VM with this plan — the same flow the portal uses. Treat it as opaque; its fields may grow over time. Billing charges are always computed server-side from `plan_id`, not from this echoed copy.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

```swift
import Foundation

let headers = ["Authorization": "Bearer <token>"]

let request = NSMutableURLRequest(url: NSURL(string: "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/plans?workspace_id=710995&vm_type=cloud")! as URL,
                                        cachePolicy: .useProtocolCachePolicy,
                                    timeoutInterval: 10.0)
request.httpMethod = "GET"
request.allHTTPHeaderFields = headers

let session = URLSession.shared
let dataTask = session.dataTask(with: request as URLRequest, completionHandler: { (data, response, error) -> Void in
  if (error != nil) {
    print(error as Any)
  } else {
    let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse
    print(httpResponse)
  }
})

dataTask.resume()
```
