## Types

### BillingCatalogSelection

A Billing catalog SKU selection as the VM engine accepts it. `sku_id` and `sku_code` are required; other catalog fields are accepted and stored as sent.

- `sku_id` (BillingCatalogSelectionSkuId, required) — Billing catalog SKU ID.
- `sku_code` (string, required) — Billing catalog SKU code. Stored in upper case.
- `product_id` (BillingCatalogSelectionProductId, optional, nullable) — Billing catalog product ID.
- `product_code` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing catalog product code.
- `display_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the SKU, as listed in the billing catalog.

### RecoveryVolumeManifestItem

One volume captured in a recovery point (backup run or snapshot set): how it was attached at capture time, the stored artifact that holds its data, and where it was restored.

- `source_volume_id` (string, required) — ID of the volume that was captured.
- `source_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the source volume.
- `resource_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Backend storage resource name of the source volume.
- `role` (enum, optional, default: data) — - `root`: the VM's root disk. - `data`: an attached data volume.
  - Allowed values: `root`, `data`
- `size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Provisioned size of the volume in GiB.
- `display_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size in GiB as shown in the portal.
- `device_bus` (string, optional, nullable) — Virtual disk bus the volume was attached on, for example `virtio`.
- `device_slot` (string, optional, nullable) — Guest device name of the attachment, for example `vda`.
- `boot_index` (integer, optional, nullable) — Position in the boot order; 0 for the boot disk, null for volumes not in the boot order.
- `attachment_mode` (string, optional, nullable) — Attachment mode at capture time, for example `boot` for the root disk or `single-writer` for a data volume.
- `guest_device` (string, optional, nullable) — Device name as seen inside the guest OS.
- `device_path` (string, optional, nullable) — Device path inside the guest, for example `/dev/vdb`.
- `filesystem_uuid` (string, optional, nullable) — Filesystem UUID detected on the volume, when known.
- `filesystem_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Filesystem type detected on the volume, for example `ext4`, when known.
- `mount_hint` (string, optional, nullable) — Mount point the volume is expected to use, for example `/` for the root disk.
- `mount_state_at_capture` (string, optional, nullable) — Mount state recorded at capture time, for example `mounted`, `instructions_pending` or `instructions_acknowledged`.
- `mount_instructions` (string, optional, nullable) — Human-readable instructions for mounting the volume after a restore.
- `delete_on_termination` (boolean, optional, nullable) — Whether the source volume was set to be deleted together with its VM.
- `source_attachment_present` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Whether the source volume was still attached to the VM when the manifest was last refreshed.
- `artifact_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of stored artifact that holds this volume's data in the recovery point.
- `artifact_ref` (string, optional, nullable) — Reference to that artifact in the backup store.
- `artifact_chain_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Backup chain the artifact belongs to.
- `artifact_backup_type` (string, optional, nullable) — `full` or `incremental`, for the artifact.
- `artifact_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size of the stored artifact in bytes.
- `billing_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes billed for storing this volume's artifact.
- `storage_usage` (map from string to any, optional, nullable) — Storage usage details reported by the backup store, as key-value data.
- `restored_volume_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the volume created by the most recent restore of this entry, when one was performed.
- `restored_resource_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Backend storage resource name of the restored volume.
- `restored_device_path` (string, optional, nullable) — Device path of the restored volume inside the target VM.
- `restored_target_vm_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VM the restored volume was attached to.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

### RecoveryPointSummary

Short description of the volumes a recovery point contains.

- `root_only` (boolean, optional, default: true) — True when only the root disk was captured.
- `root_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the captured root disk.
- `data_volume_names` (list of string, optional) — Display names of the captured data volumes.
- `summary_text` (string, optional, default: Root) — Ready-to-display summary of the captured volumes; `Root` when only the root disk was captured.

### LiveDriftSummary

Difference between the volumes in a recovery point and the volumes attached to the VM now.

- `drifted` (boolean, optional, default: false) — True when the VM's current volumes differ from the recovery point.
- `missing_from_live` (list of string, optional) — Volumes in the recovery point that are no longer attached to the VM.
- `new_live_only` (list of string, optional) — Volumes attached to the VM now that are not in the recovery point.
- `message` (string, optional, nullable) — Human-readable description of the drift, when any.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### BillingCatalogSelectionSkuId

Billing catalog SKU ID.

- string
- double

### BillingCatalogSelectionProductId

Billing catalog product ID.

- string
- double

title: Restore a cloud VM backup

# Restore a cloud VM backup

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vms/{vm_id}/backups/actions/restore
Content-Type: application/json

Restores a cloud VM backup recovery point by replacing the VM, creating a new VM, or restoring a single volume. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vms/$VM_ID/backups/actions/restore?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"recovery_point_id": "<recovery_point_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/cloud-vms/restore-cloud-vm-backup

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a BackupRestoreRequest.

- `recovery_point_id` (string, required) — Recovery point to restore: the `recovery_point_id` of a succeeded backup run.
- `target_mode` (enum, optional, default: replace) — Where to restore. - `replace`: onto the source VM, replacing its current disks (default). - `new_vm`: into a new VM described by the `target_*` fields. - `volume_only`: only the volume named in `selected_volume_id`.
  - Allowed values: `replace`, `new_vm`, `volume_only`
- `target_vm_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Name for the new VM (`new_vm` mode).
- `target_cpu` (integer, optional, nullable) — vCPUs for the new VM (1-256).
- `target_ram_mb` (integer, optional, nullable) — RAM for the new VM in MB (512-2097152).
- `target_disk_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Root disk for the new VM in GB (10-10000).
- `target_plan_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Compute plan for the new VM, from `GET /compute/plans`.
- `target_plan_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Name of that plan as listed in the compute catalog.
- `target_plan_code` (string, optional, nullable) — SKU code of that plan as listed in the compute catalog.
- `target_plan_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Plan type label as listed in the compute catalog.
- `target_performance_category` (string, optional, nullable) — Performance category of that plan as listed in the compute catalog.
- `target_plan_monthly_rate` (double, optional, nullable) — Monthly rate of that plan as listed in the compute catalog.
- `target_plan_hourly_rate` (double, optional, nullable) — Hourly rate of that plan as listed in the compute catalog.
- `target_bandwidth_tb` (BackupRestoreRequestTargetBandwidthTb, optional, nullable) — Included bandwidth of that plan in TB, as a number or a display string.
- `target_bandwidth_display` (string, optional, nullable) — Display label for the included bandwidth.
- `target_network_bandwidth` (string, optional, nullable) — Network bandwidth label of that plan.
- `target_compute_node_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Compute node to place the new VM on; omit to let the service choose.
- `target_gpu_type` (string, optional, nullable) — GPU type for a new GPU VM.
- `target_gpu_model` (string, optional, nullable) — GPU model for a new GPU VM, for example `A100`.
- `target_gpu_count` (integer, optional, nullable) — Number of GPUs for a new GPU VM (0-16).
- `target_gpu_memory_gb` (double, optional, nullable) — GPU memory for a new GPU VM in GB.
- `target_gpu_memory_display` (string, optional, nullable) — Display label for the GPU memory.
- `target_site_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Site for the new VM, from `GET /compute/sites`.
- `target_site_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of that site.
- `selected_volume_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Volume to restore in `volume_only` mode.
- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the record. Default `api`.
- `auto_start` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Start the VM once the restore completes. Default true.

## Response

### 200

Backup restore started successfully.

- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the organization that owns the VM.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the workspace the VM belongs to.
- `restore_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the restore job.
- `source_vm_id` (string, required) — VM the recovery point was taken from.
- `target_mode` (enum, required) — - `replace`: restored onto the source VM. - `new_vm`: restored into a new VM. - `volume_only`: a single volume was restored.
  - Allowed values: `replace`, `new_vm`, `volume_only`
- `recovery_point_id` (string, required) — Recovery point that was restored.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a backup run, snapshot set or restore. - `queued`: accepted and waiting to start. - `running`: in progress. - `succeeded`: finished; the recovery point is usable. - `failed`: stopped with an error (see `error_message`). - `cancelled`: stopped before it completed.
  - Allowed values: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
- `organization_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the owning organization, when the service has it.
- `workspace_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the workspace, when the service has it.
- `target_vm_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VM that received the restore: the source VM for `replace`, the new VM for `new_vm`.
- `target_vm_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the target VM.
- `recovery_point_type` (enum, optional) — - `backup`: the recovery point is a backup run. - `snapshot`: the recovery point is a snapshot set.
  - Allowed values: `backup`, `snapshot`
- `started_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the restore started (ISO 8601); null while queued.
- `completed_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the restore finished (ISO 8601); null until it does.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `failed`.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

title: Get a cloud VM backup run

# Get a cloud VM backup run

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vm-backups/runs/{run_id}

Returns one workspace-owned cloud VM backup run or recovery point. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# RUN_ID: Backup run or recovery-point ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vm-backups/runs/$RUN_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/cloud-vms/get-cloud-vm-backup-run

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `run_id` (string, required) — Backup run or recovery-point ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Backup run returned successfully.

- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the organization that owns the VM.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the workspace the VM belongs to.
- `run_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the backup run.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM that was backed up.
- `trigger` (enum, required) — What started the run. - `scheduled`: the policy schedule. - `manual`: an on-demand request from a user. - `api`: an on-demand request through the API.
  - Allowed values: `scheduled`, `manual`, `api`
- `backup_type` (enum, required) — - `full`: a complete copy of the captured volumes. - `incremental`: only the changes since the previous run in the chain.
  - Allowed values: `full`, `incremental`
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a backup run, snapshot set or restore. - `queued`: accepted and waiting to start. - `running`: in progress. - `succeeded`: finished; the recovery point is usable. - `failed`: stopped with an error (see `error_message`). - `cancelled`: stopped before it completed.
  - Allowed values: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
- `organization_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the owning organization, when the service has it.
- `workspace_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the workspace, when the service has it.
- `source_run_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of an earlier run this run derives from, when the service records one.
- `vm_backup_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the backup record in the backup store, when the service records one.
- `vm_type` (string, optional, nullable, default: cloud) — `cloud` or `gpu`. Default `cloud`.
- `vm_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the VM at run time.
- `os_type` (string, optional, nullable) — OS family of the VM (`linux` or `windows`) at run time.
- `os_distro` (string, optional, nullable) — OS distribution of the VM at run time.
- `template_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Template the VM was created from.
- `policy_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Backup policy the run belongs to, when a policy created it.
- `chain_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the backup chain (a full backup and the incremental runs that follow it) the run belongs to.
- `recovery_point_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Value to send as `recovery_point_id` when restoring from this run.
- `storage_backend` (string, optional, nullable) — Identifier of the storage backend that holds the captured data.
- `started_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the run started (ISO 8601); null while queued.
- `completed_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the run finished (ISO 8601); null until it does.
- `size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size of the captured data in GiB.
- `source_disk_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Provisioned size of the source root disk in GiB at capture time.
- `bytes_transferred` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes transferred to the backup store during the run.
- `backup_stored_size_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes the backup occupies in the backup store.
- `backup_stored_size_gb` (double, optional, nullable) — `backup_stored_size_bytes` expressed in GiB.
- `protected_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes of source data protected by this recovery point.
- `billing_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes billed for storing this recovery point.
- `billing_storage_source` (string, optional, default: unavailable) — How `billing_storage_bytes` was obtained. - `metered`: measured in the backup store. - `metered_from_manifest`: summed from the volume manifest. - `unavailable`: not measured yet.
- `metering_status` (string, optional, default: unavailable) — `metered` once storage has been measured for billing; `unavailable` until then.
- `captured_volume_count` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Number of volumes in the recovery point.
- `root_only` (boolean, optional, default: true) — True when only the root disk was captured.
- `captured_topology_hash` (string, optional, nullable) — Hash of the VM's volume layout at capture time; a different hash on the live VM means the layout drifted.
- `capture_scope` (enum, optional, nullable) — Which volumes the recovery point contains. - `root_only`: the root disk only. - `all_attached`: the root disk and every attached data volume. - `selective`: the root disk and the data volumes that were selected.
  - Allowed values: `root_only`, `all_attached`, `selective`
- `recovery_point_type` (enum, optional, default: backup) — Always `backup` for a backup run.
  - Allowed values: `backup`
- `volume_manifest` (list of RecoveryVolumeManifestItem, optional) — One entry per captured volume.
- `volume_manifest_summary` (RecoveryPointSummary, optional) — Short description of the volumes a recovery point contains.
- `live_drift_summary` (LiveDriftSummary, optional) — Difference between the volumes in a recovery point and the volumes attached to the VM now.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `failed`.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### RecoveryVolumeManifestItem

One volume captured in a recovery point (backup run or snapshot set): how it was attached at capture time, the stored artifact that holds its data, and where it was restored.

- `source_volume_id` (string, required) — ID of the volume that was captured.
- `source_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the source volume.
- `resource_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Backend storage resource name of the source volume.
- `role` (enum, optional, default: data) — - `root`: the VM's root disk. - `data`: an attached data volume.
  - Allowed values: `root`, `data`
- `size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Provisioned size of the volume in GiB.
- `display_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size in GiB as shown in the portal.
- `device_bus` (string, optional, nullable) — Virtual disk bus the volume was attached on, for example `virtio`.
- `device_slot` (string, optional, nullable) — Guest device name of the attachment, for example `vda`.
- `boot_index` (integer, optional, nullable) — Position in the boot order; 0 for the boot disk, null for volumes not in the boot order.
- `attachment_mode` (string, optional, nullable) — Attachment mode at capture time, for example `boot` for the root disk or `single-writer` for a data volume.
- `guest_device` (string, optional, nullable) — Device name as seen inside the guest OS.
- `device_path` (string, optional, nullable) — Device path inside the guest, for example `/dev/vdb`.
- `filesystem_uuid` (string, optional, nullable) — Filesystem UUID detected on the volume, when known.
- `filesystem_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Filesystem type detected on the volume, for example `ext4`, when known.
- `mount_hint` (string, optional, nullable) — Mount point the volume is expected to use, for example `/` for the root disk.
- `mount_state_at_capture` (string, optional, nullable) — Mount state recorded at capture time, for example `mounted`, `instructions_pending` or `instructions_acknowledged`.
- `mount_instructions` (string, optional, nullable) — Human-readable instructions for mounting the volume after a restore.
- `delete_on_termination` (boolean, optional, nullable) — Whether the source volume was set to be deleted together with its VM.
- `source_attachment_present` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Whether the source volume was still attached to the VM when the manifest was last refreshed.
- `artifact_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of stored artifact that holds this volume's data in the recovery point.
- `artifact_ref` (string, optional, nullable) — Reference to that artifact in the backup store.
- `artifact_chain_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Backup chain the artifact belongs to.
- `artifact_backup_type` (string, optional, nullable) — `full` or `incremental`, for the artifact.
- `artifact_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size of the stored artifact in bytes.
- `billing_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes billed for storing this volume's artifact.
- `storage_usage` (map from string to any, optional, nullable) — Storage usage details reported by the backup store, as key-value data.
- `restored_volume_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the volume created by the most recent restore of this entry, when one was performed.
- `restored_resource_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Backend storage resource name of the restored volume.
- `restored_device_path` (string, optional, nullable) — Device path of the restored volume inside the target VM.
- `restored_target_vm_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VM the restored volume was attached to.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

### RecoveryPointSummary

Short description of the volumes a recovery point contains.

- `root_only` (boolean, optional, default: true) — True when only the root disk was captured.
- `root_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the captured root disk.
- `data_volume_names` (list of string, optional) — Display names of the captured data volumes.
- `summary_text` (string, optional, default: Root) — Ready-to-display summary of the captured volumes; `Root` when only the root disk was captured.

### LiveDriftSummary

Difference between the volumes in a recovery point and the volumes attached to the VM now.

- `drifted` (boolean, optional, default: false) — True when the VM's current volumes differ from the recovery point.
- `missing_from_live` (list of string, optional) — Volumes in the recovery point that are no longer attached to the VM.
- `new_live_only` (list of string, optional) — Volumes attached to the VM now that are not in the recovery point.
- `message` (string, optional, nullable) — Human-readable description of the drift, when any.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vm-backups/runs/run_123"
```

# Get a cloud VM backup restore

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vm-backups/restores/{restore_id}

Returns the current status of a cloud VM backup restore. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# RESTORE_ID: Snapshot or backup restore operation ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/cloud-vm-backups/restores/$RESTORE_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/cloud-vms/get-cloud-vm-backup-restore

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `restore_id` (string, required) — Snapshot or backup restore operation ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Backup restore status returned successfully.

- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the organization that owns the VM.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the workspace the VM belongs to.
- `restore_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the restore job.
- `source_vm_id` (string, required) — VM the recovery point was taken from.
- `target_mode` (enum, required) — - `replace`: restored onto the source VM. - `new_vm`: restored into a new VM. - `volume_only`: a single volume was restored.
  - Allowed values: `replace`, `new_vm`, `volume_only`
- `recovery_point_id` (string, required) — Recovery point that was restored.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a backup run, snapshot set or restore. - `queued`: accepted and waiting to start. - `running`: in progress. - `succeeded`: finished; the recovery point is usable. - `failed`: stopped with an error (see `error_message`). - `cancelled`: stopped before it completed.
  - Allowed values: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
- `organization_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the owning organization, when the service has it.
- `workspace_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the workspace, when the service has it.
- `target_vm_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VM that received the restore: the source VM for `replace`, the new VM for `new_vm`.
- `target_vm_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the target VM.
- `recovery_point_type` (enum, optional) — - `backup`: the recovery point is a backup run. - `snapshot`: the recovery point is a snapshot set.
  - Allowed values: `backup`, `snapshot`
- `started_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the restore started (ISO 8601); null while queued.
- `completed_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the restore finished (ISO 8601); null until it does.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Error detail when `status` is `failed`.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

# Get operation status

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/operations/{operation_id}

Returns the status of an async compute operation (create, delete, start, stop, reboot). Works for both cloud VM and GPU VM operations. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# OPERATION_ID: Operation ID returned by a create, delete, or power-action request
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/operations/$OPERATION_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/cloud-vms/get-compute-operation

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `operation_id` (string, required) — Operation ID returned by a create, delete, or power-action request.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

Operation returned successfully.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `action` (enum, required) — What the operation does. - `create`, `delete`: create or delete the VM. - `start`, `stop`, `reboot`: power actions. - `resize`, `resize_plan`, `resize_root_disk`: change the shape or the root disk. - `attach_volume`, `detach_volume`: block volume attachment. - `update_access`: SSH key or password change. - `snapshot`, `restore`: snapshot or restore. - `rebuild`, `rescue`: rebuild the VM or boot it into rescue mode.
  - Allowed values: `create`, `start`, `stop`, `reboot`, `delete`, `resize`, `attach_volume`, `detach_volume`, `resize_plan`, `resize_root_disk`, `update_access`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `rebuild`, `rescue`
- `status` (enum, required) — - `accepted`: queued, not started. - `running`: in progress. - `waiting`: paused until an external step completes. - `compensating`: rolling back after a failure. - `succeeded`: finished successfully. - `failed`: finished with an error; see `error_code` and `error_message`. - `cancelled`: stopped before completion. - `timed_out`: did not finish within the allowed time.
  - Allowed values: `accepted`, `running`, `waiting`, `compensating`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the status last changed (ISO 8601).
- `current_step` (string, optional, nullable) — Name of the step currently running, when the workflow reports one.
- `error_code` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable error code when `status` is `failed`.
- `error_message` (string, optional, nullable) — Human-readable error detail when `status` is `failed`.

# List GPU VMs

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms

Returns one page of GPU VMs in the workspace, newest first: 10 by default, at most 100 per page. Use `limit` and `offset` to page through the rest. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/list-gpu-vms

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `limit` (integer, optional, default: 10) — Maximum number of records to return. The server returns 10 when this is omitted; use `offset` to read further pages.
- `offset` (integer, optional, default: 0) — Number of records to skip before the first one returned.

## Response

### 200

GPU VMs returned successfully.

- `list of GpuVm`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### GpuVm

A GPU VM.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique VM ID.
- `name` (string, optional) — Display name of the VM.
- `status` (enum, optional) — Lifecycle status of the VM. - `pending`: create accepted, not started yet. - `creating`, `provisioning`: compute, disk and network resources are being allocated. - `configuring`: the guest is being configured (keys, network, cloud-init). - `running`: powered on. - `starting`: a start is in progress. - `stopping`: a stop is in progress. - `stopped`: powered off. - `rebooting`: a reboot is in progress. - `resizing`, `resizing_plan`, `resizing_disk`: a CPU/memory or root-disk change is being applied. - `attaching_volume`, `detaching_volume`: a block volume is being attached or detached. - `deleting`: a delete is in progress. - `deleted`: the VM no longer exists. - `error`: the last operation failed; see the operation or events for detail.
  - Allowed values: `pending`, `creating`, `provisioning`, `configuring`, `running`, `starting`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `rebooting`, `resizing`, `attaching_volume`, `detaching_volume`, `resizing_plan`, `resizing_disk`, `deleting`, `deleted`, `error`
- `cpu` (integer, optional) — vCPUs.
- `ram_mb` (integer, optional) — Memory in MB.
- `disk_gb` (integer, optional) — Root disk size in GB.
- `os_type` (string, optional) — OS family: `linux` or `windows`.
- `os_distro` (string, optional) — OS distribution, for example `ubuntu`.
- `gpu_count` (integer, optional) — Number of attached GPUs.
- `gpu_model` (string, optional) — GPU model, for example `A100`.
- `plan_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Name of the compute plan the VM runs on.
- `public_ip` (string, optional, nullable) — Public IPv4 address; null when the VM has none.
- `private_ip` (string, optional, nullable) — Private IPv4 address; null when none is assigned.
- `tags` (list of string, optional) — Tags given at creation.
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the VM was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the VM record was last changed (ISO 8601).

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

title: Create a GPU VM

# Create a GPU VM

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a GPU VM. Returns an operation you can poll for status. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# BILLING_CATALOG: the selected plan's billing_catalog object from GET /compute/plans, passed through unchanged
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "ml-training-01", "plan_id": "019f25b7-c1b3-7a9e-bfb9-8c83e323b517", "site_id": "68b99bd78a8eda32ff3f16ea", "template_id": "tmpl_ubuntu_2204_cuda", "os_distro": "ubuntu", "os_type": "linux", "cpu": 8, "ram_mb": 32768, "gpu_count": 1, "gpu_model": "A100", "billing_catalog": '"$BILLING_CATALOG"'}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/create-gpu-vm

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a CreateGpuVmRequest.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name for the virtual machine.
- `site_id` (string, required) — Placement site ID from `GET /compute/sites`. Required: the API refuses a create without it (400 `invalid_site_id`). Use the same value when filtering plans and images.
- `os_distro` (string, required) — Operating system distribution (e.g. ubuntu, centos, debian, rocky).
- `os_type` (enum, required) — Operating system family.
  - Allowed values: `linux`
- `template_id` (string, required) — GPU-compatible template ID returned by the compute catalog.
- `cpu` (integer, required) — Number of vCPUs.
- `ram_mb` (integer, required) — RAM in megabytes.
- `gpu_count` (integer, required) — Number of GPUs to attach.
- `gpu_model` (string, required) — GPU model (e.g. A100, H100, L40S, RTX4090).
- `plan_id` (string, required) — Billable GPU plan ID returned by the compute catalog.
- `billing_catalog` (map from string to any, required) — The selected plan's `billing_catalog` object from `GET /compute/plans?vm_type=gpu`, passed through unmodified — the same flow the portal uses. Treat it as opaque. Billing charges are always computed server-side from `plan_id`, not from this echoed copy.
- `disk_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Root disk size in gigabytes.
- `ssh_key_ids` (list of string, optional) — SSH key IDs to inject into the VM.
- `ssh_keys` (list of string, optional) — Inline public SSH keys to install on the VM, in addition to the keys referenced by `ssh_key_ids`.
- `vpc_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VPC to launch the VM into. Send it together with `subnet_id`; one without the other is refused. Omit both to launch on the public provider network.
- `subnet_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Subnet of `vpc_id` for the VM's VPC NIC. Send it together with `vpc_id`.
- `network_connectivity` (enum, optional, nullable) — How the VM reaches the internet. With a VPC it defaults to `private`. Without a VPC it is accepted only as `public_ip` together with `reserved_public_ip_id`, which attaches that Reserved IP on the public provider network. `public_ip` is refused on a `nat_gateway` VPC, and on a `private` VPC it needs `reserved_public_ip_id`.
  - Allowed values: `private`, `nat`, `public_ip`
- `vpc_attachment_mode` (enum, optional, default: primary) — GPU VMs support only `primary`: with a VPC, the VPC NIC is the VM's only NIC. `secondary` is refused with 400.
  - Allowed values: `primary`
- `reserved_public_ip_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Reserved IP to attach at launch. Needs `network_connectivity: public_ip`. Accepted with a VPC or, without one, on the public provider network.
- `tags` (list of string, optional) — Arbitrary tags for filtering and organization.

## Response

### 202

VM creation accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

### 402 Payment Required Error

Billing refused the request (`billing_denied`). `billing_reason` carries Billing's reason unchanged, for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` (a plan limit) or `resource_usage_unavailable` (Billing could not count usage). `billing_sku_code`, `billing_evaluated_at` and `admission_context_id` identify the decision. Nothing is provisioned; resolve the reason and retry with the same idempotency key where supported.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.

### 403 Forbidden Error

Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. - `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 409 Conflict Error

The request conflicts with the current resource state.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 423 Locked Error

The organization is suspended (`organization_suspended`), so writes are refused.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

```swift
import Foundation

let headers = [
  "X-Idempotency-Key": "4f2a9c1e-7b3d-4e8a-9f10-2c5d6e7f8a9b",
  "Authorization": "Bearer <token>",
  "Content-Type": "application/json"
]
let parameters = [
  "name": "ml-training-01",
  "site_id": "68b99bd78a8eda32ff3f16ea",
  "os_distro": "ubuntu",
  "os_type": "linux",
  "template_id": "tmpl_ubuntu_2204_cuda",
  "cpu": 8,
  "ram_mb": 32768,
  "gpu_count": 1,
  "gpu_model": "A100",
  "plan_id": "019f25b7-c1b3-7a9e-bfb9-8c83e323b517"
] as [String : Any]

let postData = JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: parameters, options: [])

let request = NSMutableURLRequest(url: NSURL(string: "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms?workspace_id=710995")! as URL,
                                        cachePolicy: .useProtocolCachePolicy,
                                    timeoutInterval: 10.0)
request.httpMethod = "POST"
request.allHTTPHeaderFields = headers
request.httpBody = postData as Data

let session = URLSession.shared
let dataTask = session.dataTask(with: request as URLRequest, completionHandler: { (data, response, error) -> Void in
  if (error != nil) {
    print(error as Any)
  } else {
    let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse
    print(httpResponse)
  }
})

dataTask.resume()
```

title: Get a GPU VM

# Get a GPU VM

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}

Returns a single GPU VM. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/get-gpu-vm

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

GPU VM returned successfully.

- `id` (string, optional) — Unique VM ID.
- `name` (string, optional) — Display name of the VM.
- `status` (enum, optional) — Lifecycle status of the VM. - `pending`: create accepted, not started yet. - `creating`, `provisioning`: compute, disk and network resources are being allocated. - `configuring`: the guest is being configured (keys, network, cloud-init). - `running`: powered on. - `starting`: a start is in progress. - `stopping`: a stop is in progress. - `stopped`: powered off. - `rebooting`: a reboot is in progress. - `resizing`, `resizing_plan`, `resizing_disk`: a CPU/memory or root-disk change is being applied. - `attaching_volume`, `detaching_volume`: a block volume is being attached or detached. - `deleting`: a delete is in progress. - `deleted`: the VM no longer exists. - `error`: the last operation failed; see the operation or events for detail.
  - Allowed values: `pending`, `creating`, `provisioning`, `configuring`, `running`, `starting`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `rebooting`, `resizing`, `attaching_volume`, `detaching_volume`, `resizing_plan`, `resizing_disk`, `deleting`, `deleted`, `error`
- `cpu` (integer, optional) — vCPUs.
- `ram_mb` (integer, optional) — Memory in MB.
- `disk_gb` (integer, optional) — Root disk size in GB.
- `os_type` (string, optional) — OS family: `linux` or `windows`.
- `os_distro` (string, optional) — OS distribution, for example `ubuntu`.
- `gpu_count` (integer, optional) — Number of attached GPUs.
- `gpu_model` (string, optional) — GPU model, for example `A100`.
- `plan_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Name of the compute plan the VM runs on.
- `public_ip` (string, optional, nullable) — Public IPv4 address; null when the VM has none.
- `private_ip` (string, optional, nullable) — Private IPv4 address; null when none is assigned.
- `tags` (list of string, optional) — Tags given at creation.
- `created_at` (datetime, optional) — When the VM was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the VM record was last changed (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 404 Not Found Error

The requested resource was not found.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

# Delete a GPU VM

DELETE https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}
Content-Type: application/json

Deletes a GPU VM. Returns an operation you can poll for status. A VM with an automatically assigned public IP needs `public_ip_action` in the body. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X DELETE "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"public_ip_action": "reserve", "reserved_ip_label": "<reserved_ip_label>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/delete-gpu-vm

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a VmDeleteRequest.

- `public_ip_action` (enum, optional, nullable) — What to do with the VM's automatically assigned public IP. `reserve` converts it to a Reserved IP in this workspace; `release` releases it with the VM. Required when the VM has an automatically assigned public IP. `reserve` on a VM without one is refused with 400.
  - Allowed values: `reserve`, `release`
- `reserved_ip_label` (string, optional, nullable) — Label for the Reserved IP that `reserve` creates. Blank is treated as not set.
- `reserved_ip_billing_catalog` (VmDeleteRequestReservedIpBillingCatalog, optional, nullable) — Billing catalog identifiers used to bill the Reserved IP that `reserve` creates. Required with `public_ip_action: reserve`, with a non-empty `sku_id`; refused with 400 otherwise.

## Response

### 202

VM deletion accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.

- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. # Start a GPU VM

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/start
Content-Type: application/json

Starts a stopped GPU VM. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/start?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"force": false}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/start-gpu-vm

```swift
})
```

title: Stop a GPU VM
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/stop-gpu-vm
