# Stop a GPU VM

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/stop
Content-Type: application/json

Stops a running GPU VM. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/stop?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"force": false}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/stop-gpu-vm

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a PowerActionRequest.

- `force` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Force the action even if the VM is in a transitional state.

## Response

### 202

VM stop accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.

# Reboot a GPU VM

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/reboot
Content-Type: application/json

Reboots a GPU VM. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/reboot?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"force": false}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/reboot-gpu-vm

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a PowerActionRequest.

- `force` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Force the action even if the VM is in a transitional state.

## Response

### 202

VM reboot accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. - `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.

# Get GPU VM metrics

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/metrics

Returns current resource-usage metrics for a GPU VM. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/metrics?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/get-gpu-vm-metrics

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

## Response

### 200

VM metrics returned successfully.

- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM.
- `vm_type` (enum, required) — - `cloud` - `gpu`
  - Allowed values: `cloud`, `gpu`
- `power_state` (string, required) — Power state observed on the host when the sample was taken: `running`, `stopped`, `paused`, `suspended`, `blocked`, `crashed` or `unknown`.
- `monitoring_status` (enum, required) — - `active`: a recent sample exists. - `stale`: the last sample is older than the freshness threshold. - `unavailable`: no sample has been collected.
  - Allowed values: `active`, `stale`, `unavailable`
- `month_rx_bytes` (integer, required, default: 0) — Bytes received so far in the current calendar month.
- `month_tx_bytes` (integer, required, default: 0) — Bytes transmitted so far in the current calendar month.
- `last_collected_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the sample was collected (ISO 8601).
- `cpu_percent` (double, optional, nullable) — CPU utilisation, 0-100.
- `memory_used_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Memory in use, in bytes.
- `memory_used_percent` (double, optional, nullable) — Memory in use as a percentage of the VM's memory, 0-100.
- `storage_used_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Disk space in use, in bytes.
- `storage_total_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Disk capacity visible to the guest, in bytes.
- `storage_used_percent` (double, optional, nullable) — Disk space in use as a percentage of `storage_total_bytes`, 0-100.
- `storage_provisioned_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Disk capacity provisioned for the VM, in bytes.
- `disk_read_bps` (double, optional, nullable) — Disk read throughput in bytes per second.
- `disk_write_bps` (double, optional, nullable) — Disk write throughput in bytes per second.
- `disk_read_iops` (double, optional, nullable) — Disk read operations per second.
- `disk_write_iops` (double, optional, nullable) — Disk write operations per second.
- `net_rx_bps` (double, optional, nullable) — Network receive rate in bytes per second.
- `net_tx_bps` (double, optional, nullable) — Network transmit rate in bytes per second.

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

# Update GPU VM access settings

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/access
Content-Type: application/json

Adds or removes SSH keys, resets the Linux user password, or changes SSH password authentication on a GPU VM without rebooting it or interrupting running GPU workloads. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/access?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"requested_by": "api", "admin_username": "<admin_username>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/update-gpu-vm-access

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a VmAccessUpdateRequest.

- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the operation. Default `api`.
- `admin_username` (string, optional, nullable) — Linux account to update. Defaults to the VM admin user.
- `ssh_key_mode` (enum, optional, nullable) — - `add`: install the given keys. - `remove`: remove the given keys.
  - Allowed values: `add`, `remove`
- `ssh_keys` (list of string, optional, default: []) — Inline public SSH keys to add or remove.
- `ssh_key_ids` (list of string, optional, default: []) — Secret Store SSH key IDs to add or remove.
- `ssh_key_secret_refs` (list of SshKeySecretRef, optional, default: []) — SSH public keys kept in Secret Store, referenced by store key and secret name.
- `new_password` (string, optional, nullable) — New password for `admin_username`.
- `password_auth_enabled` (boolean, optional, nullable) — Enable (`true`) or disable (`false`) SSH password authentication.
- `confirm_remove_last_ssh_key` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Must be `true` to remove the VM's last remaining SSH key.

## Response

### 202

Access update accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

# Precheck a GPU VM resize

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/resize/precheck
Content-Type: application/json

Checks whether a GPU VM can take a requested CPU, memory, or root-disk change before you start the resize. The attached GPU stays the same. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/resize/precheck?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cpu": 1, "ram_mb": 1}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/precheck-gpu-vm-resize

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a VmResizeRequest.

- `cpu` (integer, optional) — Target vCPUs.
- `ram_mb` (integer, optional) — Target memory in MB.
- `disk_gb` (integer, optional) — Target root disk size in GB.
- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the operation. Default `api`.

## Response

### 200

Resize decision returned successfully.

- `decision` (enum, required) — - `in_place`: the change can be applied on the current host. - `migration_required`: the VM must move to another host first. - `blocked`: the change cannot be made; see `reasons`.
  - Allowed values: `in_place`, `migration_required`, `blocked`
- `reasons` (list of string, required) — Why the decision was reached.
- `warnings` (list of string, required) — Non-blocking warnings about the change.
- `migration_checklist` (list of string, required) — Items to confirm before a migration.
- `migration_steps` (list of string, required) — Steps a migration would perform.
- `requires_stop` (boolean, required) — Whether the VM must be stopped for the change.
- `downtime_expected` (boolean, required) — Whether the change interrupts the VM.
- `no_changes` (boolean, required) — True when the target shape equals the current one.
- `current_state` (string, required) — VM lifecycle status recorded by the engine.
- `current` (VmResizeShape, required) — A VM shape: vCPUs, memory and root disk.
- `target` (VmResizeShape, required) — A VM shape: vCPUs, memory and root disk.
- `mode` (enum, optional, nullable) — Same values as `decision`; present when the engine reports the mode separately.
  - Allowed values: `in_place`, `migration_required`, `blocked`
- `live_state` (string, optional, nullable) — Power state observed on the host, when available.

# Resize a GPU VM

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/resize
Content-Type: application/json

Changes a GPU VM's CPU and memory, and optionally grows its root disk, after the same precheck the portal runs. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/resize?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cpu": 1, "ram_mb": 1}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/resize-gpu-vm

- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

title: Resize a GPU VM plan

# Resize a GPU VM plan

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/resize-plan
Content-Type: application/json

Moves a GPU VM to a different CPU and memory plan. Downgrades require explicit confirmation. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/resize-plan?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cpu": 1, "ram_mb": 1}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/resize-gpu-vm-plan

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a VmResizePlanRequest.

- `cpu` (integer, required) — Target vCPUs (1-256).
- `ram_mb` (integer, required) — Target memory in MB.
- `allow_online` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Permit the change while the VM is running. Default false.
- `confirm_downgrade` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Must be `true` when the target shape is smaller than the current one.
- `billing_catalog` (BillingCatalogSelection, optional) — Optional. The target plan's `billing_catalog` from `GET /compute/plans`. The VM engine records it with the resize.
- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the operation. Default `api`.

## Response

### 202

Plan resize accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

import Foundation

let headers = [
  "X-Idempotency-Key": "4f2a9c1e-7b3d-4e8a-9f10-2c5d6e7f8a9b",

# Resize a GPU VM root disk

PATCH https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/resize-root-disk
Content-Type: application/json

Increases a GPU VM's root disk size, for example to fit larger models or datasets. Shrinking a root disk is not supported. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X PATCH "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/resize-root-disk?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"new_size_gb": 1}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/resize-gpu-vm-root-disk

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a VmResizeRootDiskRequest.

- `new_size_gb` (integer, required) — Target root disk size in GB.
- `allow_online` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Permit the change while the VM is running. Default false.
- `billing_catalog` (BillingCatalogSelection, optional) — Optional. A Billing catalog selection that the VM engine records with the resize.
- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the operation. Default `api`.

## Response

### 202

Root-disk resize accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

## Types

### BillingCatalogSelection

A Billing catalog SKU selection as the VM engine accepts it. `sku_id` and `sku_code` are required; other catalog fields are accepted and stored as sent.

- `sku_id` (BillingCatalogSelectionSkuId, required) — Billing catalog SKU ID.
- `sku_code` (string, required) — Billing catalog SKU code. Stored in upper case.
- `product_id` (BillingCatalogSelectionProductId, optional, nullable) — Billing catalog product ID.
- `product_code` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing catalog product code.
- `display_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the SKU, as listed in the billing catalog.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### BillingCatalogSelectionSkuId

Billing catalog SKU ID.

- string
- double

### BillingCatalogSelectionProductId

Billing catalog product ID.

- string
- double

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"net/http"
	"io"
)

func main() {

	url := "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/vm_123/actions/resize-root-disk?workspace_id=710995"

	payload := strings.NewReader("{\n  \"new_size_gb\": 1\n}")

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("PATCH", url, payload)

	req.Header.Add("X-Idempotency-Key", "4f2a9c1e-7b3d-4e8a-9f10-2c5d6e7f8a9b")
	req.Header.Add("Authorization", "Bearer <token>")
	req.Header.Add("Content-Type", "application/json")

	res, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(res.Body)

	fmt.Println(res)
	fmt.Println(string(body))

}

# Attach a volume to a GPU VM

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/attach-volume
Content-Type: application/json

Attaches a persistent block storage volume to a GPU VM, for datasets, checkpoints, or model weights. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/attach-volume?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"volume_id": "<volume_id>", "billing_catalog": {"sku_id": "<sku_id>", "sku_code": "<sku_code>"}}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/attach-gpu-vm-volume

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a VmAttachVolumeRequest.

- `volume_id` (string, required) — ID of the block storage volume to attach.
- `billing_catalog` (BillingCatalogSelection, required) — Required. The Block Storage SKU from the Billing catalog that the VM engine records for this attachment. Copy it from the volume's `metadata.billing_catalog` (`GET /block-storage/volumes/{volume_id}`).
- `mode` (enum, optional, default: single-writer) — - `single-writer`: only this VM may write to the volume (default). - `multi-writer`: the volume may be attached to several VMs.
  - Allowed values: `single-writer`, `multi-writer`
- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the operation. Default `api`.

## Response

### 202

Volume attachment accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.

## Types

### BillingCatalogSelection

A Billing catalog SKU selection as the VM engine accepts it. `sku_id` and `sku_code` are required; other catalog fields are accepted and stored as sent.

- `sku_id` (BillingCatalogSelectionSkuId, required) — Billing catalog SKU ID.
- `sku_code` (string, required) — Billing catalog SKU code. Stored in upper case.
- `product_id` (BillingCatalogSelectionProductId, optional, nullable) — Billing catalog product ID.
- `product_code` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing catalog product code.
- `display_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the SKU, as listed in the billing catalog.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### BillingCatalogSelectionSkuId

Billing catalog SKU ID.

- string
- double

### BillingCatalogSelectionProductId

Billing catalog product ID.

- string
- double

---
title: Detach a volume from a GPU VM
url: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/detach-gpu-vm-volume

# Detach a volume from a GPU VM

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/actions/detach-volume
Content-Type: application/json

Detaches a persistent block storage volume from a GPU VM. Stop jobs using it and unmount its filesystem in the guest first unless force is used. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/actions/detach-volume?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"volume_id": "<volume_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/detach-gpu-vm-volume

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Headers

- `X-Idempotency-Key` (string, required) — Unique key used to safely retry write operations.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a VmDetachVolumeRequest.

- `volume_id` (string, required) — ID of the block storage volume to detach.
- `force` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Detach even if the volume still appears to be in use. Default false.
- `confirm_unmounted` (boolean, optional, default: false) — Confirms the volume was unmounted inside the guest. Default false.
- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the operation. Default `api`.

## Response

### 202

Volume detachment accepted.

- `operation_id` (string, required) — ID of the queued operation.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the operation acts on.
- `status` (string, required) — Always `accepted`.
- `submitted_at` (datetime, required) — When the operation was accepted (ISO 8601).

Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 503 Service Unavailable Error

A service the request depends on did not answer. Gateway codes: `workspace_verification_unavailable`, `principal_verification_unavailable` and `principal_authorization_unavailable`; on billable creates also `billing_admission_timeout`, `billing_admission_unavailable`, `billing_admission_disabled`, `billing_admission_not_configured` and the catalog codes `compute_catalog_unavailable`, `compute_catalog_not_configured`, `product_catalog_timeout`, `product_catalog_unavailable`, `product_catalog_not_configured` and `unsupported_product_quote`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.

# Acknowledge GPU VM mount guidance

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/mount-guidance/acknowledge
Content-Type: application/json

Records that you have reviewed the guest mount instructions for a data volume attached to a GPU VM. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/mount-guidance/acknowledge?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"volume_id": "<volume_id>"}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/acknowledge-gpu-vm-mount-guidance

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a MountGuidanceAcknowledgeRequest.

- `volume_id` (string, required) — ID of the attached block storage volume.

## Response

### 200

Mount guidance acknowledged successfully.

- `status` (string, required, default: ok) — Always `ok`.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM.
- `volume_id` (string, required) — ID of the volume.
- `mount_state` (string, optional, nullable) — Mount state recorded after the acknowledgement, for example `instructions_acknowledged`.
- `instructions_acknowledged_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the acknowledgement was recorded (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

# List GPU VM events

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/events

Returns a GPU VM's lifecycle and operation event timeline. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/events?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/list-gpu-vm-events

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `limit` (integer, optional, default: 100) — Maximum number of items to return (1-500). Default 100.

## Response

### 200

VM events returned successfully.

- `list of VmEvent`

## Errors

### 401 Unauthorized Error

The API token is missing, malformed or unknown (`invalid_api_key`).

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

### 403 Forbidden Error

The token may not make this call. Gateway codes: `insufficient_scope` (with `required_scope`), `key_revoked`, `key_disabled`, `key_inactive`, `key_expired`, `unknown_route`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `principal_inactive`, `principal_not_member` and `principal_permission_denied`. On writes, also `organization_restricted` (an admin restricted the organization) and `verification_required` (the token's user has not completed identity verification). A product service may also refuse with `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

## Types

### VmEvent

One entry in a VM's event timeline.

- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the organization that owns the VM.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the workspace the VM belongs to.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM.
- `event_type` (string, required) — Dotted event name, for example `operation.accepted`, `vm.reboot.succeeded` or `snapshot.restore.failed`.
- `message` (string, required) — Human-readable description of the event.
- `payload` (map from string to any, required) — Event-specific key-value details.
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the event was recorded (ISO 8601).
- `organization_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the owning organization, when the service has it.
- `workspace_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the workspace, when the service has it.
- `operation_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Operation that produced the event, when it belongs to one.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

# Get GPU VM metric timeseries

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/metrics/timeseries

Returns rolled-up metric series for a GPU VM over a supported time range. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/metrics/timeseries?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/get-gpu-vm-metrics-timeseries

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `range` (enum, optional, default: 1h) — Time window to return, ending now. - `30m` - `1h` - `6h` - `24h` - `7d` Default `1h`.
  - Allowed values: `30m`, `1h`, `6h`, `24h`, `7d`

## Response

### 200

VM metric timeseries returned successfully.

- `range` (enum, required) — Window covered. - `30m` - `1h` - `6h` - `24h` - `7d`
  - Allowed values: `30m`, `1h`, `6h`, `24h`, `7d`
- `resolution` (enum, required) — Spacing between points. - `1m` - `5m` - `15m` - `2h`
  - Allowed values: `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `2h`
- `from` (datetime, required) — Start of the window (ISO 8601).
- `to` (datetime, required) — End of the window (ISO 8601).
- `series` (map from string to list of list of any, required) — Map of series name to `[timestamp, value]` pairs; `value` is null where no sample exists. Series: `cpu_percent`, `memory_used_percent`, `storage_used_percent`, `disk_read_bps`, `disk_write_bps`, `disk_read_iops`, `disk_write_iops`, `net_rx_bps`, `net_tx_bps`.

# Get GPU VM monthly bandwidth

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/metrics/bandwidth

Returns a GPU VM's received and transmitted byte totals for a calendar month. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/metrics/bandwidth?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID&month=2026-08" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/get-gpu-vm-bandwidth

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `month` (string, required) — Calendar month to report, as `YYYY-MM` (for example `2026-08`).

## Response

### 200

VM bandwidth summary returned successfully.

- `month` (string, required) — Month in `YYYY-MM` form.
- `rx_bytes` (integer, required, default: 0) — Bytes received in the month.
- `tx_bytes` (integer, required, default: 0) — Bytes transmitted in the month.
- `last_updated_at` (datetime, optional, nullable) — When the counters were last updated (ISO 8601).

## Errors

### 400 Bad Request Error

The request is invalid. From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

# List GPU VM snapshots

GET https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/snapshots

Lists recovery snapshots for one GPU VM. Requires scope: vm.read.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/snapshots?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN"
```


Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/list-gpu-vm-snapshots

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.
- `limit` (integer, optional, default: 50) — Maximum number of records to return.
- `offset` (integer, optional, default: 0) — Number of items to skip before the first returned item. Default 0.
- `search` (string, optional) — Return only snapshot sets whose name contains this text.

## Response

### 200

Snapshots returned successfully.

- `snapshots` (list of SnapshotSet, required) — Snapshot sets on this page.
- `total` (integer, required, default: 0) — Total number of snapshot sets matching the request.

## Errors

The response descriptions list the codes for each status.

- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.

## Types

### SnapshotSet

A snapshot set: a point-in-time capture of a VM's root disk and, depending on `capture_scope`, its data volumes. It is a recovery point that the snapshot restore action accepts.

- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the organization that owns the VM.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the workspace the VM belongs to.
- `snapshot_set_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the snapshot set.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the snapshot was taken from.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the snapshot set.
- `recovery_point_id` (string, required) — Recovery point ID of this snapshot set.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a backup run, snapshot set or restore. - `queued`: accepted and waiting to start. - `running`: in progress. - `succeeded`: finished; the recovery point is usable. - `failed`: stopped with an error (see `error_message`). - `cancelled`: stopped before it completed.
  - Allowed values: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the snapshot set was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the snapshot set was last updated (ISO 8601).
- `organization_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the owning organization, when the service has it.
- `workspace_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the workspace, when the service has it.
- `vm_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the VM at capture time.
- `vm_type` (enum, optional) — Kind of virtual machine. - `cloud`: general-purpose cloud VM. - `gpu`: VM with attached GPUs.
  - Allowed values: `cloud`, `gpu`
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description given at creation.
- `recovery_point_type` (enum, optional, default: snapshot) — Always `snapshot` for a snapshot set.
  - Allowed values: `snapshot`
- `capture_scope` (enum, optional, default: all_attached) — Which volumes the recovery point contains. - `root_only`: the root disk only. - `all_attached`: the root disk and every attached data volume. - `selective`: the root disk and the data volumes that were selected.
  - Allowed values: `root_only`, `all_attached`, `selective`
- `captured_volume_count` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Number of volumes in the snapshot set.
- `root_only` (boolean, optional, default: true) — True when only the root disk was captured.
- `size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size of the captured data in GiB.
- `source_disk_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Provisioned size of the source root disk in GiB at capture time.
- `display_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size in GiB as shown in the portal.
- `display_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — `display_size_gb` expressed in bytes.
- `backend_protected_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes of protected data as reported by the storage backend.
- `protected_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes of source data protected by this snapshot set.
- `billing_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes billed for storing this snapshot set.
- `billing_storage_source` (string, optional, default: unavailable) — How `billing_storage_bytes` was obtained. - `metered`: measured in the backup store. - `metered_from_manifest`: summed from the volume manifest. - `unavailable`: not measured yet.
- `metering_status` (string, optional, default: unavailable) — `metered` once storage has been measured for billing; `unavailable` until then.
- `storage_backend` (string, optional, nullable) — Identifier of the storage backend that holds the captured data.
- `captured_topology_hash` (string, optional, nullable) — Hash of the VM's volume layout at capture time; a different hash on the live VM means the layout drifted.
- `root_volume_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the captured root disk.
- `root_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the captured root disk.
- `volume_manifest` (list of RecoveryVolumeManifestItem, optional) — One entry per captured volume.
- `volume_manifest_summary` (RecoveryPointSummary, optional) — Short description of the volumes a recovery point contains.
- `live_drift_summary` (LiveDriftSummary, optional) — Difference between the volumes in a recovery point and the volumes attached to the VM now.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

### ErrorDetail

Error detail from the product service.

- string
- map from string to any
- list of any

### RecoveryVolumeManifestItem

One volume captured in a recovery point (backup run or snapshot set): how it was attached at capture time, the stored artifact that holds its data, and where it was restored.

- `source_volume_id` (string, required) — ID of the volume that was captured.
- `source_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the source volume.
- `resource_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Backend storage resource name of the source volume.
- `role` (enum, optional, default: data) — - `root`: the VM's root disk. - `data`: an attached data volume.
  - Allowed values: `root`, `data`
- `size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Provisioned size of the volume in GiB.
- `display_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size in GiB as shown in the portal.
- `device_bus` (string, optional, nullable) — Virtual disk bus the volume was attached on, for example `virtio`.
- `device_slot` (string, optional, nullable) — Guest device name of the attachment, for example `vda`.
- `boot_index` (integer, optional, nullable) — Position in the boot order; 0 for the boot disk, null for volumes not in the boot order.
- `attachment_mode` (string, optional, nullable) — Attachment mode at capture time, for example `boot` for the root disk or `single-writer` for a data volume.
- `guest_device` (string, optional, nullable) — Device name as seen inside the guest OS.
- `device_path` (string, optional, nullable) — Device path inside the guest, for example `/dev/vdb`.
- `filesystem_uuid` (string, optional, nullable) — Filesystem UUID detected on the volume, when known.
- `filesystem_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Filesystem type detected on the volume, for example `ext4`, when known.
- `mount_hint` (string, optional, nullable) — Mount point the volume is expected to use, for example `/` for the root disk.
- `mount_state_at_capture` (string, optional, nullable) — Mount state recorded at capture time, for example `mounted`, `instructions_pending` or `instructions_acknowledged`.
- `mount_instructions` (string, optional, nullable) — Human-readable instructions for mounting the volume after a restore.
- `delete_on_termination` (boolean, optional, nullable) — Whether the source volume was set to be deleted together with its VM.
- `source_attachment_present` (boolean, optional, default: true) — Whether the source volume was still attached to the VM when the manifest was last refreshed.
- `artifact_type` (string, optional, nullable) — Kind of stored artifact that holds this volume's data in the recovery point.
- `artifact_ref` (string, optional, nullable) — Reference to that artifact in the backup store.
- `artifact_chain_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Backup chain the artifact belongs to.
- `artifact_backup_type` (string, optional, nullable) — `full` or `incremental`, for the artifact.
- `artifact_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size of the stored artifact in bytes.
- `billing_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes billed for storing this volume's artifact.
- `storage_usage` (map from string to any, optional, nullable) — Storage usage details reported by the backup store, as key-value data.
- `restored_volume_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the volume created by the most recent restore of this entry, when one was performed.
- `restored_resource_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Backend storage resource name of the restored volume.
- `restored_device_path` (string, optional, nullable) — Device path of the restored volume inside the target VM.
- `restored_target_vm_id` (string, optional, nullable) — VM the restored volume was attached to.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

### RecoveryPointSummary

Short description of the volumes a recovery point contains.

- `root_only` (boolean, optional, default: true) — True when only the root disk was captured.
- `root_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the captured root disk.
- `data_volume_names` (list of string, optional) — Display names of the captured data volumes.
- `summary_text` (string, optional, default: Root) — Ready-to-display summary of the captured volumes; `Root` when only the root disk was captured.

### LiveDriftSummary

Difference between the volumes in a recovery point and the volumes attached to the VM now.

- `drifted` (boolean, optional, default: false) — True when the VM's current volumes differ from the recovery point.
- `missing_from_live` (list of string, optional) — Volumes in the recovery point that are no longer attached to the VM.
- `new_live_only` (list of string, optional) — Volumes attached to the VM now that are not in the recovery point.
- `message` (string, optional, nullable) — Human-readable description of the drift, when any.

title: Create a GPU VM snapshot

# Create a GPU VM snapshot

POST https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/{vm_id}/snapshots
Content-Type: application/json

Creates a recovery snapshot of a GPU VM's root disk, all attached disks, or selected data disks. Requires scope: vm.write.

```
# Example request with curl (set IBEE_API_TOKEN to a platform API token and WORKSPACE_ID to the workspace first).
# VM_ID: Virtual machine ID
curl -X POST "https://api.ibee.ai/v1/compute/gpu-vms/$VM_ID/snapshots?workspace_id=$WORKSPACE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $IBEE_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "<name>", "billing_catalog": {"sku_id": "<sku_id>", "sku_code": "<sku_code>"}}'
```

Reference: https://ibee.ai/docs/api-reference/gpu-vms/create-gpu-vm-snapshot

## Authentication

- `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — IBEE platform API token. Production tokens start with `ibee_prod_key_`; development tokens start with `ibee_dev_key_`. Use a token only with its matching gateway environment.

## Servers

- `https://api.ibee.ai/v1` (Production, default)
- `https://api.ibee.co.in/v1` (Development)

## Request

### Path parameters

- `vm_id` (string, required) — Virtual machine ID.

### Query parameters

- `workspace_id` (string, required) — The positive numeric workspace ID to scope this request to. Zero, negative, and non-numeric values are rejected.

### Body (application/json)

This endpoint expects a SnapshotCreateRequest.

- `name` (string, required) — Display name for the snapshot set.
- `billing_catalog` (BillingCatalogSelection, required) — Required. The snapshot storage SKU from the Billing catalog that the VM engine records for this snapshot. No public operation lists it yet.
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Optional description (up to 1024 characters).
- `mode` (enum, optional, default: all_attached) — Which volumes to capture. - `root_only`: the root disk only. - `all_attached`: the root disk and every attached data volume (default). - `selective`: the root disk and the volumes in `selected_data_volume_ids`.
  - Allowed values: `root_only`, `all_attached`, `selective`
- `selected_data_volume_ids` (list of string, optional, default: []) — Data volume IDs to include when `mode` is `selective`.
- `requested_by` (string, optional, default: api) — Free-text label for who or what made the request, stored with the record. Default `api`.

## Response

### 200

Snapshot created or queued successfully.

- `organization_id` (string, required) — ID of the organization that owns the VM.
- `workspace_id` (string, required) — ID of the workspace the VM belongs to.
- `snapshot_set_id` (string, required) — Unique ID of the snapshot set.
- `vm_id` (string, required) — ID of the VM the snapshot was taken from.
- `name` (string, required) — Display name of the snapshot set.
- `recovery_point_id` (string, required) — Recovery point ID of this snapshot set.
- `status` (enum, required) — Lifecycle status of a backup run, snapshot set or restore. - `queued`: accepted and waiting to start. - `running`: in progress. - `succeeded`: finished; the recovery point is usable. - `failed`: stopped with an error (see `error_message`). - `cancelled`: stopped before it completed.
  - Allowed values: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`
- `created_at` (datetime, required) — When the snapshot set was created (ISO 8601).
- `updated_at` (datetime, required) — When the snapshot set was last updated (ISO 8601).
- `organization_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the owning organization, when the service has it.
- `workspace_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the workspace, when the service has it.
- `vm_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the VM at capture time.
- `vm_type` (enum, optional) — Kind of virtual machine. - `cloud`: general-purpose cloud VM. - `gpu`: VM with attached GPUs.
  - Allowed values: `cloud`, `gpu`
- `description` (string, optional, nullable) — Description given at creation.
- `recovery_point_type` (enum, optional, default: snapshot) — Always `snapshot` for a snapshot set.
  - Allowed values: `snapshot`
- `capture_scope` (enum, optional, default: all_attached) — Which volumes the recovery point contains. - `root_only`: the root disk only. - `all_attached`: the root disk and every attached data volume. - `selective`: the root disk and the data volumes that were selected.
  - Allowed values: `root_only`, `all_attached`, `selective`
- `captured_volume_count` (integer, optional, default: 1) — Number of volumes in the snapshot set.
- `root_only` (boolean, optional, default: true) — True when only the root disk was captured.
- `size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size of the captured data in GiB.
- `source_disk_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Provisioned size of the source root disk in GiB at capture time.
- `display_size_gb` (integer, optional, nullable) — Size in GiB as shown in the portal.
- `display_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — `display_size_gb` expressed in bytes.
- `backend_protected_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes of protected data as reported by the storage backend.
- `protected_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes of source data protected by this snapshot set.
- `billing_storage_bytes` (integer, optional, nullable) — Bytes billed for storing this snapshot set.
- `billing_storage_source` (string, optional, default: unavailable) — How `billing_storage_bytes` was obtained. - `metered`: measured in the backup store. - `metered_from_manifest`: summed from the volume manifest. - `unavailable`: not measured yet.
- `metering_status` (string, optional, default: unavailable) — `metered` once storage has been measured for billing; `unavailable` until then.
- `storage_backend` (string, optional, nullable) — Identifier of the storage backend that holds the captured data.
- `captured_topology_hash` (string, optional, nullable) — Hash of the VM's volume layout at capture time; a different hash on the live VM means the layout drifted.
- `root_volume_id` (string, optional, nullable) — ID of the captured root disk.
- `root_volume_name` (string, optional, nullable) — Display name of the captured root disk.
- `volume_manifest` (list of RecoveryVolumeManifestItem, optional) — One entry per captured volume.
- `volume_manifest_summary` (RecoveryPointSummary, optional) — Short description of the volumes a recovery point contains.
- `live_drift_summary` (LiveDriftSummary, optional) — Difference between the volumes in a recovery point and the volumes attached to the VM now.
- `metadata` (map from string to any, optional) — Additional service-specific key-value data.

## Errors

From the gateway: `workspace_id_required` or `invalid_workspace_id`; on billable creates also `invalid_json_body` and selection codes such as `plan_id_required`, `invalid_site_id`, `compute_billing_term_required` or `invalid_block_storage_selection`. Otherwise the product service's `detail`.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`. The response descriptions list the codes for each status.
- `required_scope` (string, optional, nullable) — The scope the token lacks, with `insufficient_scope`.
- `billing_reason` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing's reason with `billing_denied`, passed through unchanged: for example `insufficient_balance`, `credit_limit_exceeded`, `initial_topup_required`, `resource_limit_reached` or `resource_usage_unavailable`.
- `billing_sku_code` (string, optional, nullable) — The SKU the billing admission checked, when there was one.
- `billing_evaluated_at` (string, optional, nullable) — When Billing made the decision, as Billing returned it.
- `admission_context_id` (string, optional, nullable) — Billing admission context for this request, derived from the token, workspace, route and `X-Idempotency-Key`, so a retry with the same key gets the same id.
- `detail` (ErrorDetail, optional) — Error detail from the product service.

Nothing is provisioned; resolve the reason and retry with the same idempotency key where supported.

- `error` (string, optional, nullable) — Machine-readable code from the gateway's authorization step, for example `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_scope`, `organization_restricted`, `organization_suspended`, `verification_required` or `billing_denied`.
